modules.title: Foundation of Agriculture, Discipline and Farm Orientation
modules.content:
Module 1 of 7. Foundation of Agriculture, Discipline and Farm Orientation

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 1. Introduction to Agriculture and Food Security

Teaching focus
Meaning of agriculture, importance of food production, agriculture as service to God and society, dignity of farm work.

Scripture
Genesis 2:15 “And the LORD God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.”

Practice
Day 1: Walk around the farm area and identify available land, water sources and access points.
Day 2: List common crops grown in the community and discuss their uses.
Day 3: Identify farm problems in the community, such as poor soil, pests, lack of water or poor storage.
Day 4: Clean a small farm area as a group.
Day 5: Write a simple reflection on why food production is important.

Character
Agriculture begins with stewardship. God expects people to care for the land, not waste it.

Week 2. Farm Discipline, Tools and Safety

Teaching focus
Farm rules, tool handling, farm safety, punctuality, cleanliness and teamwork.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 14:40 “Let all things be done decently and in order.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify basic farm tools and state their uses.
Day 2: Demonstrate safe carrying and storage of cutlasses, hoes, rakes and shovels.
Day 3: Practise cleaning tools after use.
Day 4: Mark a tool storage area and arrange tools properly.
Day 5: Complete a farm safety checklist.

Character
Orderliness prevents accidents and helps work move smoothly.

Week 3. Land Clearing and Farm Site Preparation

Teaching focus
Choosing a farm site, land clearing, removing stones, clearing weeds and preparing for bed making.

Scripture
Proverbs 14:23 “In all labour there is profit: but the talk of the lips tendeth only to penury.”

Practice
Day 1: Inspect the farm site and identify obstacles.
Day 2: Clear weeds under supervision.
Day 3: Remove stones, sticks and waste materials from the farm area.
Day 4: Divide the land into small training plots.
Day 5: Review the cleared land and record work done.

Character
Real progress comes through labour, not talk alone.

Week 4. Soil, Compost and Environmental Stewardship

Teaching focus
Types of soil, soil fertility, composting, organic matter and care for the environment.

Scripture
Psalm 24:1 “The earth is the LORD’s, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein.”

Practice
Day 1: Collect soil samples from different areas and compare colour and texture.
Day 2: Identify materials that can be used for compost.
Day 3: Prepare a simple compost heap.
Day 4: Water and cover the compost heap properly.
Day 5: Record compost materials used and discuss the value of soil care.

Character
The earth belongs to God. Trainees must care for soil, water, crops and the environment responsibly.

modules.title: Crop Production Foundation
modules.content:
Module 2 of 7. Crop Production Foundation

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 5. Nursery Bed Preparation

Teaching focus
Meaning of nursery, crops raised in nurseries, nursery site selection, soil preparation and protection.

Scripture
Zechariah 4:10 “For who hath despised the day of small things?”

Practice
Day 1: Select a suitable nursery site.
Day 2: Clear and prepare a small nursery bed.
Day 3: Mix soil with compost or organic matter.
Day 4: Level the nursery bed and create drainage channels.
Day 5: Shade the nursery area using available materials.

Character
Small beginnings matter. A seedling may look small, but with care it can become fruitful.

Week 6. Seed Selection and Sowing

Teaching focus
Good seeds, poor seeds, seed spacing, sowing depth, watering and early crop care.

Scripture
Galatians 6:7 “Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.”

Practice
Day 1: Sort good seeds from damaged seeds.
Day 2: Prepare seed rows on the nursery bed.
Day 3: Sow seeds at the correct depth.
Day 4: Water the nursery carefully.
Day 5: Record seed type and quantity planted according to the farm record system.

Character
What a person sows matters. Good seed, good habits and good character produce good results.

Week 7. Germination, Seedling Care and Nursery Management

Teaching focus
Germination, watering, shade management, thinning, pest observation and seedling health.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 3:7 “So then neither is he that planteth any thing, neither he that watereth; but God that giveth the increase.”

Practice
Day 1: Observe germination and count emerging seedlings.
Day 2: Water seedlings correctly without flooding.
Day 3: Remove weeds from the nursery bed.
Day 4: Identify weak or diseased seedlings.
Day 5: Record nursery progress in the farm logbook.

Character
Trainees plant and water, but God gives increase. This teaches humility and dependence on God.

Week 8. Farm Bed Making and Field Layout

Teaching focus
Raised beds, flat beds, ridges, spacing, drainage and field organisation.

Scripture
Proverbs 24:3 “Through wisdom is an house builded; and by understanding it is established.”

Practice
Day 1: Measure and mark farm beds.
Day 2: Prepare raised beds or ridges under supervision.
Day 3: Create pathways between beds.
Day 4: Add compost or organic matter to the beds.
Day 5: Draw a simple field layout in the farm record book.

Character
Good planning produces order. A disorganised farm creates waste, confusion and poor results.

modules.title: Planting, Crop Care and Maintenance
modules.content:
Module 3 of 7. Planting, Crop Care and Maintenance

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 9. Transplanting Seedlings

Teaching focus
When to transplant, handling seedlings, transplanting depth, watering and reducing transplant shock.

Scripture
Isaiah 61:3 “That they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he might be glorified.”

Practice
Day 1: Select healthy seedlings for transplanting.
Day 2: Water nursery before transplanting.
Day 3: Transplant seedlings into prepared beds.
Day 4: Water transplanted seedlings.
Day 5: Observe survival rate and record losses.

Character
Lives, like seedlings, need proper handling and the right environment to grow.

Week 10. Direct Planting and Crop Spacing

Teaching focus
Direct seeding, spacing, plant population and thinning.

Scripture
Ecclesiastes 3:2 “A time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted.”

Practice
Day 1: Mark planting points using correct spacing.
Day 2: Sow seeds directly in the field.
Day 3: Cover seeds properly.
Day 4: Water planted beds where needed.
Day 5: Record seed quantity, bed number and spacing used.

Character
There is a right time and a right method for every productive work.

Week 11. Watering, Mulching and Moisture Management

Teaching focus
Importance of water, watering schedule, mulching materials, moisture conservation and avoiding water waste.

Scripture
Isaiah 58:11 “And the LORD shall guide thee continually, and satisfy thy soul in drought, and make fat thy bones: and thou shalt be like a watered garden.”

Practice
Day 1: Water crops at the correct time.
Day 2: Collect dry grass, leaves or approved mulching materials.
Day 3: Apply mulch around crops properly.
Day 4: Compare mulched and unmulched soil moisture.
Day 5: Record watering schedule and observations.

Character
A watered garden is fruitful. In the same way, a disciplined life that receives God’s Word and correction becomes fruitful.

Week 12. Weeding and Crop Maintenance

Teaching focus
Weed identification, effect of weeds, safe weeding and regular crop maintenance.

Scripture
Song of Solomon 2:15 “Take us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vines: for our vines have tender grapes.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify weeds in the farm area.
Day 2: Weed between crop rows carefully.
Day 3: Weed around plants without damaging roots.
Day 4: Clean pathways and drainage channels.
Day 5: Record weeding activity and crop condition.

Character
Small problems can destroy growth if ignored. Trainees must remove bad habits early, just as weeds must be removed from the farm.

modules.title: Crop Health, Farm Records and Basic Livestock Awareness
modules.content:
Module 4 of 7. Crop Health, Farm Records and Basic Livestock Awareness

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 13. Pest and Disease Observation

Teaching focus
Common signs of pests and diseases, early reporting, safe control methods and observation discipline.

Scripture
Proverbs 27:23 “Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, and look well to thy herds.”

Practice
Day 1: Inspect leaves, stems and soil for pests.
Day 2: Identify signs of disease, such as yellowing, spots or wilting.
Day 3: Remove badly affected plant parts under supervision.
Day 4: Prepare a pest and disease observation record.
Day 5: Discuss safe and unsafe pest control practices.

Character
A responsible person observes what is entrusted to him or her. Neglect leads to loss.

Week 14. Safe Use of Farm Inputs

Teaching focus
Organic inputs, fertilisers, simple pest control, safe handling, storage and correct application.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:3 “A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify different farm inputs available.
Day 2: Demonstrate safe storage of inputs.
Day 3: Apply compost or approved input under supervision.
Day 4: Wash hands and tools after input handling.
Day 5: Record input type, quantity and location applied.

Character
Wisdom recognises danger early and takes safety seriously.

Week 15. Farm Records and Simple Data Collection

Teaching focus
Importance of records, planting records, labour records, input records, harvest records and expense records.

Scripture
Habakkuk 2:2 “And the LORD answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.”

Practice
Day 1: Create a simple farm record book.
Day 2: Record crop type, plot number and planting details.
Day 3: Record labour activities done on the farm.
Day 4: Record tools and inputs used.
Day 5: Review records for accuracy and neatness.

Character
Clear records prevent confusion. Truthful writing is part of accountability.

Week 16. Poultry, Livestock and Fish Farming Awareness

Teaching focus
Introduction to poultry, livestock and fish farming, animal care, hygiene, feeding and observation.

Scripture
Proverbs 12:10 “A righteous man regardeth the life of his beast: but the tender mercies of the wicked are cruel.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify common livestock and poultry in the community.
Day 2: Prepare a simple animal care checklist.
Day 3: Observe feeding and watering needs using a demonstration model.
Day 4: Discuss signs of sickness in animals.
Day 5: Write a simple livestock or fish farming record template.

Character
Caring for animals teaches compassion, observation and responsibility.

modules.title: Harvesting, Post-Harvest Handling and Agribusiness
modules.content:
Module 5 of 7. Harvesting, Post-Harvest Handling and Agribusiness

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 17. Harvesting Principles

Teaching focus
When to harvest, careful harvesting, avoiding damage and preserving quality.

Scripture
Psalm 126:5 “They that sow in tears shall reap in joy.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify signs that crops are ready for harvest.
Day 2: Harvest selected crops carefully under supervision.
Day 3: Sort harvested produce.
Day 4: Grade produce by size, quality or condition.
Day 5: Record harvest quantity and quality.

Character
Harvest rewards faithful labour. Trainees must learn that disciplined effort produces joy.

Week 18. Post-Harvest Handling and Storage

Teaching focus
Cleaning, sorting, drying, packaging, storage, reducing losses and preserving value.

Scripture
John 6:12 “When they were filled, he said unto his disciples, Gather up the fragments that remain, that nothing be lost.”

Practice
Day 1: Clean harvested produce.
Day 2: Sort damaged produce from good produce.
Day 3: Demonstrate simple drying or shade handling where suitable.
Day 4: Package produce for sale or storage.
Day 5: Record post-harvest losses and discuss prevention.

Character
Waste is not good stewardship. Trainees must learn to preserve value and reduce losses.

Week 19. Farm Budgeting and Costing

Teaching focus
Farm expenses, input costs, labour costs, transport costs, sales and profit.

Scripture
Luke 14:28 “For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it?”

Practice
Day 1: List all costs involved in a small vegetable plot.
Day 2: Estimate cost of seeds, compost, labour and water.
Day 3: Prepare a simple farm budget.
Day 4: Compare estimated cost with possible selling price.
Day 5: Calculate simple profit or loss using a sample example.

Character
Wise people count the cost before starting. Poor planning leads to waste and failure.

Week 20. Marketing Farm Produce

Teaching focus
Market observation, customers, pricing, packaging, negotiation, honesty and customer care.

Scripture
Proverbs 11:1 “A false balance is abomination to the LORD: but a just weight is his delight.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify possible buyers for farm produce.
Day 2: Compare prices from local markets or sample price lists.
Day 3: Practise packaging produce neatly.
Day 4: Role-play selling produce to a customer.
Day 5: Prepare a simple marketing plan for one farm product.

Character
Farm produce must be sold with honesty. False measurement and cheating destroy trust.

modules.title: Agribusiness Planning, Cooperatives and Value Addition
modules.content:
Module 6 of 7. Agribusiness Planning, Cooperatives and Value Addition

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 21. Agribusiness Opportunities

Teaching focus
Agriculture as business, small enterprise ideas, service opportunities and community food needs.

Scripture
Deuteronomy 8:18 “But thou shalt remember the LORD thy God: for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth.”

Practice
Day 1: List agribusiness opportunities in the community.
Day 2: Match each opportunity with required skills.
Day 3: Identify customers for one agribusiness idea.
Day 4: Discuss how to start small.
Day 5: Write one simple agribusiness idea note.

Character
The ability to create wealth must be used with gratitude, humility and obedience to God.

Week 22. Value Addition and Processing Awareness

Teaching focus
Meaning of value addition, cleaning, drying, packaging, processing and increasing product value.

Scripture
Proverbs 24:4 “And by knowledge shall the chambers be filled with all precious and pleasant riches.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify raw farm products that can be improved.
Day 2: Demonstrate cleaning and packaging of produce.
Day 3: Discuss simple processing ideas such as drying, grinding or packaging.
Day 4: Compare raw produce and packaged produce.
Day 5: Write a value addition plan for one product.

Character
Knowledge increases value. Trainees must learn how skill and wisdom can improve simple products.

Week 23. Cooperative Farming and Group Enterprise

Teaching focus
Meaning of cooperatives, group savings, shared tools, group farming, trust and accountability.

Scripture
Ecclesiastes 4:9 “Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss the meaning of a farming cooperative.
Day 2: Create a sample cooperative group structure.
Day 3: Write simple cooperative rules.
Day 4: Prepare a group farming budget.
Day 5: Present a cooperative farming idea.

Character
Teamwork can increase productivity, but it requires trust, honesty and accountability.

Week 24. Farm Enterprise Planning

Teaching focus
Simple farm business plan, goals, customers, costs, tools, labour, risks and expected profit.

Scripture
Proverbs 16:3 “Commit thy works unto the LORD, and thy thoughts shall be established.”

Practice
Day 1: Choose one farm enterprise idea.
Day 2: Write the problem the enterprise will solve.
Day 3: List required tools, inputs and labour.
Day 4: Prepare estimated cost and selling plan.
Day 5: Present the first draft of a farm enterprise plan.

Character
Planning should be committed to God. Trainees must plan carefully and depend on God for wisdom.

modules.title: Advanced Practice, Attachment Preparation and Final Departmental Evaluation
modules.content:
Module 7 of 7. Advanced Practice, Attachment Preparation and Final Departmental Evaluation

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 25. Departmental Mini-Project Planning

Teaching focus
Planning a supervised farm project, team roles, tools, budget, safety and expected output.

Scripture
Nehemiah 2:18 “Then I told them of the hand of my God which was good upon me; as also the king’s words that he had spoken unto me. And they said, Let us rise up and build.”

Practice
Day 1: Choose a departmental mini-project.
Day 2: Write project goals and expected results.
Day 3: Assign team roles.
Day 4: Prepare tools and input list.
Day 5: Submit project plan for trainer approval.

Character
Godly vision must lead to organised action. Trainees must rise and build responsibly.

Week 26. Departmental Mini-Project Implementation

Teaching focus
Carrying out a small farm project with supervision, discipline, records and teamwork.

Scripture
Nehemiah 4:6 “So built we the wall; and all the wall was joined together unto the half thereof: for the people had a mind to work.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare the project site.
Day 2: Begin project implementation.
Day 3: Continue implementation and record progress.
Day 4: Monitor safety, quality and teamwork.
Day 5: Complete project activity for the week and review.

Character
A willing mind produces progress. Teamwork grows when people are ready to work.

Week 27. Final Practical Demonstration and Portfolio

Teaching focus
Demonstrating skills learnt, organising evidence, presenting farm records and preparing for assessment.

Scripture
2 Timothy 2:15 “Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed.”

Practice
Day 1: Demonstrate tool identification and safe use.
Day 2: Demonstrate nursery, planting or farm bed preparation.
Day 3: Demonstrate record keeping and simple budgeting.
Day 4: Organise departmental portfolio.
Day 5: Present practical evidence to trainer.

Character
A faithful worker should not be ashamed. Skill, study and diligence prepare a trainee for approval.

Week 28. Industrial Attachment Preparation

Teaching focus
Preparing for farm placement, agribusiness attachment, supervisor conduct, daily logs and workplace expectations.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:29 “Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify possible attachment placements.
Day 2: Prepare attachment learning goals.
Day 3: Practise writing daily farm attachment logs.
Day 4: Review safety and workplace behaviour.
Day 5: Complete final departmental readiness assessment.

Character
Diligence opens doors. A trainee who works faithfully can be trusted with greater opportunities.

modules.title: Introduction to AI, Wisdom and Responsible Technology
modules.content:
Module 1 of 7. Introduction to AI, Wisdom and Responsible Technology

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 1. What Is Artificial Intelligence?

Teaching focus
Meaning of AI, simple examples of AI, where AI is used, AI as a tool and the difference between human beings and machines.

Scripture
Proverbs 4:7 “Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss what trainees have heard about AI.
Day 2: Identify examples of AI in phones, search tools, translation tools and chat tools.
Day 3: Discuss what AI can do and what it cannot do.
Day 4: Compare AI assistance with human wisdom and responsibility.
Day 5: Write a reflection on why AI must be used with wisdom.

Character
Technology without wisdom can mislead people. Wisdom must guide the use of AI.

Week 2. AI Is a Tool, Not God

Teaching focus
AI as a human-made tool, limits of AI, human responsibility, spiritual discernment, prayer, Scripture and conscience.

Scripture
James 1:5 “If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss why AI should not replace God’s wisdom.
Day 2: List situations where human judgement is still needed.
Day 3: Discuss why AI should not replace prayer, Scripture or spiritual counsel.
Day 4: Prepare a “Wise Use of AI” poster.
Day 5: Write a personal pledge on using AI under the fear of God.

Character
AI may give information, but wisdom comes from God. Trainees must not worship technology.

Week 3. Benefits and Opportunities of AI

Teaching focus
AI for learning, business, communication, productivity, creativity, records, translation awareness, planning and problem-solving.

Scripture
Daniel 1:17 “As for these four children, God gave them knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom.”

Practice
Day 1: List ways AI can help students learn.
Day 2: List ways AI can help small businesses.
Day 3: List ways AI can help offices and organisations.
Day 4: List ways AI can support ministry and community service.
Day 5: Prepare a chart showing useful AI opportunities.

Character
Skill must be used for service, not pride. AI should help trainees serve better.

Week 4. Risks, Limits and Dangers of AI

Teaching focus
Wrong answers, fake information, bias, privacy risks, overdependence, plagiarism, laziness, fake images, scams and deception.

Scripture
1 Thessalonians 5:21 “Prove all things; hold fast that which is good.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss examples of wrong or misleading AI answers.
Day 2: Identify risks of copying AI work without checking.
Day 3: Discuss why private information should not be shared carelessly.
Day 4: Prepare an AI risk checklist.
Day 5: Write a reflection on why AI output must be tested.

Character
A wise trainee does not believe everything immediately. All things must be tested.

modules.title: Prompt Writing, Asking Better Questions and Checking Answers
modules.content:
Module 2 of 7. Prompt Writing, Asking Better Questions and Checking Answers

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 5. Introduction to Prompt Writing

Teaching focus
Meaning of prompt, asking clear questions, giving context, stating the task and requesting the right format.

Scripture
Proverbs 18:15 “The heart of the prudent getteth knowledge; and the ear of the wise seeketh knowledge.”

Practice
Day 1: Write simple questions for an AI tool.
Day 2: Improve unclear prompts into clear prompts.
Day 3: Add context to a prompt.
Day 4: Ask for a response in bullet points, table or paragraph form.
Day 5: Compare weak prompts and strong prompts.

Character
Wise people ask well. Better questions often produce better answers.

Week 6. Giving Context and Clear Instructions

Teaching focus
Audience, purpose, tone, length, examples, constraints and expected result.

Scripture
Habakkuk 2:2 “And the LORD answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.”

Practice
Day 1: Write a prompt for a school announcement.
Day 2: Write a prompt for a business customer message.
Day 3: Write a prompt for a training outline.
Day 4: Add audience and purpose to each prompt.
Day 5: Review prompts for clarity.

Character
Clear instructions help work move faster and reduce confusion.

Week 7. Reviewing and Improving AI Output

Teaching focus
Checking grammar, checking facts, improving tone, correcting mistakes, asking follow-up questions and editing output.

Scripture
2 Corinthians 13:5 “Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves.”

Practice
Day 1: Review a sample AI-generated paragraph.
Day 2: Identify spelling and grammar issues.
Day 3: Identify unclear statements.
Day 4: Improve the paragraph manually.
Day 5: Prepare a checklist for reviewing AI output.

Character
Review is not weakness. Careful checking improves quality.

Week 8. Fact-Checking and Avoiding Misinformation

Teaching focus
AI hallucination awareness, checking dates, names, places, quotations, figures, laws, health advice and important claims.

Scripture
Proverbs 14:15 “The simple believeth every word: but the prudent man looketh well to his going.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify claims that need checking.
Day 2: Compare an AI answer with a reliable source provided by the trainer.
Day 3: Mark uncertain claims.
Day 4: Practise asking AI to explain uncertainty.
Day 5: Prepare a fact-checking guide.

Character
A prudent person does not believe every word. Important information must be checked.

modules.title: AI for Learning, Writing, Research and Communication
modules.content:
Module 3 of 7. AI for Learning, Writing, Research and Communication

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 9. AI as a Learning Assistant

Teaching focus
Using AI to explain topics, create study plans, generate practice questions, summarise lessons and support revision.

Scripture
Proverbs 1:5 “A wise man will hear, and will increase learning; and a man of understanding shall attain unto wise counsels.”

Practice
Day 1: Ask AI to explain a simple topic.
Day 2: Ask AI to create a study plan.
Day 3: Ask AI to prepare revision questions.
Day 4: Answer the revision questions.
Day 5: Reflect on how AI can support learning without replacing study.

Character
AI can support learning, but trainees must still study, think and practise.

Week 10. AI for Writing and Editing

Teaching focus
Drafting letters, improving grammar, simplifying text, changing tone, summarising and proofreading.

Scripture
Proverbs 25:11 “A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in pictures of silver.”

Practice
Day 1: Draft a simple letter with AI assistance.
Day 2: Improve grammar in a paragraph.
Day 3: Rewrite a message in a polite tone.
Day 4: Summarise a short passage.
Day 5: Manually review and improve the final text.

Character
Words matter. AI-assisted writing must still be truthful, respectful and suitable.

Week 11. AI for Research Support

Teaching focus
Generating research questions, outlining topics, summarising information, organising notes and avoiding plagiarism.

Scripture
Proverbs 18:15 “The heart of the prudent getteth knowledge; and the ear of the wise seeketh knowledge.”

Practice
Day 1: Use AI to generate research questions on a safe topic.
Day 2: Create an outline from the research question.
Day 3: Summarise notes in the trainee’s own words.
Day 4: Identify where sources are needed.
Day 5: Prepare a simple research summary with proper acknowledgement.

Character
Research must be honest. AI should support thinking, not replace integrity.

Week 12. AI for Professional Communication

Teaching focus
Emails, announcements, customer messages, apology messages, meeting notes, reminders and respectful digital language.

Scripture
Colossians 4:6 “Let your speech be alway with grace, seasoned with salt, that ye may know how ye ought to answer every man.”

Practice
Day 1: Draft a professional email.
Day 2: Draft a customer response.
Day 3: Draft a meeting reminder.
Day 4: Improve rude wording into respectful wording.
Day 5: Prepare a professional communication portfolio.

Character
Digital communication must be gracious, respectful and clear.

modules.title: AI for Work, Business, Ministry and Community Development
modules.content:
Module 4 of 7. AI for Work, Business, Ministry and Community Development

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 13. AI for Office Productivity

Teaching focus
Task lists, meeting agendas, minutes, reports, summaries, schedules, office messages and document organisation.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 14:40 “Let all things be done decently and in order.”

Practice
Day 1: Use AI to create a meeting agenda.
Day 2: Use AI to summarise sample meeting notes.
Day 3: Use AI to prepare a task list.
Day 4: Use AI to draft a simple office report.
Day 5: Review all outputs for accuracy and order.

Character
AI can support order, but the worker remains responsible for the final result.

Week 14. AI for Small Business and Entrepreneurship

Teaching focus
Business ideas, customer messages, product descriptions, simple business plans, marketing ideas and service improvement.

Scripture
Deuteronomy 8:18 “But thou shalt remember the LORD thy God: for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth.”

Practice
Day 1: Use AI to generate business ideas for a local community.
Day 2: Use AI to write a product description.
Day 3: Use AI to create a customer message.
Day 4: Use AI to outline a simple business plan.
Day 5: Review the plan for honesty, realism and local relevance.

Character
Wealth creation must honour God. AI enterprise must be honest and useful.

Week 15. AI for Ministry and Community Service

Teaching focus
Announcements, teaching outlines, outreach planning, volunteer schedules, community needs assessment and service communication.

Scripture
Matthew 5:16 “Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.”

Practice
Day 1: Use AI to draft a church or ministry announcement.
Day 2: Use AI to prepare a community outreach checklist.
Day 3: Use AI to create a volunteer schedule.
Day 4: Use AI to outline a community service project.
Day 5: Discuss why AI must not replace prayer, Scripture and pastoral guidance.

Character
Technology should help good works shine, but God must receive the glory.

Week 16. AI for Agriculture, Construction and Practical Trades

Teaching focus
Using AI for farm planning, maintenance checklists, safety reminders, construction reports, training notes and customer communication.

Scripture
Proverbs 24:3 “Through wisdom is an house builded; and by understanding it is established.”

Practice
Day 1: Use AI to create a farm task checklist.
Day 2: Use AI to draft a construction safety reminder.
Day 3: Use AI to prepare a simple maintenance report.
Day 4: Use AI to create customer communication for a technical service.
Day 5: Review AI outputs for practicality and safety.

Character
Practical work still requires human skill, supervision and safety. AI should support, not replace, competence.

modules.title: AI Ethics, Privacy, Safety and Digital Integrity
modules.content:
Module 5 of 7. AI Ethics, Privacy, Safety and Digital Integrity

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 17. AI, Privacy and Confidential Information

Teaching focus
Personal data, passwords, financial information, student records, customer data, ministry information and what not to share with AI.

Scripture
Proverbs 11:13 “A talebearer revealeth secrets: but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter.”

Practice
Day 1: Define personal and confidential information.
Day 2: Identify examples of information that should not be entered into AI tools.
Day 3: Practise rewriting a prompt without private details.
Day 4: Prepare a data privacy checklist.
Day 5: Write a confidentiality pledge.

Character
A faithful person protects confidential matters. Digital tools must not become channels for careless disclosure.

Week 18. Plagiarism, Copyright and Academic Honesty

Teaching focus
Original work, copying, giving credit, using AI responsibly, school assignments, ministry materials and business content.

Scripture
Proverbs 10:9 “He that walketh uprightly walketh surely: but he that perverteth his ways shall be known.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss plagiarism and why it is wrong.
Day 2: Compare original writing and copied writing.
Day 3: Use AI to generate ideas, then write in personal words.
Day 4: Practise acknowledging help or sources where appropriate.
Day 5: Prepare an academic honesty guide.

Character
A trainee must walk uprightly. AI must not be used to cheat.

Week 19. Deepfakes, Fake Images and Digital Deception

Teaching focus
Fake pictures, fake voices, impersonation, false news, manipulated media, reputational harm and responsible sharing.

Scripture
Exodus 20:16 “Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss what false witness means in the digital world.
Day 2: Identify signs that an image, video or message may be misleading.
Day 3: Discuss why impersonation is wrong.
Day 4: Prepare a responsible sharing checklist.
Day 5: Write a digital truth pledge.

Character
Spreading falsehood online is still false witness. Trainees must not use AI to deceive.

Week 20. AI, Fraud, Scams and Cybercrime Awareness

Teaching focus
AI-assisted scams, fake messages, fake documents, phishing, impersonation, cybercrime and reporting suspicious activity.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:3 “A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify examples of scam messages.
Day 2: Discuss how AI can be misused for fraud.
Day 3: Practise spotting suspicious requests.
Day 4: Prepare a cyber safety response plan.
Day 5: Discuss why trainees must never use AI for crime.

Character
A wise trainee avoids digital danger and refuses dishonest gain.

modules.title: AI Productivity, Local Problem-Solving and Enterprise
modules.content:
Module 6 of 7. AI Productivity, Local Problem-Solving and Enterprise

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 21. AI for Personal Productivity and Time Management

Teaching focus
Planning the day, reminders, study schedules, task prioritisation, goal tracking and avoiding digital laziness.

Scripture
Proverbs 21:5 “The thoughts of the diligent tend only to plenteousness; but of every one that is hasty only to want.”

Practice
Day 1: Use AI to create a daily schedule.
Day 2: Use AI to organise tasks by priority.
Day 3: Use AI to create a weekly learning plan.
Day 4: Review the plan for realism.
Day 5: Write a discipline plan for reducing wasted screen time.

Character
AI should support diligence, not laziness.

Week 22. AI for Local Problem-Solving

Teaching focus
Identifying community problems, generating solutions, analysing options, planning community projects and checking feasibility.

Scripture
Nehemiah 2:18 “Then I told them of the hand of my God which was good upon me; as also the king’s words that he had spoken unto me. And they said, Let us rise up and build.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify one local community problem.
Day 2: Use AI to brainstorm possible solutions.
Day 3: Select realistic solutions and reject unrealistic ones.
Day 4: Prepare a simple project plan.
Day 5: Present the plan to the class.

Character
Ideas must become responsible action. Trainees must rise and build.

Week 23. AI-Assisted Digital Services

Teaching focus
Typing, editing, document formatting, CV drafting, customer messages, flyers, business plans and service quality.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:29 “Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.”

Practice
Day 1: Create a sample AI-assisted document service.
Day 2: Draft and edit a CV or application letter under supervision.
Day 3: Create a simple flyer with AI-assisted wording.
Day 4: Prepare a customer message for a small business.
Day 5: Build a mini-portfolio of AI-assisted digital services.

Character
Diligence and quality make a worker valuable. AI should not reduce excellence.

Week 24. AI Enterprise Opportunities and Responsible Business

Teaching focus
AI-assisted services, pricing, customer trust, confidentiality, quality control, ethical limits and starting small.

Scripture
Deuteronomy 8:18 “But thou shalt remember the LORD thy God: for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth.”

Practice
Day 1: List enterprise opportunities using AI responsibly.
Day 2: Choose one AI-assisted service.
Day 3: Prepare a service description.
Day 4: Prepare a small-start budget.
Day 5: Write an AI-assisted enterprise idea note.

Character
The power to create wealth comes from God. AI enterprise must be honest, safe and useful.

modules.title: Advanced Practice, Departmental Project and Attachment Preparation
modules.content:
Module 7 of 7. Advanced Practice, Departmental Project and Attachment Preparation

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 25. Departmental Mini-Project Planning

Teaching focus
Planning an AI awareness project, team roles, tools, ethics, output, privacy, verification and presentation.

Scripture
Habakkuk 2:2 “And the LORD answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.”

Practice
Day 1: Choose a safe AI awareness mini-project.
Day 2: Prepare project goals and expected results.
Day 3: Prepare prompts, documents and verification checklist.
Day 4: Assign team roles and ethical rules.
Day 5: Submit project plan for trainer approval.

Character
Clear planning helps AI work remain useful, safe and accountable.

Week 26. Departmental Mini-Project Implementation

Teaching focus
Carrying out a supervised AI project with accuracy, privacy, teamwork, verification and final presentation.

Scripture
Nehemiah 4:6 “So built we the wall; and all the wall was joined together unto the half thereof: for the people had a mind to work.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare devices, prompts and working files.
Day 2: Generate drafts or outputs under supervision.
Day 3: Review, correct and verify outputs.
Day 4: Prepare final document, presentation or awareness material.
Day 5: Submit project progress report.

Character
Progress comes when people have a mind to work and the discipline to check their work.

Week 27. Final Practical Demonstration and Portfolio

Teaching focus
Demonstrating prompt writing, AI-assisted writing, fact-checking, privacy awareness, ethical use and portfolio evidence.

Scripture
2 Timothy 2:15 “Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed.”

Practice
Day 1: Demonstrate prompt writing.
Day 2: Demonstrate reviewing and improving AI output.
Day 3: Demonstrate fact-checking and privacy protection.
Day 4: Organise AI awareness portfolio.
Day 5: Present practical evidence to the trainer.

Character
A trained worker should not be ashamed. Diligence, ethics and competence prepare trainees for approval.

Week 28. Industrial Attachment Preparation

Teaching focus
Preparing for digital or administrative placement, supervisor conduct, data confidentiality, responsible AI use, daily logs and final readiness.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:29 “Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify possible AI awareness attachment placements.
Day 2: Prepare personal attachment learning goals.
Day 3: Practise writing daily AI and digital skills attachment logs.
Day 4: Review confidentiality, office conduct and responsible AI behaviour.
Day 5: Complete final departmental readiness assessment.

Character
Diligence opens doors. A faithful AI-aware trainee can serve responsibly in modern workplaces.

modules.title: Building Orientation, Safety and Site Discipline
modules.content:
Module 1 of 7. Building Orientation, Safety and Site Discipline

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 1. Introduction to Building Construction

Teaching focus
Meaning of building construction, importance of buildings, types of buildings, community development and dignity of building work.

Scripture
Psalm 127:1 “Except the LORD build the house, they labour in vain that build it.”

Practice
Day 1: Walk around the Academy environment and identify different types of buildings.
Day 2: List common buildings in the community and their uses.
Day 3: Discuss how poor buildings affect safety, health and comfort.
Day 4: Identify stages involved in building a simple house.
Day 5: Write a reflection on why building work must be done with care.

Character
Building work must begin with humility before God. Human labour needs divine wisdom and guidance.

Week 2. Building Site Safety and Discipline

Teaching focus
Site hazards, protective equipment, safe movement, tool safety, obedience to instructions and respect for site rules.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:3 “A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify common building site hazards.
Day 2: Demonstrate correct use of boots, helmets, gloves and reflective jackets where available.
Day 3: Practise safe movement around a building site.
Day 4: Prepare a basic building site safety checklist.
Day 5: Conduct a supervised safety inspection of a practice area.

Character
Safety is wisdom. A disciplined trainee protects life and prevents avoidable accidents.

Week 3. Building Tools and Their Uses

Teaching focus
Common building tools, safe handling, cleaning, storage, tool accountability and care.

Scripture
Luke 16:10 “He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify basic building tools and state their uses.
Day 2: Practise safe carrying of trowel, hammer, shovel, tape and spirit level.
Day 3: Clean tools after use.
Day 4: Arrange tools in a tool storage area.
Day 5: Complete a tool issue and return record.

Character
Faithfulness begins with small things. Tool care shows whether a trainee can be trusted.

Week 4. Building Materials and Material Stewardship

Teaching focus
Blocks, cement, sand, gravel, water, timber, nails, reinforcement bars, roofing sheets, storage and waste control.

Scripture
John 6:12 “When they were filled, he said unto his disciples, Gather up the fragments that remain, that nothing be lost.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify common building materials.
Day 2: Discuss the uses of cement, blocks, sand, gravel, timber and water.
Day 3: Demonstrate proper storage of cement and timber.
Day 4: Identify ways materials are wasted on building sites.
Day 5: Prepare a material stewardship checklist.

Character
Waste is poor stewardship. Building materials must be protected and used wisely.

Teaching focus
Length, width, height, measuring tape, simple units, accuracy and recording measurements.

Scripture
Proverbs 11:1 “A false balance is abomination to the LORD: but a just weight is his delight.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify measuring tools used on building sites.
Day 2: Practise measuring simple lengths with measuring tape.
Day 3: Measure the length, width and height of simple objects.
Day 4: Record measurements neatly in a site notebook.
Day 5: Compare group measurements and discuss errors.

Character
Accuracy is part of integrity. Careless measurement can damage an entire building project.

Week 6. Introduction to Simple Building Drawings

Teaching focus
Meaning of building drawings, simple plans, elevations, symbols, dimensions and why drawings matter.

Scripture
Habakkuk 2:2 “And the LORD answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.”

Practice
Day 1: Observe a simple building plan.
Day 2: Identify walls, doors, windows and rooms on a simple drawing.
Day 3: Locate dimensions on a drawing.
Day 4: Draw a simple room layout.
Day 5: Explain why workers must follow approved drawings.

Character
Clear plans prevent confusion. A trainee must learn to follow instructions and not build by guesswork.

Week 7. Setting-Out Awareness for Buildings

Teaching focus
Building lines, pegs, strings, right angles, site layout, simple rectangular setting-out and accuracy.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 14:40 “Let all things be done decently and in order.”

Practice
Day 1: Demonstrate how to use pegs and string.
Day 2: Mark a straight line on the ground.
Day 3: Mark a simple rectangular building layout under supervision.
Day 4: Check diagonals and right-angle awareness.
Day 5: Record layout dimensions in a site notebook.

Character
Order matters. If setting-out is wrong, the building can be wrongly positioned from the beginning.

Week 8. Site Clearing and Foundation Preparation

Teaching focus
Clearing site, removing obstacles, soil awareness, access paths, foundation marking and trench safety.

Scripture
Proverbs 24:27 “Prepare thy work without, and make it fit for thyself in the field; and afterwards build thine house.”

Practice
Day 1: Inspect a practice site and identify obstacles.
Day 2: Clear light vegetation and waste under supervision.
Day 3: Remove stones, sticks and unsafe objects.
Day 4: Mark sample foundation lines.
Day 5: Discuss trench safety and record site preparation work.

Character
Preparation comes before building. A wise worker prepares properly before construction begins.

Week 9. Foundation Awareness

Teaching focus
Purpose of foundations, soil, trenches, concrete blinding, foundation walls, backfilling and foundation safety.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 3:10 “According to the grace of God which is given unto me, as a wise masterbuilder, I have laid the foundation.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss why foundations are important.
Day 2: Observe soil differences in the training area.
Day 3: Mark a sample trench line.
Day 4: Discuss safe excavation and trench collapse risks.
Day 5: Draw a simple foundation awareness diagram.

Character
A strong building begins with a strong foundation. A strong life also begins with truth, discipline and faith.

Week 10. Blocks, Mortar and Basic Walling Materials

Teaching focus
Types of blocks, quality of blocks, mortar materials, cement-sand-water mix awareness and safe handling.

Scripture
Luke 14:28 “For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost?”

Practice
Day 1: Identify different blocks where available.
Day 2: Discuss strong and weak blocks.
Day 3: Identify cement, sand and water for mortar.
Day 4: Mix mortar under supervision.
Day 5: Record materials used and discuss waste prevention.

Character
Good building requires planning and proper material use. Guesswork causes waste and weak work.

Week 11. Block Laying Under Supervision

Teaching focus
Mortar bed, block placement, joints, alignment, level, plumb awareness and careful work.

Scripture
Ecclesiastes 9:10 “Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might.”

Practice
Day 1: Observe trainer demonstration of block laying.
Day 2: Practise spreading mortar under supervision.
Day 3: Lay blocks on a practice line under supervision.
Day 4: Check alignment and level.
Day 5: Clean the work area and record lessons learnt.

Character
Work should be done with seriousness. Half-hearted labour produces poor results.

Week 12. Wall Alignment, Openings and Quality Checks

Teaching focus
Straight walls, level, plumb awareness, door and window openings, lintel awareness and wall quality.

Scripture
Amos 7:7 “Behold, the Lord stood upon a wall made by a plumbline, with a plumbline in his hand.”

Practice
Day 1: Demonstrate use of spirit level and line.
Day 2: Check a practice wall for alignment.
Day 3: Identify door and window openings on a simple drawing.
Day 4: Discuss lintel purpose and safety.
Day 5: Complete a wall quality checklist.

Character
God values uprightness. Building straight walls should remind trainees to live straight lives.

Week 13. Concrete Materials and Mixing Awareness

Teaching focus
Cement, sand, aggregate, water, concrete uses, mix ratios at awareness level, strength and safety.

Scripture
Proverbs 24:3 “Through wisdom is an house builded; and by understanding it is established.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify concrete materials.
Day 2: Discuss where concrete is used in buildings.
Day 3: Demonstrate measuring materials for concrete.
Day 4: Mix a small concrete sample under supervision.
Day 5: Record materials and mixing observations.

Character
Strong work requires understanding. Trainees must know what they are doing and why.

Week 14. Concrete Placing, Compaction and Curing

Teaching focus
Placing concrete, avoiding too much water, compaction awareness, curing and protecting fresh concrete.

Scripture
James 1:4 “But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.”

Practice
Day 1: Place concrete in a sample mould or practice area.
Day 2: Discuss air spaces and compaction.
Day 3: Protect the concrete sample.
Day 4: Water and cure the concrete sample.
Day 5: Observe curing and record lessons.

Character
Concrete gains strength through process and time. People also mature through patience and discipline.

Week 15. Reinforcement and Formwork Awareness

Teaching focus
Steel bars, binding wire, reinforcement safety, timber formwork, temporary support and supervised observation.

Scripture
Ecclesiastes 4:12 “And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify reinforcement bars and binding wire.
Day 2: Discuss why concrete is reinforced.
Day 3: Observe safe handling of steel bars.
Day 4: Identify timber used for formwork.
Day 5: Observe a simple formwork model and record safety rules.

Character
Strength often comes through proper support. In life and building, support systems matter.

Week 16. Roofing, Doors and Windows Awareness

Teaching focus
Roof types, roof members, roofing sheets, rainwater control, door and window openings, safety at height.

Scripture
Proverbs 21:31 “The horse is prepared against the day of battle: but safety is of the LORD.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify different roof types from pictures or buildings.
Day 2: Identify timber, nails and roofing sheets where available.
Day 3: Discuss roof leaks and rainwater control.
Day 4: Identify door and window frames in buildings.
Day 5: Discuss safety rules around ladders and heights.

Character
Preparation is important, but safety ultimately requires wisdom, discipline and dependence on God.

Week 17. Plumbing Awareness in Buildings

Teaching focus
Water supply, drainage pipes, fittings, toilets, sinks, leaks, sanitation and reporting faults.

Scripture
Isaiah 58:11 “And thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify basic plumbing pipes and fittings.
Day 2: Trace simple water flow in a safe building example.
Day 3: Identify common leaks and drainage problems.
Day 4: Discuss water conservation.
Day 5: Prepare a simple plumbing fault report.

Character
Water must be managed wisely. Poor plumbing can damage buildings and harm health.

Week 18. Electrical Safety Awareness in Buildings

Teaching focus
Basic electrical safety, exposed wires, sockets, switches, danger signs and reporting faults.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:3 “A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify electrical hazards from pictures or safe examples.
Day 2: Discuss why trainees must not touch exposed wires.
Day 3: Learn how to report electrical faults.
Day 4: Identify safe and unsafe extension cable use.
Day 5: Complete an electrical safety awareness checklist.

Character
Wisdom avoids danger. Trainees must not pretend to know electrical work when they are not trained for it.

Week 19. Plastering, Screeding and Surface Preparation

Teaching focus
Purpose of plastering, surface preparation, mortar consistency, screeding awareness, neatness and quality.

Scripture
Colossians 3:23 “And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.”

Practice
Day 1: Observe wall surface preparation.
Day 2: Identify plastering tools.
Day 3: Observe plaster mixing demonstration.
Day 4: Practise applying plaster on a small sample surface under supervision.
Day 5: Review surface quality and clean the area.

Character
Visible finishing should be done with care, but hidden preparation also matters before God.

Week 20. Painting, Tiling and Final Finishing Awareness

Teaching focus
Paint types awareness, surface preparation, tiling awareness, spacing, neatness, cleaning and finishing quality.

Scripture
Psalm 90:17 “And let the beauty of the LORD our God be upon us: and establish thou the work of our hands upon us.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify finishing materials.
Day 2: Prepare a small surface for painting demonstration.
Day 3: Observe painting technique.
Day 4: Discuss tiling layout and spacing awareness.
Day 5: Complete a finishing quality checklist.

Character
Good finishing brings beauty and value. Trainees should ask God to establish the work of their hands.

Teaching focus
Site layout, material storage, tool storage, movement paths, waste control, cleanliness and supervisor reporting.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 14:40 “Let all things be done decently and in order.”

Practice
Day 1: Draw a simple building site organisation plan.
Day 2: Arrange tools and materials in assigned areas.
Day 3: Identify unsafe site organisation problems.
Day 4: Prepare a site cleanliness checklist.
Day 5: Conduct a supervised site organisation review.

Character
Order supports safety, speed and quality.

Week 22. Building Records and Material Control

Teaching focus
Material records, tool records, labour records, daily site logs, delivery notes and waste tracking.

Scripture
Habakkuk 2:2 “And the LORD answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.”

Practice
Day 1: Create a simple building site logbook.
Day 2: Record sample materials received.
Day 3: Record tools issued and returned.
Day 4: Record materials used for a sample task.
Day 5: Review records for accuracy and neatness.

Character
Clear records protect accountability and reduce confusion.

Week 23. Building Costing and Simple Estimation

Teaching focus
Material list, labour cost awareness, transport cost, waste allowance, simple quotation and cost control.

Scripture
Luke 14:28 “For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost?”

Practice
Day 1: List materials needed for a small block wall.
Day 2: Estimate number of blocks needed at awareness level.
Day 3: Estimate cement and sand needs at simple level.
Day 4: Add transport and labour awareness cost.
Day 5: Prepare a simple building cost sheet.

Character
Wise builders count the cost before starting. Poor costing causes waste and abandoned projects.

Week 24. Building Enterprise Opportunities

Teaching focus
Building as business, small service opportunities, honest pricing, customer care, quality and reputation.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:1 “A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold.”

Practice
Day 1: List building-related enterprise opportunities.
Day 2: Identify customers for one building service.
Day 3: Prepare a simple service description.
Day 4: Role-play customer communication.
Day 5: Prepare a simple building enterprise idea note.

Character
A good name is valuable. Poor workmanship and dishonesty can destroy future opportunities.

Week 25. Departmental Mini-Project Planning

Teaching focus
Planning a safe building-related project, roles, tools, materials, cost, safety and expected outcome.

Scripture
Nehemiah 2:18 “Then I told them of the hand of my God which was good upon me; as also the king’s words that he had spoken unto me. And they said, Let us rise up and build.”

Practice
Day 1: Choose a safe departmental mini-project.
Day 2: Write project goals and expected results.
Day 3: Prepare a tool and material list.
Day 4: Assign team roles and safety officers.
Day 5: Submit project plan for trainer approval.

Character
Vision must become organised action. Trainees must rise and build responsibly.

Week 26. Departmental Mini-Project Implementation

Teaching focus
Carrying out a supervised building-related project with safety, teamwork, records and quality control.

Scripture
Nehemiah 4:6 “So built we the wall; and all the wall was joined together unto the half thereof: for the people had a mind to work.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare project area and tools.
Day 2: Begin project implementation under supervision.
Day 3: Continue assigned tasks and record progress.
Day 4: Check safety, quality and teamwork.
Day 5: Clean the area and review progress.

Character
Progress comes when people have a mind to work.

Week 27. Final Practical Demonstration and Portfolio

Teaching focus
Demonstrating tool use, measurement, block work awareness, concrete awareness, records, safety and project evidence.

Scripture
2 Timothy 2:15 “Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed.”

Practice
Day 1: Demonstrate tool identification and safe handling.
Day 2: Demonstrate measurement and marking.
Day 3: Demonstrate basic block laying or mortar preparation under supervision.
Day 4: Organise building construction portfolio.
Day 5: Present practical evidence to trainer.

Character
A trained worker should not be ashamed. Diligence, skill and discipline prepare trainees for approval.

Week 28. Industrial Attachment Preparation

Teaching focus
Preparing for building site placement, supervisor conduct, site safety, daily logs, workplace expectations and final readiness.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:29 “Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify possible building construction attachment placements.
Day 2: Prepare personal attachment learning goals.
Day 3: Practise writing daily building attachment logs.
Day 4: Review site safety and workplace behaviour.
Day 5: Complete final departmental readiness assessment.

Character
Diligence opens doors. A faithful trainee can be trusted with greater responsibility.

modules.title: Communication Foundations, Listening and Speech Discipline
modules.content:
Module 1 of 7. Communication Foundations, Listening and Speech Discipline

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 1. Introduction to Communication Skills

Teaching focus
Meaning of communication, types of communication, importance of communication, communication process and common communication problems.

Scripture
Proverbs 18:21 “Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss the meaning of communication.
Day 2: Identify verbal, non-verbal, written and digital communication.
Day 3: Discuss examples of good and poor communication.
Day 4: Identify how words can build or destroy.
Day 5: Write a reflection on the power of the tongue.

Character
Words carry power. A trainee must use words carefully and responsibly.

Week 2. Listening Skills

Teaching focus
Active listening, attention, patience, avoiding interruption, understanding instructions and listening before responding.

Scripture
James 1:19 “Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath.”

Practice
Day 1: Practise listening to short instructions.
Day 2: Repeat key points after listening.
Day 3: Role-play listening without interrupting.
Day 4: Practise asking clarifying questions.
Day 5: Prepare a listening checklist.

Character
Good communication begins with listening. A wise person does not rush to speak.

Week 3. Speaking Clearly and Respectfully

Teaching focus
Voice, tone, pronunciation awareness, simple language, politeness, confidence and respectful expression.

Scripture
Colossians 4:6 “Let your speech be alway with grace, seasoned with salt, that ye may know how ye ought to answer every man.”

Practice
Day 1: Practise speaking clearly and audibly.
Day 2: Practise greeting and introducing oneself.
Day 3: Practise changing harsh words into polite words.
Day 4: Give a one-minute personal introduction.
Day 5: Prepare a graceful speech guide.

Character
Speech should carry grace. A trainee must not use words to insult or wound people.

Week 4. Barriers to Communication

Teaching focus
Noise, poor listening, unclear speech, wrong assumptions, anger, fear, language barriers, distractions and poor body language.

Scripture
Proverbs 18:13 “He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify communication barriers.
Day 2: Role-play misunderstanding caused by poor listening.
Day 3: Practise clarifying unclear instructions.
Day 4: Discuss how anger affects communication.
Day 5: Prepare a communication barrier solution chart.

Character
Answering before understanding brings shame. A trainee must listen properly before responding.

modules.title: Reading, Writing, Messages and Everyday Communication
modules.content:
Module 2 of 7. Reading, Writing, Messages and Everyday Communication

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 5. Reading for Understanding

Teaching focus
Reading instructions, identifying key points, summarising messages, asking questions and avoiding careless interpretation.

Scripture
Proverbs 4:7 “Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.”

Practice
Day 1: Read a simple instruction note.
Day 2: Identify the main message.
Day 3: Summarise the message in simple words.
Day 4: Ask questions about unclear parts.
Day 5: Complete a reading comprehension exercise.

Character
Understanding is important. A trainee should not act on a message he or she does not understand.

Week 6. Writing Simple Messages and Notices

Teaching focus
Clear sentences, short messages, notices, announcements, dates, times, locations and proofreading.

Scripture
Habakkuk 2:2 “And the LORD answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.”

Practice
Day 1: Write a simple announcement.
Day 2: Write a notice for a class activity.
Day 3: Add date, time and venue correctly.
Day 4: Proofread and correct mistakes.
Day 5: Present the notice to the class.

Character
Written communication should be plain so that people can understand and act.

Week 7. Writing Letters and Formal Messages

Teaching focus
Greeting, purpose, body, closing, respectful tone, official language and correct formatting.

Scripture
Proverbs 25:11 “A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in pictures of silver.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify parts of a simple formal letter.
Day 2: Write a request letter.
Day 3: Write an appreciation letter.
Day 4: Rewrite an informal message in a formal tone.
Day 5: Submit a corrected formal letter.

Character
The right words, properly arranged, can open doors and solve problems.

Week 8. Apology, Appreciation and Encouragement

Teaching focus
Sincere apology, saying thank you, encouraging others, correcting with love and restoring relationships.

Scripture
Ephesians 4:32 “And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you.”

Practice
Day 1: Write a sincere apology message.
Day 2: Write an appreciation message.
Day 3: Practise encouraging a discouraged colleague.
Day 4: Role-play correcting someone respectfully.
Day 5: Write a reflection on kindness in communication.

Character
Good communication should help heal relationships and encourage others.

modules.title: Interpersonal, Team and Workplace Communication
modules.content:
Module 3 of 7. Interpersonal, Team and Workplace Communication

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 9. Interpersonal Communication

Teaching focus
Greeting, introduction, respect, personal boundaries, politeness, patience, empathy and relationship building.

Scripture
Romans 12:10 “Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another.”

Practice
Day 1: Practise respectful greetings.
Day 2: Practise introducing oneself and another person.
Day 3: Role-play making a polite request.
Day 4: Practise showing empathy in conversation.
Day 5: Prepare an interpersonal communication checklist.

Character
Communication should honour people and strengthen relationships.

Week 10. Team Communication

Teaching focus
Group discussion, teamwork, giving updates, listening to teammates, sharing ideas and respecting different opinions.

Scripture
Ecclesiastes 4:9 “Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss the importance of communication in teams.
Day 2: Hold a group discussion on a simple topic.
Day 3: Practise giving a team progress update.
Day 4: Practise disagreeing respectfully.
Day 5: Present a group communication lesson.

Character
Teamwork improves when people speak clearly and listen respectfully.

Week 11. Receiving Instructions and Reporting Back

Teaching focus
Listening to instructions, writing notes, asking questions, carrying out tasks, reporting progress and reporting challenges.

Scripture
Proverbs 19:20 “Hear counsel, and receive instruction, that thou mayest be wise in thy latter end.”

Practice
Day 1: Listen to a supervisor’s instruction and write it down.
Day 2: Ask clarification questions.
Day 3: Prepare a task completion report.
Day 4: Role-play reporting a delay.
Day 5: Prepare an instruction and feedback checklist.

Character
A wise trainee receives instruction and reports back responsibly.

Week 12. Workplace Reports and Daily Updates

Teaching focus
Daily reports, progress updates, incident reports, problem reporting, factual writing and supervisor communication.

Scripture
Ephesians 4:25 “Wherefore putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare a simple daily activity report.
Day 2: Prepare a progress update.
Day 3: Prepare an incident report from a sample case.
Day 4: Review reports for truthfulness and clarity.
Day 5: Present a report to the trainer.

Character
Reports must be truthful. False reporting destroys trust.

modules.content:
Module 4 of 7. Public Speaking, Presentation and Meeting Communication

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 13. Introduction to Public Speaking

Teaching focus
Confidence, preparation, message structure, audience awareness, voice control, body language and nervousness management.

Scripture
2 Timothy 1:7 “For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss fear of speaking in public.
Day 2: Prepare a one-minute talk.
Day 3: Practise standing posture and voice projection.
Day 4: Deliver a one-minute talk.
Day 5: Receive respectful feedback.

Character
Confidence grows through preparation and practice. Fear must not stop useful communication.

Week 14. Organising a Speech or Presentation

Teaching focus
Introduction, main points, examples, conclusion, time management and simple presentation structure.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 14:40 “Let all things be done decently and in order.”

Practice
Day 1: Choose a short presentation topic.
Day 2: Prepare an introduction.
Day 3: Prepare three main points.
Day 4: Prepare a conclusion.
Day 5: Present the organised speech.

Character
A message should be orderly so that listeners can follow and understand.

Week 15. Meeting Communication and Minute Awareness

Teaching focus
Speaking in meetings, agenda, turn-taking, asking questions, recording decisions and action points.

Scripture
Proverbs 11:14 “Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare a meeting agenda.
Day 2: Hold a mock meeting.
Day 3: Practise speaking briefly and clearly.
Day 4: Record decisions and action points.
Day 5: Present meeting notes.

Character
Meetings require counsel, order and respect for others.

Week 16. Storytelling, Testimony and Persuasive Communication

Teaching focus
Using stories, personal testimony, examples, persuasion, emotional control, truthfulness and ethical influence.

Scripture
Psalm 107:2 “Let the redeemed of the LORD say so, whom he hath redeemed from the hand of the enemy.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss how stories help people understand.
Day 2: Prepare a short personal testimony or life lesson.
Day 3: Practise using examples to explain an idea.
Day 4: Discuss ethical persuasion.
Day 5: Present a short story or testimony.

Character
Stories and testimonies should be truthful and used to encourage, teach and build others.

modules.content:
Module 5 of 7. Digital Communication, Media Literacy and Conflict Handling

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 17. Digital Communication and Online Etiquette

Teaching focus
SMS, WhatsApp, email, social media, tone, timing, clarity, respect, privacy and responsible posting.

Scripture
Philippians 4:8 “Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss good and bad digital communication.
Day 2: Rewrite an unclear message clearly.
Day 3: Rewrite a rude message respectfully.
Day 4: Prepare a responsible social media post.
Day 5: Write a digital communication pledge.

Character
Online communication should reflect truth, honour and good report.

Week 18. Email and Professional Messaging

Teaching focus
Subject line, greeting, body, attachment, closing, response time, proofreading and professional tone.

Scripture
Colossians 4:6 “Let your speech be alway with grace, seasoned with salt, that ye may know how ye ought to answer every man.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify parts of a professional email.
Day 2: Write a professional email.
Day 3: Write a follow-up message.
Day 4: Practise attaching a document where available.
Day 5: Review emails for tone and clarity.

Character
Professional messages should be clear, respectful and gracious.

Week 19. Media Literacy, Rumours and Responsible Sharing

Teaching focus
Fake news, rumours, verification, forwarding messages, harmful content, online reputation and responsible speech.

Scripture
Exodus 20:16 “Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss how rumours spread.
Day 2: Identify messages that should not be forwarded.
Day 3: Practise checking information before sharing.
Day 4: Prepare a responsible sharing checklist.
Day 5: Write a reflection on false witness in digital communication.

Character
Sharing false information is dangerous. Trainees must not bear false witness online or offline.

Week 20. Conflict Communication and Peacebuilding

Teaching focus
Anger control, listening in conflict, apology, mediation, soft answers, avoiding insults and seeking peace.

Scripture
Proverbs 15:1 “A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss common causes of conflict.
Day 2: Role-play a disagreement handled badly.
Day 3: Role-play the same disagreement handled respectfully.
Day 4: Practise giving a soft answer.
Day 5: Prepare a peacebuilding communication guide.

Character
Soft words can reduce anger. Harsh words can increase conflict.

Week 21. Leadership Communication

Teaching focus

Scripture
Nehemiah 2:18 “Then I told them of the hand of my God which was good upon me; as also the king’s words that he had spoken unto me. And they said, Let us rise up and build.”

Practice
Day 1: Practise explaining a simple vision.
Day 2: Practise giving instructions clearly.
Day 3: Practise encouraging a team.
Day 4: Practise correcting someone respectfully.
Day 5: Present a leadership communication role-play.

Character
Good leaders communicate vision and encourage people to build responsibly.

Week 22. Customer Service and Community Communication

Teaching focus
Welcoming customers, listening to needs, explaining services, handling complaints, giving directions and protecting trust.

Scripture
Matthew 7:12 “Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them.”

Practice
Day 1: Practise welcoming a customer or visitor.
Day 2: Practise listening to a customer complaint.
Day 3: Practise explaining a service clearly.

Week 23. Communication for Ministry, Teaching and Training

Scripture

Day 2: Practise explaining a short lesson.
Day 3: Practise leading a group discussion.
Day 4: Practise asking open questions.
Day 5: Present a five-minute teaching exercise.

Week 24. Communication Enterprise Opportunities

Teaching focus

Scripture

Practice

Day 3: Prepare a simple service description.

modules.title: Advanced Practice, Departmental Project and Attachment Preparation
modules.content:
Module 7 of 7. Advanced Practice, Departmental Project and Attachment Preparation

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 25. Departmental Mini-Project Planning

Teaching focus
Planning a communication project, audience, purpose, message, channel, team roles, materials, ethics and expected outcome.

Scripture
Habakkuk 2:2 “And the LORD answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.”

Practice
Day 1: Choose a communication mini-project.
Day 2: Identify the audience and purpose.
Day 3: Prepare key messages and communication channels.
Day 4: Assign team roles and prepare materials.
Day 5: Submit the project plan for trainer approval.

Character
Clear planning makes communication more useful and effective.

Week 26. Departmental Mini-Project Implementation

Teaching focus
Carrying out a supervised communication project with speaking, writing, teamwork, feedback and ethical communication.

Scripture
Nehemiah 4:6 “So built we the wall; and all the wall was joined together unto the half thereof: for the people had a mind to work.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare communication materials.
Day 2: Deliver messages, presentations or written content under supervision.
Day 3: Collect feedback from the audience.
Day 4: Review clarity, tone and impact.
Day 5: Prepare a progress report.

Character
Progress comes when people communicate, work together and remain disciplined.

Week 27. Final Practical Demonstration and Portfolio

Teaching focus
Demonstrating listening, speaking, writing, presentation, workplace communication, conflict handling and portfolio evidence.

Scripture
2 Timothy 2:15 “Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed.”

Practice
Day 1: Demonstrate listening and instruction response.
Day 2: Demonstrate formal writing and report writing.
Day 3: Demonstrate presentation and conflict communication.
Day 4: Organise communication skills portfolio.
Day 5: Present practical evidence to the trainer.

Character
A trained worker should not be ashamed. Communication skill requires practice, discipline and character.

Week 28. Industrial Attachment Preparation

Teaching focus
Preparing for workplace communication, supervisor conduct, customer service, written reports, confidentiality, daily logs and final readiness.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:29 “Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify possible attachment settings where communication skills are needed.
Day 2: Prepare personal attachment learning goals.
Day 3: Practise writing daily communication attachment logs.
Day 4: Review workplace speech, confidentiality and reporting standards.
Day 5: Complete final departmental readiness assessment.

Character
Diligent communicators can serve in important places.
