modules.title: Construction Orientation, Safety and Dignity of Labour
modules.content:
Module 1 of 7. Construction Orientation, Safety and Dignity of Labour

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 1. Introduction to Construction Technology

Teaching focus
Meaning of construction, importance of building, types of construction projects, dignity of construction work and the role of trained workers.

Scripture
Proverbs 24:3 “Through wisdom is an house builded; and by understanding it is established.”

Practice
Day 1: Walk around the Academy environment and identify buildings, drainage, walkways and structures.
Day 2: List different construction projects in the community.
Day 3: Identify people involved in construction, such as labourers, masons, carpenters, plumbers, electricians, engineers and supervisors.
Day 4: Discuss common construction problems in communities, such as poor workmanship, weak drainage and unsafe buildings.
Day 5: Write a reflection on why construction must be done with wisdom.

Character
Construction must be done with wisdom and understanding. A careless builder can endanger lives.

Week 2. Construction Site Discipline and Safety

Teaching focus
Construction site rules, personal protective equipment, hazard awareness, punctuality, obedience and site order.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:3 “A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify common site hazards such as sharp objects, falling materials, open trenches and exposed wires.
Day 2: Demonstrate correct use of helmets, boots, gloves and reflective jackets where available.
Day 3: Practise safe movement around a construction area.
Day 4: Prepare a basic site safety checklist.
Day 5: Conduct a supervised site safety inspection.

Character
Safety is wisdom. A wise trainee sees danger early and avoids careless behaviour.

Week 3. Construction Tools and Their Uses

Teaching focus
Common construction tools, their uses, safe handling, cleaning, storage and tool accountability.

Scripture
Luke 16:10 “He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify basic construction tools and state their uses.
Day 2: Practise safe carrying of tools such as hammer, trowel, shovel, measuring tape and spirit level.
Day 3: Clean tools after use.
Day 4: Arrange tools in a tool storage area.
Day 5: Complete a tool issue and return record.

Character
Faithfulness begins with small things. A trainee who handles tools carelessly cannot be trusted with bigger responsibilities.

Week 4. Building Materials and Material Stewardship

Teaching focus
Cement, sand, gravel, blocks, water, timber, nails, reinforcement awareness, storage and waste prevention.

Scripture
John 6:12 “When they were filled, he said unto his disciples, Gather up the fragments that remain, that nothing be lost.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify common building materials.
Day 2: Discuss the uses of cement, sand, gravel, blocks and timber.
Day 3: Demonstrate proper storage of cement and other materials.
Day 4: Identify ways materials are wasted on construction sites.
Day 5: Prepare a material stewardship checklist.

Character
Waste is poor stewardship. Materials must be handled carefully because waste increases cost and delays work.

modules.title: Measurement, Setting-Out Awareness and Site Preparation
modules.content:
Module 2 of 7. Measurement, Setting-Out Awareness and Site Preparation

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 5. Basic Measurement in Construction

Teaching focus
Length, width, height, measuring tape, units of measurement, accuracy and recording measurements.

Scripture
Proverbs 11:1 “A false balance is abomination to the LORD: but a just weight is his delight.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify measuring tools.
Day 2: Practise measuring simple lengths using measuring tape.
Day 3: Measure width and height of simple objects.
Day 4: Record measurements neatly.
Day 5: Compare group measurements and discuss errors.

Character
Accuracy is part of integrity. False or careless measurement can damage construction work.

Week 6. Lines, Angles and Simple Setting-Out

Teaching focus
Straight lines, pegs, strings, right angles, marking boundaries and simple building layout awareness.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 14:40 “Let all things be done decently and in order.”

Practice
Day 1: Demonstrate how to use pegs and string.
Day 2: Mark a straight line on the ground.
Day 3: Mark a simple rectangular layout under supervision.
Day 4: Check alignment using string.
Day 5: Record layout dimensions in a simple site notebook.

Character
Order is necessary in construction. A wrongly marked line can affect the entire structure.

Week 7. Site Clearing and Preparation

Teaching focus
Clearing site, removing waste, preparing safe access, basic drainage awareness and teamwork.

Scripture
Isaiah 40:3 “Prepare ye the way of the LORD, make straight in the desert a highway for our God.”

Practice
Day 1: Inspect a practice site and identify obstacles.
Day 2: Clear waste materials under supervision.
Day 3: Remove stones, sticks and unsafe objects.
Day 4: Create safe movement paths.
Day 5: Review the prepared site and record work completed.

Character
Preparation matters. A good builder prepares the ground before building.

Week 8. Foundation Awareness

Teaching focus
Meaning of foundation, importance of strong foundation, excavation awareness, soil observation and safety around trenches.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 3:10 “According to the grace of God which is given unto me, as a wise masterbuilder, I have laid the foundation.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss why foundations are important.
Day 2: Observe different soil types around the training area.
Day 3: Mark a sample foundation line under supervision.
Day 4: Discuss trench safety and dangers of collapse.
Day 5: Draw a simple foundation awareness diagram.

Character
A strong life, like a strong building, needs a strong foundation.

modules.title: Block Work, Mortar and Masonry Basics
modules.content:
Module 3 of 7. Block Work, Mortar and Masonry Basics

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 9. Introduction to Masonry and Block Work

Teaching focus
Meaning of masonry, types of blocks, uses of blocks, wall construction and role of the mason.

Scripture
Nehemiah 4:6 “So built we the wall; and all the wall was joined together unto the half thereof: for the people had a mind to work.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify different block types where available.
Day 2: Discuss strong and weak blocks.
Day 3: Carry and stack blocks safely.
Day 4: Arrange blocks along a marked line.
Day 5: Record lessons on block handling.

Character
Good work requires a willing mind. Team effort helps walls rise.

Week 10. Mortar Materials and Mixing

Teaching focus
Cement, sand, water, mortar mix, correct proportion awareness, avoiding excess water and safe mixing.

Scripture
Luke 14:28 “For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost?”

Practice
Day 1: Identify cement, sand and water as mortar materials.
Day 2: Demonstrate measuring materials for mortar.
Day 3: Mix mortar under supervision.
Day 4: Observe good and poor mortar consistency.
Day 5: Record materials used in the mortar mix.

Character
A builder must count, measure and plan. Guesswork creates waste and weak work.

Week 11. Laying Blocks Under Supervision

Teaching focus
Mortar bed, block placement, joints, alignment, level and safe supervised practice.

Scripture
Ecclesiastes 9:10 “Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might.”

Practice
Day 1: Observe trainer demonstration of block laying.
Day 2: Practise spreading mortar under supervision.
Day 3: Lay blocks on a practice line under supervision.
Day 4: Check alignment and level.
Day 5: Clean the work area and record lessons learnt.

Character
Work must be done with seriousness. Half-hearted work produces poor results.

Week 12. Wall Alignment, Level and Quality

Teaching focus
Checking straightness, plumb awareness, level awareness, joint thickness and correction of errors.

Scripture
Amos 7:7 “Behold, the Lord stood upon a wall made by a plumbline, with a plumbline in his hand.”

Practice
Day 1: Demonstrate the use of spirit level.
Day 2: Check a practice wall for alignment.
Day 3: Identify uneven joints.
Day 4: Correct simple alignment errors under supervision.
Day 5: Complete a wall quality checklist.

Character
God values uprightness. Construction teaches trainees to build straight and live straight.

modules.title: Concrete, Reinforcement Awareness, Carpentry and Formwork Basics
modules.content:
Module 4 of 7. Concrete, Reinforcement Awareness, Carpentry and Formwork Basics

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 13. Introduction to Concrete

Teaching focus
Meaning of concrete, cement, sand, aggregate, water, concrete uses and concrete strength awareness.

Scripture
Proverbs 24:3 “Through wisdom is an house builded; and by understanding it is established.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify concrete materials.
Day 2: Discuss where concrete is used.
Day 3: Demonstrate basic concrete material measurement.
Day 4: Observe concrete mixing under supervision.
Day 5: Record materials and mixing observations.

Character
Strong work requires understanding. Trainees must know what they are mixing and why.

Week 14. Concrete Mixing, Placing and Curing

Teaching focus
Mixing concrete, placing concrete, avoiding too much water, compaction awareness and curing.

Scripture
James 1:4 “But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.”

Practice
Day 1: Mix a small concrete sample under supervision.
Day 2: Place concrete in a sample mould or training area.
Day 3: Discuss compaction and air gaps.
Day 4: Water and protect concrete for curing.
Day 5: Observe curing process and record lessons.

Character
Concrete needs time to gain strength. People also need patience and process to mature.

Week 15. Reinforcement Awareness and Safety

Teaching focus
Purpose of reinforcement, steel bars, tying awareness, sharp edges, spacing awareness and safety.

Scripture
Ecclesiastes 4:12 “And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify reinforcement bars where available.
Day 2: Discuss why concrete is strengthened with steel.
Day 3: Observe safe handling of reinforcement.
Day 4: Practise simple tying with trainer supervision where appropriate.
Day 5: Record reinforcement safety rules.

Character
Strength often comes through proper support. Teamwork and inner strength help people stand.

Week 16. Carpentry and Formwork Awareness

Teaching focus
Timber use, formwork, measuring timber, nailing, temporary support, safe handling of carpentry tools.

Scripture
Exodus 31:3 “And I have filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify timber and simple carpentry tools.
Day 2: Measure and mark timber under supervision.
Day 3: Observe cutting and nailing demonstration.
Day 4: Observe simple formwork assembly.
Day 5: Remove nails safely from waste timber and clean the area.

Character
Skill is a gift that must be developed with wisdom, understanding and discipline.

modules.title: Building Services Awareness, Finishes and Maintenance
modules.content:
Module 5 of 7. Building Services Awareness, Finishes and Maintenance

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 17. Plumbing Awareness in Buildings

Teaching focus
Water supply basics, drainage awareness, pipes, fittings, leaks, sanitation and reporting faults.

Scripture
Isaiah 58:11 “And thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify basic plumbing pipes and fittings.
Day 2: Trace simple water flow in a building where safe.
Day 3: Identify common leaks and drainage problems.
Day 4: Discuss water conservation.
Day 5: Prepare a simple plumbing fault report.

Character
Water must be managed wisely. Waste of water and poor drainage can damage buildings and communities.

Week 18. Electrical Safety Awareness

Teaching focus
Basic electrical safety, danger of exposed wires, reporting faults, no unauthorised electrical work and safe behaviour.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:3 “A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify electrical hazards from pictures or supervised examples.
Day 2: Discuss why trainees must not touch exposed wires.
Day 3: Learn how to report electrical faults.
Day 4: Identify safe and unsafe extension cable use.
Day 5: Complete an electrical safety awareness checklist.

Character
Wisdom avoids danger. Trainees must not pretend to know electrical work when they are not trained for it.

Week 19. Plastering and Rendering Awareness

Teaching focus
Purpose of plastering, wall preparation, mortar consistency, surface finishing and quality control.

Scripture
Colossians 3:23 “And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.”

Practice
Day 1: Observe wall surface preparation.
Day 2: Identify plastering tools.
Day 3: Observe plaster mixing demonstration.
Day 4: Practise applying plaster on a small sample board under supervision.
Day 5: Review surface quality and clean the area.

Character
Finishing work should be done with care. Hidden and visible work both matter before God.

Week 20. Painting, Tiling and Finishing Awareness

Teaching focus
Surface preparation, paint types awareness, tiling awareness, neatness, finishing quality and customer satisfaction.

Scripture
Psalm 90:17 “And let the beauty of the LORD our God be upon us: and establish thou the work of our hands upon us.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify finishing materials.
Day 2: Prepare a small surface for painting demonstration.
Day 3: Observe painting technique.
Day 4: Discuss tiling layout and spacing awareness.
Day 5: Complete a finishing quality checklist.

Character
Good finishing brings beauty and value. Trainees should desire God to establish the work of their hands.

modules.title: Construction Management, Costing, Quality and Enterprise
modules.content:
Module 6 of 7. Construction Management, Costing, Quality and Enterprise

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 21. Construction Site Organisation

Teaching focus
Site layout, material storage, movement paths, waste control, tool storage, teamwork and supervisor reporting.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 14:40 “Let all things be done decently and in order.”

Practice
Day 1: Draw a simple site organisation plan.
Day 2: Arrange tools and materials in assigned areas.
Day 3: Identify unsafe site organisation problems.
Day 4: Prepare a site cleanliness checklist.
Day 5: Conduct a supervised site organisation review.

Character
Order supports safety, speed and quality.

Week 22. Construction Records and Material Control

Teaching focus
Material records, tool records, labour records, daily site logs, delivery notes and waste tracking.

Scripture
Habakkuk 2:2 “And the LORD answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.”

Practice
Day 1: Create a simple material record sheet.
Day 2: Record sample cement, sand, blocks and tools received.
Day 3: Record materials used for a sample task.
Day 4: Compare materials received and materials used.
Day 5: Review records for accuracy.

Character
Clear records protect honesty and accountability.

Week 23. Construction Costing and Simple Estimation

Teaching focus
Material list, labour cost awareness, transport cost, waste allowance, simple quotation and cost control.

Scripture
Luke 14:28 “For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost?”

Practice
Day 1: List materials needed for a small block work task.
Day 2: Estimate number of blocks needed for a sample wall.
Day 3: Estimate cement and sand needs at a simple awareness level.
Day 4: Add transport and labour awareness cost.
Day 5: Prepare a simple construction cost sheet.

Character
Wise builders count the cost before starting.

Week 24. Construction Enterprise Opportunities

Teaching focus
Construction as business, small service opportunities, customer care, honest pricing, quality and reputation.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:1 “A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold.”

Practice
Day 1: List construction-related enterprise opportunities.
Day 2: Identify customers for one construction service.
Day 3: Prepare a simple service description.
Day 4: Role-play customer communication.
Day 5: Prepare a simple construction enterprise idea note.

Character
A good name is valuable in construction. Poor work and dishonesty destroy future opportunities.

Module 7 of 7. Advanced Practice, Departmental Project and Attachment Preparation

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 25. Departmental Mini-Project Planning

Teaching focus
Planning a simple construction-related project, roles, tools, materials, cost, safety and expected outcome.

Scripture
Nehemiah 2:18 “Then I told them of the hand of my God which was good upon me; as also the king’s words that he had spoken unto me. And they said, Let us rise up and build.”

Practice
Day 1: Choose a safe departmental mini-project.
Day 2: Write project goals and expected results.
Day 3: Prepare a tool and material list.
Day 4: Assign team roles and safety officers.
Day 5: Submit project plan for trainer approval.

Character
Vision must become organised action. Trainees must rise and build responsibly.

Week 26. Departmental Mini-Project Implementation

Teaching focus
Carrying out a supervised construction project with safety, teamwork, records and quality control.

Scripture
Nehemiah 4:6 “So built we the wall; and all the wall was joined together unto the half thereof: for the people had a mind to work.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare project area and tools.
Day 2: Begin project implementation under supervision.
Day 3: Continue assigned tasks and record progress.
Day 4: Check safety, quality and teamwork.
Day 5: Clean the area and review progress.

Character
Progress comes when people have a mind to work.

Week 27. Final Practical Demonstration and Portfolio

Teaching focus
Demonstrating tool use, measurement, block work awareness, record keeping, safety and project evidence.

Scripture
2 Timothy 2:15 “Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed.”

Practice
Day 1: Demonstrate tool identification and safe handling.
Day 2: Demonstrate measurement and marking.
Day 3: Demonstrate basic block laying or mortar preparation under supervision.
Day 4: Organise construction portfolio.
Day 5: Present practical evidence to trainer.

Character
A trained worker should not be ashamed. Diligence, skill and discipline prepare trainees for approval.

Week 28. Industrial Attachment Preparation

Teaching focus
Preparing for construction placement, supervisor conduct, site safety, daily logs, workplace expectations and final readiness.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:29 “Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify possible construction attachment placements.
Day 2: Prepare personal attachment learning goals.
Day 3: Practise writing daily construction attachment logs.
Day 4: Review site safety and workplace behaviour.
Day 5: Complete final departmental readiness assessment.

Character
Diligence opens doors. A faithful trainee can be trusted with greater responsibility.

modules.title: Finance Orientation, Stewardship and Basic Records
modules.content:
Module 1 of 7. Finance Orientation, Stewardship and Basic Records

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 1. Introduction to Finance and Accounting

Teaching focus
Meaning of finance, meaning of accounting, importance of financial records, money as stewardship and the role of finance workers.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 4:2 “Moreover it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss what finance and accounting mean.
Day 2: List places where accounting is needed, such as shops, farms, ministries, schools and NGOs.
Day 3: Identify common financial documents, such as receipts, invoices and payment vouchers.
Day 4: Discuss why money requires trust.
Day 5: Write a reflection on why faithfulness is required in financial work.

Character
Finance work is stewardship. A trainee must be faithful before being trusted with money.

Week 2. Income, Expenses and Simple Financial Language

Teaching focus
Income, expenses, profit, loss, assets, liabilities, capital, savings and basic financial terms.

Scripture
Proverbs 4:7 “Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.”

Practice
Day 1: Define income and expenses with simple examples.
Day 2: Identify examples of assets and liabilities.
Day 3: Classify sample transactions as income or expenses.
Day 4: Calculate simple profit or loss from a small business example.
Day 5: Prepare a simple finance vocabulary sheet.

Character
Understanding comes before responsibility. A trainee must understand financial language before handling records.

Week 3. Receipts, Vouchers and Supporting Documents

Teaching focus
Receipts, payment vouchers, invoices, delivery notes, approval notes, evidence of payment and filing.

Scripture
Habakkuk 2:2 “And the LORD answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify receipts, vouchers and invoices.
Day 2: Practise writing a simple receipt.
Day 3: Practise filling a simple payment voucher.
Day 4: Match transactions with supporting documents.
Day 5: Arrange documents in a simple file.

Character
Clear documentation protects truth and reduces confusion.

Week 4. Honesty, Confidentiality and Financial Character

Teaching focus
Financial honesty, confidentiality, avoiding gossip, avoiding fraud, reporting mistakes and respecting authority.

Scripture
Proverbs 11:1 “A false balance is abomination to the LORD: but a just weight is his delight.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss dishonest practices in finance work.
Day 2: Role-play how to report a cash mistake honestly.
Day 3: Discuss why financial information must be kept confidential.
Day 4: Prepare a finance ethics pledge.
Day 5: Review practical examples of honest and dishonest records.

Character
Dishonesty in finance is dangerous. God delights in truth and fairness.

modules.title: Bookkeeping, Cashbook and Petty Cash
modules.content:
Module 2 of 7. Bookkeeping, Cashbook and Petty Cash

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 5. Introduction to Bookkeeping

Teaching focus
Meaning of bookkeeping, daily recording, income records, expense records, accuracy and neatness.

Scripture
Luke 16:10 “He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much.”

Practice
Day 1: Create a simple income record sheet.
Day 2: Create a simple expense record sheet.
Day 3: Record sample sales and expenses.
Day 4: Check records for missing details.
Day 5: Prepare a neat weekly transaction summary.

Character
Small records matter. Faithfulness in little entries prepares trainees for greater financial responsibility.

Week 6. Simple Cashbook Preparation

Teaching focus
Cash received, cash paid, balance, date, description, reference number and daily closing balance.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 14:40 “Let all things be done decently and in order.”

Practice
Day 1: Learn the columns of a simple cashbook.
Day 2: Record sample cash received.
Day 3: Record sample cash paid out.
Day 4: Calculate closing balance.
Day 5: Review cashbook errors and correct them.

Character
Order in records protects money and supports accountability.

Week 7. Petty Cash Management

Teaching focus
Meaning of petty cash, small expenses, petty cash voucher, approvals, float, replenishment and safe custody.

Scripture
Proverbs 21:5 “The thoughts of the diligent tend only to plenteousness; but of every one that is hasty only to want.”

Practice
Day 1: Define petty cash and list examples of petty expenses.
Day 2: Fill a petty cash voucher.
Day 3: Record petty cash payments.
Day 4: Balance petty cash using sample figures.
Day 5: Prepare a petty cash report.

Character
Small expenses must be controlled. Careless small spending can become a big loss.

Week 8. Cash Counting, Cash Security and Error Reporting

Teaching focus
Cash counting, cash shortage, cash surplus, safe storage, two-person verification and honest reporting.

Scripture
Ephesians 4:25 “Wherefore putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour.”

Practice
Day 1: Practise counting sample cash or training notes.
Day 2: Compare counted cash with recorded balance.
Day 3: Identify cash shortage or surplus in an exercise.
Day 4: Role-play reporting a cash difference.
Day 5: Prepare a cash handling checklist.

Character
A finance trainee must speak truthfully. Hiding cash errors can lead to greater trouble.

modules.title: Budgeting, Savings, Cost Control and Personal Finance
modules.content:
Module 3 of 7. Budgeting, Savings, Cost Control and Personal Finance

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 9. Personal Budgeting

Teaching focus
Income, needs, wants, savings, giving, transport, food, communication, emergency planning and spending control.

Scripture
Proverbs 21:20 “There is treasure to be desired and oil in the dwelling of the wise; but a foolish man spendeth it up.”

Practice
Day 1: List common personal income and expenses.
Day 2: Separate needs from wants.
Day 3: Prepare a simple weekly personal budget.
Day 4: Discuss how impulsive spending causes lack.
Day 5: Review and improve the budget.

Character
Wise people do not spend everything they receive. Discipline in personal finance prepares trainees for public finance.

Week 10. Departmental and Project Budgeting

Teaching focus
Budget purpose, expected income, planned expenses, approval, monitoring and budget discipline.

Scripture
Luke 14:28 “For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost?”

Practice
Day 1: List items needed for a small departmental project.
Day 2: Estimate cost for each item.
Day 3: Prepare a simple project budget.
Day 4: Identify possible savings or waste.
Day 5: Present the budget to the trainer.

Character
Wise people count the cost before starting. Budgeting prevents waste and abandoned projects.

Week 11. Cost Control and Waste Reduction

Teaching focus
Cost control, avoiding waste, comparing prices, preventing leakage, tracking expenses and wise purchasing.

Scripture
John 6:12 “When they were filled, he said unto his disciples, Gather up the fragments that remain, that nothing be lost.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify common causes of financial waste.
Day 2: Compare prices from sample suppliers.
Day 3: Review a sample budget and identify waste.
Day 4: Prepare a cost control checklist.
Day 5: Write a short note on why waste is poor stewardship.

Character
Waste is not good stewardship. Money, materials and time must be used wisely.

Week 12. Savings, Debt and Financial Discipline

Teaching focus
Saving habits, emergency funds, debt awareness, borrowing dangers, repayment discipline and avoiding unnecessary debt.

Scripture
Romans 13:7 “Render therefore to all their dues: tribute to whom tribute is due; custom to whom custom; fear to whom fear; honour to whom honour.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss why saving is important.
Day 2: Prepare a simple savings plan.
Day 3: Discuss good and bad borrowing.
Day 4: Prepare a simple debt repayment schedule.
Day 5: Discuss why financial obligations must be honoured.

Character
A person of integrity takes financial commitments seriously.

modules.title: Sales, Purchases, Stock and Banking Awareness
modules.content:
Module 4 of 7. Sales, Purchases, Stock and Banking Awareness

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 13. Sales Records and Daily Sales Summary

Teaching focus
Sales book, cash sales, credit sales awareness, sales receipt, daily sales summary and customer records.

Scripture
Proverbs 11:1 “A false balance is abomination to the LORD: but a just weight is his delight.”

Practice
Day 1: Record sample cash sales.
Day 2: Write sales receipts.
Day 3: Prepare a daily sales summary.
Day 4: Compare cash received with sales recorded.
Day 5: Discuss how false sales records damage trust.

Character
Sales records must be honest. A false record is a form of deceit.

Week 14. Purchase Records and Supplier Documentation

Teaching focus
Purchase records, invoices, delivery notes, supplier names, payment status and filing.

Scripture
Proverbs 19:20 “Hear counsel, and receive instruction, that thou mayest be wise in thy latter end.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify purchase invoices and delivery notes.
Day 2: Record sample purchases.
Day 3: Match purchase records with invoices.
Day 4: Prepare a supplier record sheet.
Day 5: Review purchase records for accuracy.

Character
A wise trainee follows instructions and records purchases properly.

Week 15. Stock and Inventory Records

Teaching focus
Opening stock, purchases, sales, closing stock, stock count, stock card, shortages and stock control.

Scripture
Proverbs 27:23 “Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, and look well to thy herds.”

Practice
Day 1: Count sample stock items.
Day 2: Create a simple stock card.
Day 3: Record stock received.
Day 4: Record stock issued or sold.
Day 5: Compare physical stock with stock record.

Character
A responsible finance worker knows the state of what is entrusted to the organisation.

Week 16. Banking, Deposits and Reconciliation Awareness

Teaching focus
Bank deposits, withdrawals, transfers, bank charges, bank statement, cashbook comparison and reconciliation awareness.

Scripture
2 Corinthians 8:21 “Providing for honest things, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify items on a sample bank statement.
Day 2: Record sample bank deposits.
Day 3: Record sample bank withdrawals and charges.
Day 4: Compare a cashbook with a bank statement.
Day 5: Identify differences and prepare a simple reconciliation note.

Character
Finance work must be honest before God and before people. Transparency builds trust.

modules.title: Payroll, Cooperative Records, Reporting and Digital Skills
modules.content:
Module 5 of 7. Payroll, Cooperative Records, Reporting and Digital Skills

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 17. Payroll and Allowance Records Awareness

Teaching focus
Wages, salaries, allowances, attendance, deductions awareness, approval, confidentiality and payment records.

Scripture
Leviticus 19:13 “Thou shalt not defraud thy neighbour, neither rob him: the wages of him that is hired shall not abide with thee all night until the morning.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss why workers must be paid correctly.
Day 2: Prepare a simple attendance-based payment sheet.
Day 3: Calculate sample daily wages.
Day 4: Prepare a payment acknowledgement form.
Day 5: Discuss payroll confidentiality and honesty.

Character
Workers’ wages must be handled fairly. Finance workers must not cheat or delay what is due.

Week 18. Cooperative and Group Savings Records

Teaching focus
Savings groups, member contributions, loan records, repayments, group accountability and trust.

Scripture
Ecclesiastes 4:9 “Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss how cooperative savings work.
Day 2: Create a member contribution sheet.
Day 3: Record sample savings contributions.
Day 4: Record sample loan and repayment entries.
Day 5: Prepare a cooperative financial summary.

Character
Group finance requires trust, honesty and accountability.

Week 19. Simple Financial Reports

Teaching focus
Daily report, weekly report, monthly summary, income and expense report, budget report and simple profit or loss.

Scripture
Habakkuk 2:2 “And the LORD answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare a daily cash report.
Day 2: Prepare a weekly income summary.
Day 3: Prepare a weekly expense summary.
Day 4: Prepare a simple profit or loss statement.
Day 5: Present the financial report clearly.

Character
Financial reports must be clear enough for others to understand and act upon.

Week 20. Basic Spreadsheet and Digital Record Keeping

Teaching focus
Spreadsheet columns, rows, simple calculations, saving files, naming files, protecting records and avoiding unauthorised editing.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 14:40 “Let all things be done decently and in order.”

Practice
Day 1: Create a simple income and expense spreadsheet.
Day 2: Enter sample transactions.
Day 3: Use simple addition to calculate totals.
Day 4: Save and name the file properly.
Day 5: Print or present a simple spreadsheet report.

Character
Digital records also require order, accuracy and truthfulness.

modules.title: Financial Control, Audit Awareness, Tax Awareness and Enterprise
modules.content:
Module 6 of 7. Financial Control, Audit Awareness, Tax Awareness and Enterprise

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 21. Internal Control and Approval Systems

Teaching focus
Authorisation, separation of duties, receipt control, payment approval, stock control, cash limits and supervision.

Scripture
Proverbs 11:14 “Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss why one person should not control everything.
Day 2: Design a simple payment approval process.
Day 3: Prepare a receipt control record.
Day 4: Review a case study of weak internal control.
Day 5: Prepare an internal control checklist.

Character
Accountability protects both the organisation and the person handling money.

Week 22. Audit Awareness and Correction of Records

Teaching focus
Meaning of audit, checking records, supporting documents, error correction, missing receipts and cooperation with auditors.

Scripture
2 Corinthians 13:5 “Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss what audit means.
Day 2: Check a sample cashbook for errors.
Day 3: Match receipts to recorded expenses.
Day 4: Identify missing documents.
Day 5: Prepare an audit readiness checklist.

Character
Checking records is not punishment. It helps reveal errors and strengthen accountability.

Week 23. Tax, Levies and Legal Financial Responsibilities Awareness

Teaching focus
Taxes, levies, licences, receipts, official payments, avoiding illegal payments and obeying lawful financial obligations.

Scripture
Romans 13:7 “Render therefore to all their dues: tribute to whom tribute is due; custom to whom custom; fear to whom fear; honour to whom honour.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss why businesses and citizens have financial responsibilities.
Day 2: Identify examples of lawful payments and receipts.
Day 3: Discuss the danger of paying money without official evidence.
Day 4: Prepare a simple official payment record.
Day 5: Discuss why receipts must be collected and filed.

Character
A Kingdom finance worker must respect lawful financial obligations and avoid dishonest shortcuts.

Week 24. Finance and Accounting Enterprise Opportunities

Teaching focus
Bookkeeping support, budget preparation, receipt management, small business records, cooperative records, church accounts support and ethical service.

Scripture
Deuteronomy 8:18 “But thou shalt remember the LORD thy God: for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth.”

Practice
Day 1: List enterprise opportunities in finance and accounting support.
Day 2: Identify customers for one bookkeeping service.
Day 3: Prepare a simple service description.
Day 4: Prepare a small-start budget.
Day 5: Write a finance and accounting enterprise idea note.

Character
The power to create wealth comes from God. Finance enterprise must be built on honesty, confidentiality, competence and faithful service.

Module 7 of 7. Advanced Practice, Departmental Project and Attachment Preparation

Week 25. Departmental Mini-Project Planning

Teaching focus
Planning a supervised finance project, roles, documents, records, confidentiality, reporting and expected results.

Scripture
Nehemiah 2:18 “Then I told them of the hand of my God which was good upon me; as also the king’s words that he had spoken unto me. And they said, Let us rise up and build.”

Practice
Day 1: Choose a safe departmental finance project.
Day 2: Prepare project goals and expected results.
Day 3: Prepare records, forms and reporting templates.
Day 4: Assign team roles and confidentiality rules.
Day 5: Submit project plan for trainer approval.

Character
Vision must become organised action. Finance work must be planned, supervised and accountable.

Week 26. Departmental Mini-Project Implementation

Teaching focus
Carrying out a supervised finance or bookkeeping project with accuracy, teamwork, confidentiality and records.

Scripture
Nehemiah 4:6 “So built we the wall; and all the wall was joined together unto the half thereof: for the people had a mind to work.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare documents and working area.
Day 2: Begin transaction recording or budgeting task.
Day 3: Continue assigned records and check accuracy.
Day 4: Prepare draft financial summary.
Day 5: Review records, correct errors and submit progress report.

modules.title: Heavy Equipment Orientation, Safety and Discipline
modules.content:
Module 1 of 7. Heavy Equipment Orientation, Safety and Discipline

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 1. Introduction to Heavy Equipment Operations

Teaching focus
Meaning of heavy equipment, importance of machines in construction and development, types of heavy equipment and dignity of machine-related work.

Scripture
Proverbs 24:3 “Through wisdom is an house builded; and by understanding it is established.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify heavy equipment through pictures, videos or supervised site observation.
Day 2: List heavy machines used in construction, road work and agriculture.
Day 3: Match each machine with its major use.
Day 4: Discuss how heavy equipment helps communities develop.
Day 5: Write a reflection on why machine work requires wisdom and understanding.

Character
Heavy equipment is powerful. It must be handled with wisdom, not excitement or pride.

Week 2. Heavy Equipment Site Safety

Teaching focus
Machine hazards, blind spots, moving equipment, reversing danger, protective equipment, safe distance and obedience to site rules.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:3 “A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify common machine hazards.
Day 2: Demonstrate correct use of boots, helmets, gloves and reflective jackets.
Day 3: Mark machine danger zones on a drawing.
Day 4: Practise safe movement around parked equipment under supervision.
Day 5: Complete a heavy equipment safety checklist.

Character
Safety is wisdom. A trainee who ignores machine danger can endanger many lives.

Week 3. Personal Protective Equipment and Site Conduct

Teaching focus
Protective clothing, reflective visibility, hearing awareness, dust protection, discipline, punctuality and professional conduct.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 14:40 “Let all things be done decently and in order.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify personal protective equipment used around machines.
Day 2: Practise wearing protective equipment correctly.
Day 3: Discuss unsafe dressing around machines.
Day 4: Prepare a PPE inspection checklist.
Day 5: Conduct a supervised PPE check.

Character
Orderliness is part of safety. A properly dressed trainee is prepared for work.

Week 4. Machine Types and Basic Functions

Teaching focus
Excavator, bulldozer, grader, wheel loader, backhoe loader, roller, crane, forklift, tipper and tractor awareness.

Scripture
Proverbs 4:7 “Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify excavators, bulldozers and graders.
Day 2: Identify wheel loaders, backhoe loaders and rollers.
Day 3: Identify cranes, forklifts and tippers at awareness level.
Day 4: Match machines with tasks such as digging, loading, grading, lifting and compacting.
Day 5: Prepare a machine identification chart.

Character
Understanding comes before responsibility. Trainees must know the purpose of a machine before working near it.

modules.content:
Module 2 of 7. Machine Inspection, Controls Awareness and Communication

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 5. Walk-Around Inspection Awareness

Teaching focus
Meaning of walk-around inspection, checking tyres, tracks, leaks, damage, mirrors, lights, horn and general machine condition.

Scripture
Proverbs 27:23 “Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, and look well to thy herds.”

Practice

Day 2: Identify tyres, tracks, mirrors, lights and steps.
Day 3: Identify visible leaks, loose parts or damage from pictures or supervised examples.
Day 4: Prepare a walk-around inspection checklist.
Day 5: Practise reporting a fault clearly.

Character
Responsible people inspect what is entrusted to them. A small fault ignored can become a serious accident.

Week 6. Fluids, Fuel and Daily Machine Checks

Teaching focus
Fuel, engine oil, hydraulic oil, coolant, grease points at awareness level, battery awareness and reporting low levels.

Scripture
Luke 16:10 “He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify fuel tank, oil dipstick area and coolant area at awareness level.
Day 2: Discuss why machines need fluids.
Day 3: Demonstrate safe checking awareness without unauthorised opening or tampering.
Day 4: Prepare a daily machine check form.
Day 5: Record sample fuel and fluid observations.

Character
Small checks protect big machines. Faithfulness in daily inspection prevents costly damage.

Week 7. Operator Controls and Seat Discipline Awareness

Teaching focus
Operator’s seat, controls awareness, pedals, levers, steering, mirrors, seat belt, start-up and shutdown awareness.

Scripture
Proverbs 19:20 “Hear counsel, and receive instruction, that thou mayest be wise in thy latter end.”

Practice
Day 1: Observe controls from outside or on a parked machine under strict supervision.
Day 2: Identify the operator’s seat and seat belt.
Day 3: Discuss why unauthorised persons must not touch controls.
Day 4: Practise naming controls from diagrams.
Day 5: Write five rules for operator seat discipline.

Character
A wise trainee listens to instruction. Touching controls without permission is dangerous and disobedient.

Week 8. Hand Signals, Banksman and Site Communication

Teaching focus
Role of banksman, hand signals, eye contact, whistle awareness, radio communication awareness and avoiding confusion.

Scripture
Ephesians 4:25 “Wherefore putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss the role of a banksman or signal person.
Day 2: Demonstrate basic hand signals using a safe non-machine exercise.
Day 3: Practise stop, move forward, reverse, slow down and emergency stop signals.
Day 4: Role-play operator and banksman communication without machine movement.
Day 5: Prepare a communication safety checklist.

Character
Clear communication protects lives. Confusion near heavy machines can cause accidents.

Week 9. Earthmoving Principles

Character
Preparation comes before building. Poor ground preparation can damage the whole project.

Week 10. Excavation and Trench Safety Awareness

Teaching focus
Excavation, trench collapse, safe distance, machine swing radius, spoil placement and reporting unsafe trenches.

Scripture
Psalm 11:3 “If the foundations be destroyed, what can the righteous do?”

Practice

Day 2: Mark safe distance from a simulated trench.
Day 3: Identify unsafe spoil placement from pictures or diagrams.
Day 4: Prepare an excavation safety checklist.
Day 5: Write a hazard report for a simulated unsafe trench.

Character
Foundations and excavations must be handled carefully. Hidden weakness can cause visible disaster.

Week 11. Loading, Hauling and Dumping Awareness

Teaching focus
Wheel loaders, excavators, tippers, loading zones, dumping zones, safe reversing, load balance and traffic control.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 14:40 “Let all things be done decently and in order.”

Practice
Day 1: Draw a simple loading and dumping site layout.
Day 2: Identify safe and unsafe loading positions.
Day 3: Discuss tipper reversing safety.
Day 4: Role-play banksman guidance without machine movement.
Day 5: Prepare a loading and hauling safety checklist.

Character
Order prevents accidents. Loading and dumping must follow clear instructions and safe movement.

Week 12. Compaction and Roller Awareness

Teaching focus
Meaning of compaction, road layers, soil moisture awareness, roller safety, vibration awareness and compaction records.

Scripture
James 1:4 “But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.”

Practice
Day 1: Compare loose soil and compacted soil.
Day 2: Discuss how rollers compact road layers.
Day 3: Observe compaction videos, pictures or supervised demonstration where available.
Day 4: Prepare a compaction observation checklist.
Day 5: Record why compaction must be done layer by layer.

Character
Strength comes through process. Just as soil must be compacted properly, character must be formed through discipline.

modules.title: Site Operations, Productivity and Machine Care
modules.content:
Module 5 of 7. Site Operations, Productivity and Machine Care

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 17. Machine Movement and Traffic Management

Teaching focus
Site traffic routes, reversing areas, pedestrian exclusion, speed control, signs, cones and flagging awareness.

Scripture
Romans 12:18 “If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.”

Practice
Day 1: Draw a simple site traffic plan.
Day 2: Mark pedestrian and machine movement areas on a practice layout.
Day 3: Identify unsafe movement routes.
Day 4: Role-play traffic control and site communication.
Day 5: Prepare a machine traffic safety checklist.

Character
Good traffic control protects peace, safety and order on the site.

Week 18. Fuel Discipline and Waste Reduction

Teaching focus
Fuel use, idle time, fuel theft prevention, fuel records, economic operation awareness and stewardship.

Scripture
John 6:12 “When they were filled, he said unto his disciples, Gather up the fragments that remain, that nothing be lost.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss how fuel is wasted on machine sites.
Day 2: Prepare a simple fuel record sheet.
Day 3: Record sample fuel issued and used.
Day 4: Discuss the danger of fuel theft and false records.
Day 5: Prepare a fuel stewardship checklist.

Character
Waste is poor stewardship. Fuel must be recorded honestly and used responsibly.

Week 19. Daily Machine Cleaning and Operator Care

Teaching focus
Cleaning cabins, steps, mirrors, windows, tracks, tyres, lights, radiator area awareness and reporting damage.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 4:2 “Moreover it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss why machines must be cleaned.
Day 2: Identify areas to clean on a parked machine or diagram.
Day 3: Prepare a machine cleaning checklist.
Day 4: Practise safe cleaning of tools or machine parts under supervision where available.
Day 5: Record cleaning and care lessons.

Character
A faithful steward cares for equipment before, during and after work.

Week 20. Productivity, Work Planning and Operator Support

Teaching focus
Daily work targets, machine allocation, task sequence, idle time reduction, operator assistant duties and supervisor reporting.

Scripture
Proverbs 21:5 “The thoughts of the diligent tend only to plenteousness; but of every one that is hasty only to want.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare a simple machine work plan.
Day 2: List tasks in proper sequence.
Day 3: Identify causes of machine idle time.
Day 4: Prepare a simple operator support checklist.
Day 5: Write a daily machine work report.

Character
Diligent planning improves productivity. Hasty work creates waste, delay and danger.

modules.title: Records, Maintenance Coordination, Costing and Enterprise
modules.content:
Module 6 of 7. Records, Maintenance Coordination, Costing and Enterprise

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 21. Machine Logbooks and Daily Reports

Teaching focus
Machine hours, task performed, operator name, fuel used, faults reported, maintenance notes and daily summary.

Scripture
Habakkuk 2:2 “And the LORD answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.”

Practice
Day 1: Create a simple machine logbook template.
Day 2: Record sample machine hours.
Day 3: Record sample fuel use.
Day 4: Record sample faults and supervisor comments.
Day 5: Review logbooks for accuracy and neatness.

Character
Clear records help supervisors make decisions. Honest records protect equipment and people.

Week 22. Maintenance Coordination Awareness

Teaching focus
Operator maintenance, mechanic roles, fault reporting, service schedule awareness, lubrication awareness and downtime prevention.

Scripture
Proverbs 27:23 “Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, and look well to thy herds.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss the difference between operator checks and mechanic repairs.
Day 2: Identify common faults that must be reported.
Day 3: Prepare a fault report form.
Day 4: Discuss why delayed maintenance causes breakdown.
Day 5: Prepare a basic maintenance coordination checklist.

Character
Diligent observation protects machines. A responsible trainee reports faults early.

Week 23. Equipment Costing and Hire Awareness

Teaching focus
Machine hire, hourly rates awareness, fuel cost, operator cost, maintenance cost, transport cost and downtime.

Scripture
Luke 14:28 “For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost?”

Practice
Day 1: List cost items in machine operation.
Day 2: Prepare a simple sample machine hire cost sheet.
Day 3: Discuss how breakdown affects cost.
Day 4: Discuss how idle time wastes money.
Day 5: Prepare a simple equipment costing reflection.

Character
Wise people count the cost. Heavy equipment work is expensive and must be managed carefully.

Week 24. Heavy Equipment Enterprise Opportunities

Teaching focus
Equipment support services, machine hire awareness, operator assistant roles, equipment yard support, fuel records, safety support and ethical enterprise.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:1 “A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold.”

Practice
Day 1: List enterprise opportunities linked to heavy equipment.
Day 2: Identify customers for one machine-related service.
Day 3: Prepare a simple service description.
Day 4: Role-play customer or contractor communication.
Day 5: Prepare a simple heavy equipment enterprise idea note.

Character
A good name is valuable. Machine-related enterprise must be built on safety, honesty and reliability.

modules.title: Advanced Practice, Departmental Project and Attachment Preparation
modules.content:
Module 7 of 7. Advanced Practice, Departmental Project and Attachment Preparation

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 25. Departmental Mini-Project Planning

Teaching focus
Planning a safe heavy equipment support project, roles, tools, records, safety controls and expected results.

Scripture
Nehemiah 2:18 “Then I told them of the hand of my God which was good upon me; as also the king’s words that he had spoken unto me. And they said, Let us rise up and build.”

Practice
Day 1: Choose a safe departmental mini-project.
Day 2: Write project goals and expected results.
Day 3: Prepare tools, records and safety checklist.
Day 4: Assign team roles and reporting duties.
Day 5: Submit project plan for trainer approval.

Character
Vision must become organised action. Trainees must rise and build responsibly.

Week 26. Departmental Mini-Project Implementation

Teaching focus
Carrying out a supervised heavy equipment support project with safety, teamwork, records and quality checks.

Scripture
Nehemiah 4:6 “So built we the wall; and all the wall was joined together unto the half thereof: for the people had a mind to work.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare project area and safety signs.
Day 2: Begin inspection, logbook or traffic layout task under supervision.
Day 3: Continue assigned tasks and record progress.
Day 4: Check safety, records and teamwork.
Day 5: Clean the area and review progress.

Character
Progress comes when people have a mind to work and are willing to cooperate.

Week 27. Final Practical Demonstration and Portfolio

Teaching focus
Demonstrating machine identification, safety checks, hand signals, logbooks, fault reports and attachment readiness.

Scripture
2 Timothy 2:15 “Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed.”

Practice
Day 1: Demonstrate machine identification.
Day 2: Demonstrate walk-around inspection awareness.
Day 3: Demonstrate hand signals and banksman communication through role-play.
Day 4: Organise heavy equipment operations portfolio.
Day 5: Present practical evidence to trainer.

Character
A trained worker should not be ashamed. Diligence, skill and discipline prepare trainees for approval.

Week 28. Industrial Attachment Preparation

Teaching focus
Preparing for heavy equipment placement, supervisor conduct, site safety, machine logbooks, daily reports and final readiness.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:29 “Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify possible heavy equipment attachment placements.
Day 2: Prepare personal attachment learning goals.
Day 3: Practise writing daily heavy equipment attachment logs.
Day 4: Review machine safety and workplace behaviour.
Day 5: Complete final departmental readiness assessment.

Character
Diligence opens doors. A faithful trainee can be trusted with greater responsibility.

modules.title: Hospitality Orientation, Service Mindset and Personal Presentation
modules.content:
Module 1 of 7. Hospitality Orientation, Service Mindset and Personal Presentation

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 1. Introduction to Hospitality Management

Teaching focus
Meaning of hospitality, importance of guest care, hospitality as service, types of hospitality organisations and dignity of service work.

Scripture
Hebrews 13:2 “Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss the meaning of hospitality.
Day 2: Identify hospitality places in the community, such as hotels, guest houses, restaurants and event centres.
Day 3: Discuss what makes a guest feel welcome.
Day 4: List poor hospitality behaviours that offend guests.
Day 5: Write a reflection on why guests must be treated with honour.

Character
Every guest should be treated with respect because hospitality is sacred.

Week 2. Service Mindset and Kingdom Hospitality

Teaching focus
Serving willingly, avoiding complaint, humility, kindness, patience and seeing service as honourable.

Scripture
1 Peter 4:9 “Use hospitality one to another without grudging.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss the difference between forced service and willing service.
Day 2: Role-play serving a guest with joy.
Day 3: Discuss common complaints in service work and how to avoid them.
Day 4: Prepare a hospitality attitude checklist.
Day 5: Write a personal service commitment.

Character
Hospitality must be given without grumbling. The attitude of the worker affects the experience of the guest.

Week 3. Personal Grooming and Professional Appearance

Teaching focus
Clean clothing, neat hair, body hygiene, fresh breath, appropriate dressing, name tags, posture and appearance standards.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 14:40 “Let all things be done decently and in order.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss why appearance matters in hospitality.
Day 2: Demonstrate proper grooming standards.
Day 3: Practise professional posture and walking.
Day 4: Prepare a personal grooming checklist.
Day 5: Conduct a supervised appearance review.

Character
Orderliness should be seen in personal appearance, speech and conduct.

Week 4. Courtesy, Respect and Communication

Teaching focus
Greeting, politeness, tone of voice, eye contact, listening, respectful words and avoiding rude responses.

Scripture
Colossians 4:6 “Let your speech be alway with grace, seasoned with salt, that ye may know how ye ought to answer every man.”

Practice
Day 1: Practise greeting guests politely.
Day 2: Practise answering simple enquiries.
Day 3: Role-play giving directions.
Day 4: Practise apologising respectfully.
Day 5: Prepare a courteous speech guide.

Character
Words can welcome or wound. Hospitality workers must speak with grace.

Module 2 of 7. Customer Service, Reception and Front Desk Basics

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 5. Customer Service Foundation

Teaching focus
Guest needs, service standards, first impressions, listening, patience and service recovery.

Scripture
Matthew 7:12 “Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss how trainees would like to be treated as guests.
Day 2: List common guest needs.
Day 3: Role-play welcoming a tired guest.
Day 4: Discuss poor customer service examples.
Day 5: Prepare a customer service checklist.

Character
Treat guests the way you would want to be treated.

Week 6. Reception and Front Desk Duties

Teaching focus
Reception area, guest welcome, enquiries, messages, bookings, check-in awareness, check-out awareness and neat records.

Scripture
Habakkuk 2:2 “And the LORD answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify reception tools and documents.
Day 2: Practise welcoming a guest at reception.
Day 3: Fill a sample guest enquiry form.
Day 4: Record a sample booking.
Day 5: Practise giving a guest simple information.

Character
Clear records help staff serve guests properly and avoid confusion.

Week 7. Telephone Etiquette and Message Taking

Teaching focus
Answering calls, polite language, clear speaking, taking messages, confirming details and confidentiality.

Scripture
Proverbs 15:1 “A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.”

Practice
Day 1: Practise answering a phone call professionally.
Day 2: Practise taking a guest message.
Day 3: Practise confirming names, phone numbers and requests.
Day 4: Role-play handling an impatient caller.
Day 5: Prepare a telephone etiquette checklist.

Character
A soft and respectful answer can calm tension and protect the reputation of the organisation.

Week 8. Handling Complaints and Difficult Guests

Teaching focus
Listening, staying calm, apologising, reporting problems, avoiding arguments and service recovery.

Scripture
James 1:19 “Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss common guest complaints.
Day 2: Practise listening without interrupting.
Day 3: Role-play apologising to a dissatisfied guest.
Day 4: Practise reporting a complaint to a supervisor.
Day 5: Write a complaint handling report.

Character
Hospitality workers must be slow to anger and quick to listen.

Week 9. Introduction to Housekeeping

Teaching focus
Meaning of housekeeping, room care, cleanliness, guest comfort, room inspection and service standards.

Scripture
Colossians 3:23 “And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify housekeeping tools and supplies.
Day 2: Discuss why clean rooms matter.
Day 3: Prepare a room cleaning checklist.
Day 4: Inspect a sample room for cleanliness.
Day 5: Write a reflection on excellence in hidden service.

Character
Housekeeping may be hidden, but God sees the quality of the work.

Week 10. Bed Making and Room Arrangement

Teaching focus
Bed making, linen handling, pillow arrangement, room layout, guest supplies and neat presentation.

Scripture
Proverbs 31:27 “She looketh well to the ways of her household, and eateth not the bread of idleness.”

Practice
Day 1: Observe bed-making demonstration.
Day 2: Practise spreading sheets neatly.
Day 3: Practise pillow and blanket arrangement.
Day 4: Arrange guest supplies neatly.
Day 5: Conduct room presentation review.

Character
A diligent person pays attention to the condition of the household or room entrusted to him or her.

Week 11. Bathroom, Toilet and Hygiene Standards

Teaching focus
Cleaning toilets, sinks, bathrooms, odour control, disinfectants, gloves, handwashing and guest safety.

Scripture
Psalm 51:10 “Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify bathroom cleaning tools and chemicals.
Day 2: Demonstrate safe use of gloves and cleaning materials.
Day 3: Practise cleaning sequence using a training area.
Day 4: Prepare a toilet hygiene checklist.
Day 5: Discuss the link between cleanliness and dignity.

Character
External cleanliness should remind trainees of the need for a clean heart and right spirit.

Week 12. Laundry, Linen and Lost Property Awareness

Teaching focus
Sorting linen, laundry awareness, towel care, damaged linen reporting, lost and found records and guest property care.

Scripture
Luke 16:10 “He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much.”

Practice
Day 1: Sort sample linen and towels.
Day 2: Identify clean, dirty and damaged linen.
Day 3: Fold towels and linen neatly.
Day 4: Complete a lost and found record.
Day 5: Prepare a linen control checklist.

Character
Faithfulness is shown in how trainees handle small items and guest property.

Matthew 25:35 “For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in.”

Day 1: Discuss the importance of feeding guests well.
Day 2: Identify plates, cups, cutlery and serving trays.
Day 3: Practise carrying a tray safely.
Day 4: Role-play serving water politely.
Day 5: Prepare a food service checklist.

Serving food and drink is a meaningful act of care.

Handwashing, clean uniforms, food contamination, safe serving, covered food, clean utensils and illness reporting.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 10:31 “Whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God.”

Day 1: Demonstrate proper handwashing.
Day 2: Identify food contamination risks.
Day 3: Practise safe handling of plates and cups.
Day 4: Prepare a food hygiene checklist.
Day 5: Discuss why food service must honour God and protect health.

Food service must be clean, careful and honourable.

Table arrangement, cutlery placement, napkins, serving sequence, clearing tables and dining area neatness.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 14:40 “Let all things be done decently and in order.”

Day 2: Practise simple table setting.
Day 3: Practise arranging chairs and tables neatly.
Day 4: Practise clearing plates respectfully.
Day 5: Conduct a table setting assessment.

Order brings beauty and comfort to service.

Week 16. Kitchen Support and Stewarding Awareness

Dishwashing, cleaning utensils, waste management, kitchen safety, hot surfaces, knives awareness and teamwork.

Scripture
Ecclesiastes 4:9 “Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.”

Practice

Day 2: Practise safe dishwashing sequence.
Day 3: Sort waste properly.
Day 4: Discuss hot surface and knife safety.
Day 5: Prepare a kitchen support checklist.

Hospitality succeeds through teamwork between service staff, kitchen staff and cleaners.

Week 17. Introduction to Event Support

Teaching focus

Scripture
Proverbs 24:27 “Prepare thy work without, and make it fit for thyself in the field; and afterwards build thine house.”

Practice
Day 1: List types of events that need hospitality support.
Day 2: Prepare an event support checklist.
Day 3: Arrange chairs for a sample meeting.
Day 4: Prepare registration table setup.
Day 5: Discuss why preparation is important before guests arrive.

Character
Good service begins before guests arrive.

Week 18. Registration, Ushering and Guest Flow

Teaching focus
Welcoming event guests, registration records, badges, seating guidance, crowd flow and respectful direction.

Scripture
Romans 12:10 “Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another.”

Practice
Day 1: Practise welcoming event guests.
Day 2: Fill a sample event attendance register.
Day 3: Practise guiding guests to seats.
Day 4: Role-play helping elderly guests.
Day 5: Prepare an ushering and registration checklist.

Character
Hospitality honours people by making them feel seen, welcomed and helped.

Week 19. Facility Care and Maintenance Reporting

Teaching focus
Facility inspection, broken furniture, faulty lights, leaking taps, blocked toilets, damaged doors and maintenance records.

Scripture
Proverbs 27:23 “Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, and look well to thy herds.”

Practice
Day 1: Inspect a room or hall for maintenance issues.
Day 2: Identify damaged furniture or fittings.
Day 3: Prepare a maintenance report.
Day 4: Prioritise urgent and non-urgent issues.
Day 5: Present facility inspection findings.

Responsible workers observe what is entrusted to them and report problems early.

Week 20. Guest Feedback and Service Improvement

Guest feedback, service review, complaint trends, improvement plans and maintaining standards.

Scripture
Proverbs 19:20 “Hear counsel, and receive instruction, that thou mayest be wise in thy latter end.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss why feedback matters.
Day 2: Prepare a simple guest feedback form.
Day 3: Review sample feedback.
Day 4: Identify areas for service improvement.
Day 5: Prepare a service improvement plan.

Character
Wise hospitality workers accept correction and improve.

Week 25. Departmental Mini-Project Planning

Teaching focus
Planning a hospitality project, team roles, guest needs, supplies, budget, records, safety and expected outcomes.

Scripture
Nehemiah 2:18 “Then I told them of the hand of my God which was good upon me; as also the king’s words that he had spoken unto me. And they said, Let us rise up and build.”

Practice
Day 1: Choose a safe departmental hospitality mini-project.
Day 2: Prepare project goals and expected results.
Day 3: Prepare supplies, checklist and budget.
Day 4: Assign team roles and service duties.
Day 5: Submit project plan for trainer approval.

Character
Vision must become organised action. Hospitality work must be planned and delivered with excellence.

Week 26. Departmental Mini-Project Implementation

Teaching focus
Carrying out a supervised hospitality project with guest care, cleanliness, teamwork, records and service review.

Scripture
Nehemiah 4:6 “So built we the wall; and all the wall was joined together unto the half thereof: for the people had a mind to work.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare the service area, tools and records.
Day 2: Begin room setup, reception or event support task.
Day 3: Continue assigned service duties and record progress.
Day 4: Check cleanliness, guest care, records and teamwork.
Day 5: Clean the area and review project performance.

Character
Progress comes when people have a mind to work and cooperate with discipline.

Week 27. Final Practical Demonstration and Portfolio

Teaching focus
Demonstrating guest welcome, reception records, housekeeping, table setting, complaint handling and portfolio evidence.

Scripture
2 Timothy 2:15 “Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed.”

Practice
Day 1: Demonstrate guest greeting and reception.
Day 2: Demonstrate room cleaning checklist and bed-making awareness.
Day 3: Demonstrate table setting and customer service role-play.
Day 4: Organise hospitality management portfolio.
Day 5: Present practical evidence to the trainer.

Character
A trained worker should not be ashamed. Diligence, skill and discipline prepare trainees for approval.

Week 28. Industrial Attachment Preparation

Teaching focus
Preparing for hospitality placement, supervisor conduct, guest privacy, service standards, daily logs and final readiness.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:29 “Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify possible hospitality attachment placements.
Day 2: Prepare personal attachment learning goals.
Day 3: Practise writing daily hospitality attachment logs.
Day 4: Review guest care, confidentiality and workplace behaviour.
Day 5: Complete final departmental readiness assessment.

Character
Diligence opens doors. A faithful hospitality trainee can serve in important places.

modules.title: Workshop Orientation, Safety and Tools
modules.content:
Module 1 of 7. Workshop Orientation, Safety and Tools

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 1. Introduction to Motor Vehicle Mechanics

Teaching focus
Meaning of motor vehicle mechanics, importance of vehicle maintenance, types of vehicles, role of mechanics and dignity of technical work.

Scripture
Colossians 3:23 “And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.”

Practice
Day 1: Walk around the workshop and identify work areas.
Day 2: List different types of vehicles seen in the community.
Day 3: Discuss why vehicles need regular maintenance.
Day 4: Identify common problems caused by poor maintenance.
Day 5: Write a reflection on why mechanic work must be done with seriousness.

Character
Mechanic work should be done heartily and responsibly because people’s lives may depend on vehicle safety.

Week 2. Workshop Safety and Personal Protective Equipment

Teaching focus
Workshop hazards, protective clothing, hot engines, sharp tools, moving parts, fire hazards, battery hazards and safe conduct.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:3 “A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify workshop hazards such as oil spills, hot parts, sharp tools and moving belts.
Day 2: Demonstrate correct use of gloves, boots, overalls and eye protection where available.
Day 3: Practise safe movement around a workshop.
Day 4: Prepare a workshop safety checklist.
Day 5: Conduct a supervised workshop safety inspection.

Character
Safety is wisdom. A trainee who ignores danger can injure himself, herself or others.

Week 3. Mechanic Tools and Their Uses

Teaching focus
Spanners, sockets, ratchets, screwdrivers, pliers, hammers, jacks, stands, oil filter wrench, tyre gauge and tool care.

Scripture
Luke 16:10 “He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify basic mechanic tools and state their uses.
Day 2: Practise selecting the right spanner or socket for a bolt.
Day 3: Practise safe use of screwdrivers and pliers.
Day 4: Clean and arrange tools after use.
Day 5: Complete a tool issue and return register.

Character
Tool care is a test of faithfulness. A careless trainee cannot be trusted with customer vehicles.

Week 4. Workshop Cleanliness, Tool Storage and Customer Property Care

Teaching focus
Clean workshop habits, oil spill control, tool organisation, waste disposal, parts arrangement and customer vehicle protection.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 14:40 “Let all things be done decently and in order.”

Practice
Day 1: Clean and arrange a workshop practice area.
Day 2: Demonstrate safe disposal of oily rags and waste materials.
Day 3: Arrange tools and parts in proper order.
Day 4: Discuss how to protect customer vehicles from scratches, dirt and missing parts.
Day 5: Prepare a workshop cleanliness checklist.

Character
Orderliness improves safety, speed, quality and customer trust.

Module 2 of 7. Vehicle Systems, Engine Bay and Basic Inspection

Week 5. Vehicle Parts and Engine Bay Orientation

Teaching focus
Vehicle body parts, engine bay, bonnet safety, radiator, battery, belts, hoses, dipstick and fluid reservoirs.

Scripture
Proverbs 4:7 “Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify external vehicle parts such as bonnet, doors, tyres, lights and mirrors.
Day 2: Open the bonnet safely under supervision.
Day 3: Identify battery, radiator, dipstick, belts and hoses.
Day 4: Draw and label a simple engine bay diagram.
Day 5: Explain why understanding comes before repair.

Character
A trainee must first understand before attempting to fix. Ignorance can damage vehicles.

Week 6. Engine Basics and Lubrication System Awareness

Teaching focus
Basic engine function, oil purpose, dipstick reading, oil leaks, oil filter awareness and why lubrication matters.

Scripture
Proverbs 27:23 “Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, and look well to thy herds.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss what an engine does.
Day 2: Identify dipstick and oil filler cap under supervision.
Day 3: Practise checking oil level on a safe vehicle or demonstration engine.
Day 4: Identify signs of oil leaks.
Day 5: Record oil inspection findings in a service checklist.

Character
A responsible mechanic checks carefully. Neglecting oil can destroy an engine.

Week 7. Cooling System Awareness

Teaching focus
Radiator, coolant, hoses, fan, overheating, coolant leaks, safe checking and danger of opening hot radiator caps.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:3 “A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify radiator, coolant reservoir and hoses.
Day 2: Discuss causes of overheating.
Day 3: Demonstrate safe coolant level checking only when the engine is cool.
Day 4: Identify hose cracks and coolant leaks from examples.
Day 5: Prepare an overheating observation report.

Character
A wise trainee respects heat and pressure. Never open a hot radiator cap.

Week 8. Basic Vehicle Inspection Checklist

Teaching focus
Visual inspection, oil, coolant, battery, tyres, lights, wipers, horn, leaks and basic reporting.

Scripture
2 Corinthians 13:5 “Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare a simple vehicle inspection checklist.
Day 2: Inspect tyres and lights under supervision.
Day 3: Inspect oil, coolant and battery area under supervision.
Day 4: Record faults found.
Day 5: Present inspection findings to the trainer.

Character
Inspection helps reveal problems before they become serious. Good workers examine carefully.
