modules.title: Electrical, Battery, Fuel and Ignition Awareness
modules.content:
Module 3 of 7. Electrical, Battery, Fuel and Ignition Awareness

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 9. Battery Safety and Battery Maintenance Awareness

Teaching focus
Battery function, terminals, corrosion, safe handling, acid danger, short circuits, jump-start awareness and reporting faults.

Scripture
Proverbs 19:20 “Hear counsel, and receive instruction, that thou mayest be wise in thy latter end.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify vehicle battery and terminals.
Day 2: Discuss battery dangers and safety rules.
Day 3: Observe battery terminal cleaning demonstration under supervision.
Day 4: Identify corrosion and loose terminals.
Day 5: Prepare a battery safety checklist.

Character
Instruction protects life. A trainee must never handle batteries carelessly.

Week 10. Basic Vehicle Electrical Awareness

Teaching focus
Lights, horn, fuses, wiring awareness, alternator awareness, starter awareness and electrical safety.

Scripture
Psalm 119:105 “Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify headlights, brake lights, indicators and reverse lights.
Day 2: Test lights under supervision.
Day 3: Discuss fuses and wiring at awareness level.
Day 4: Identify damaged wires from examples.
Day 5: Record electrical faults in a service report.

Character
Light gives direction. Vehicle lights are safety tools and must not be ignored.

Week 11. Fuel System and Fire Safety Awareness

Teaching focus
Fuel tank, fuel lines, fuel filter awareness, petrol and diesel difference at basic level, leaks, fire prevention and safe storage.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:3 “A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss fuel system basics.
Day 2: Identify fuel tank area and fuel lines at awareness level.
Day 3: Discuss the danger of smoking near fuel.
Day 4: Identify fuel leaks from pictures or supervised examples.
Day 5: Prepare a fuel fire safety checklist.

Character
Fuel must be handled with caution. Fire safety is not optional.

Week 12. Ignition, Starting System and Fault Observation

Teaching focus
Spark plug awareness, starter motor awareness, ignition switch, weak battery signs, no-start complaints and symptom recording.

Scripture
Habakkuk 2:2 “And the LORD answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss common reasons a vehicle may not start.
Day 2: Identify spark plug at awareness level where applicable.
Day 3: Discuss starter sound and weak battery signs.
Day 4: Practise asking customer questions about starting problems.
Day 5: Write a no-start symptom report.

Character
Clear records help diagnosis. A good trainee writes symptoms properly before guessing.

modules.title: Tyres, Brakes, Steering, Suspension and Transmission Awareness
modules.content:
Module 4 of 7. Tyres, Brakes, Steering, Suspension and Transmission Awareness

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 13. Tyres, Wheels and Wheel Safety

Teaching focus
Tyre pressure, tyre wear, wheel nuts, spare tyre, jack awareness, punctures and safe lifting rules.

Scripture
Proverbs 4:26 “Ponder the path of thy feet, and let all thy ways be established.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify tyre size marking at awareness level.
Day 2: Check tyre condition and wear.
Day 3: Check tyre pressure awareness where equipment is available.
Day 4: Demonstrate safe wheel nut loosening and tightening awareness.
Day 5: Discuss why tyres affect safe movement.

Character
The path of a vehicle depends greatly on tyres. Small neglect can cause serious accidents.

Week 14. Brake System Awareness

Teaching focus
Brake pedal, brake fluid awareness, brake pads, brake shoes, brake warning signs and danger of brake failure.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:3 “A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss the purpose of brakes.
Day 2: Identify brake fluid reservoir at awareness level.
Day 3: Identify brake pads or shoes from samples where available.
Day 4: Discuss signs of poor brakes.
Day 5: Prepare a brake safety observation report.

Character
A wise mechanic does not ignore brake problems. Brake faults can cost lives.

Week 15. Steering and Suspension Awareness

Teaching focus
Steering wheel, tie rods awareness, shock absorbers, springs, ball joints awareness, wheel alignment awareness and road handling.

Scripture
Proverbs 3:6 “In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss how steering helps direct a vehicle.
Day 2: Identify basic steering and suspension parts from pictures or samples.
Day 3: Observe signs of worn suspension.
Day 4: Discuss pulling to one side and vibration symptoms.
Day 5: Record steering and suspension observations.

Character
Direction matters in vehicles and in life. A person must allow God to direct his or her path.

Week 16. Transmission, Clutch and Drivetrain Awareness

Teaching focus
Manual and automatic transmission awareness, clutch awareness, gear selection, driveshaft awareness and safe driving habits.

Scripture
Ecclesiastes 3:1 “To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss the purpose of transmission.
Day 2: Identify gear lever and clutch pedal where applicable.
Day 3: Discuss wrong gear use and vehicle stress.
Day 4: Identify drivetrain parts from diagrams.
Day 5: Prepare a transmission awareness note.

Character
Timing and correct selection matter. In mechanics and life, wrong timing can cause damage.

modules.title: Servicing, Maintenance, Diagnosis and Workshop Practice
modules.content:
Module 5 of 7. Servicing, Maintenance, Diagnosis and Workshop Practice

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 17. Basic Vehicle Servicing Awareness

Teaching focus
Service intervals, oil change, filters, fluid checks, tyre checks, lights, belts and customer service records.

Scripture
Proverbs 21:5 “The thoughts of the diligent tend only to plenteousness; but of every one that is hasty only to want.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss why regular servicing is important.
Day 2: Prepare a simple service checklist.
Day 3: Observe oil change demonstration under supervision.
Day 4: Observe air filter inspection or replacement awareness.
Day 5: Complete a sample service record.

Character
Diligent maintenance prevents sudden failure. Hasty neglect leads to loss.

Week 18. Belts, Hoses, Filters and Simple Preventive Maintenance

Teaching focus
Fan belt awareness, serpentine belt awareness, hoses, air filter, fuel filter awareness and preventive maintenance.

Scripture
Song of Solomon 2:15 “Take us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vines: for our vines have tender grapes.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify belts and hoses.
Day 2: Check belts for cracks at awareness level.
Day 3: Check hoses for cracks or swelling at awareness level.
Day 4: Inspect air filter condition.
Day 5: Record small problems that can become big faults.

Character
Small faults can spoil the whole vehicle if ignored. Small bad habits can also spoil a life.

Week 19. Fault Diagnosis Awareness and Customer Questions

Teaching focus
Listening to customer complaints, recording symptoms, observing sounds, smoke, leaks, overheating and poor performance.

Scripture
Proverbs 18:13 “He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him.”

Practice
Day 1: Practise asking customers simple questions.
Day 2: Record symptoms from sample vehicle complaints.
Day 3: Identify smoke colour from pictures or videos.
Day 4: Identify leak types at awareness level.
Day 5: Prepare a fault observation report.

Character
Do not answer before listening. A good mechanic listens, observes and records before concluding.

Week 20. Workshop Job Cards, Service Reports and Quality Checks

Teaching focus
Job cards, inspection reports, parts used, labour tasks, supervisor sign-off, customer communication and quality checks.

Scripture
Ephesians 4:25 “Wherefore putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour.”

Practice
Day 1: Create a simple job card.
Day 2: Record customer complaint and vehicle details.
Day 3: Record inspection findings.
Day 4: Record work done and parts used.
Day 5: Complete a service report and review for truthfulness.

Character
Truthful reporting builds trust. A mechanic must not write false work or hide mistakes.

modules.title: Workshop Management, Costing, Customer Care and Enterprise
modules.content:
Module 6 of 7. Workshop Management, Costing, Customer Care and Enterprise

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 21. Workshop Organisation and Parts Management

Teaching focus
Workshop layout, parts storage, waste control, tool storage, used parts, new parts, labelling and cleanliness.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 14:40 “Let all things be done decently and in order.”

Practice
Day 1: Draw a simple workshop layout.
Day 2: Arrange tools and parts in assigned areas.
Day 3: Separate usable parts, damaged parts and waste.
Day 4: Label sample parts.
Day 5: Conduct a workshop organisation review.

Character
Order saves time, prevents loss and improves customer confidence.

Week 22. Parts, Pricing and Honest Costing

Teaching focus
Parts identification, genuine and fake parts awareness, labour cost, service cost, quotation awareness and honesty.

Scripture
Proverbs 11:1 “A false balance is abomination to the LORD: but a just weight is his delight.”

Practice
Day 1: List common service parts such as oil, filters, plugs and belts.
Day 2: Prepare a simple parts and labour cost sheet.
Day 3: Compare sample part prices.
Day 4: Discuss the danger of fake parts.
Day 5: Prepare an honest service quotation.

Character
A mechanic must not cheat customers. Honest pricing protects reputation.

Week 23. Customer Care and Workshop Communication

Teaching focus
Respectful greeting, listening to customers, explaining faults, managing expectations, avoiding insults and protecting customer trust.

Scripture
Colossians 4:6 “Let your speech be alway with grace, seasoned with salt, that ye may know how ye ought to answer every man.”

Practice
Day 1: Role-play receiving a customer.
Day 2: Practise asking vehicle complaint questions politely.
Day 3: Practise explaining a fault in simple language.
Day 4: Practise explaining delay or parts shortage respectfully.
Day 5: Prepare a customer communication checklist.

Character
Good speech builds trust. A mechanic must speak respectfully to customers and colleagues.

Week 24. Motor Vehicle Mechanics Enterprise Opportunities

Teaching focus
Small vehicle services, mobile checks, oil service support, battery checks, tyre pressure checks, parts sales ethics and workshop enterprise.

Scripture
Deuteronomy 8:18 “But thou shalt remember the LORD thy God: for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth.”

Practice
Day 1: List enterprise opportunities in vehicle maintenance.
Day 2: Identify customers for one vehicle service.
Day 3: Prepare a simple service description.
Day 4: Prepare a small-start budget.
Day 5: Write a motor vehicle mechanics enterprise idea note.

Character
The power to create wealth comes from God. Enterprise must be built on honesty, service and skill.

modules.title: Advanced Practice, Departmental Project and Attachment Preparation
modules.content:
Module 7 of 7. Advanced Practice, Departmental Project and Attachment Preparation

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 25. Departmental Mini-Project Planning

Teaching focus
Planning a safe workshop project, team roles, tools, materials, safety controls, records and expected outcomes.

Scripture
Nehemiah 2:18 “Then I told them of the hand of my God which was good upon me; as also the king’s words that he had spoken unto me. And they said, Let us rise up and build.”

Practice
Day 1: Choose a safe departmental mini-project.
Day 2: Write project goals and expected results.
Day 3: Prepare tools, parts and safety checklist.
Day 4: Assign team roles and reporting duties.
Day 5: Submit project plan for trainer approval.

Character
Vision must become organised action. Trainees must rise and build responsibly.

Week 26. Departmental Mini-Project Implementation

Teaching focus
Carrying out a supervised workshop project with safety, teamwork, records and quality checks.

Scripture
Nehemiah 4:6 “So built we the wall; and all the wall was joined together unto the half thereof: for the people had a mind to work.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare the workshop area and tools.
Day 2: Begin the inspection, service checklist or workshop organisation project.
Day 3: Continue assigned tasks and record progress.
Day 4: Check safety, quality, records and teamwork.
Day 5: Clean the area and review progress.

Character
Progress comes when people have a mind to work and cooperate.

Week 27. Final Practical Demonstration and Portfolio

Teaching focus
Demonstrating tool use, safety checks, vehicle inspection, service records, customer communication and portfolio evidence.

Scripture
2 Timothy 2:15 “Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed.”

Practice
Day 1: Demonstrate tool identification and safe handling.
Day 2: Demonstrate vehicle inspection checklist.
Day 3: Demonstrate oil, coolant, battery and tyre check awareness.
Day 4: Organise motor vehicle mechanics portfolio.
Day 5: Present practical evidence to the trainer.

Character
A trained worker should not be ashamed. Diligence, skill and discipline prepare trainees for approval.

Week 28. Industrial Attachment Preparation

Teaching focus
Preparing for mechanic workshop placement, supervisor conduct, workshop safety, customer care, daily logs and final readiness.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:29 “Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify possible motor vehicle mechanics attachment placements.
Day 2: Prepare personal attachment learning goals.
Day 3: Practise writing daily workshop attachment logs.
Day 4: Review workshop safety and workplace behaviour.
Day 5: Complete final departmental readiness assessment.

Character
Diligence opens doors. A faithful trainee can be trusted with greater responsibility.

modules.title: Foundations of Nation Building, Righteousness and Citizenship
modules.content:
Module 1 of 7. Foundations of Nation Building, Righteousness and Citizenship

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 1. Introduction to Nation Building

Teaching focus
Meaning of nation building, why nations matter, the role of citizens, the role of institutions and the connection between personal character and national development.

Scripture
Proverbs 14:34 “Righteousness exalteth a nation: but sin is a reproach to any people.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss the meaning of nation building.
Day 2: Identify signs of a strong nation and a weak nation.
Day 3: Discuss how personal character affects national development.
Day 4: List ways young people can build their nation.
Day 5: Write a reflection on why righteousness exalts a nation.

Character
A nation is not stronger than the character of its people. Righteous citizens help lift a nation.

Week 2. Citizenship and Civic Responsibility

Teaching focus
Meaning of citizenship, rights and responsibilities, obedience to lawful authority, public conduct and service to the common good.

Scripture
Romans 13:1 “Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss the meaning of citizenship.
Day 2: List rights and responsibilities of citizens.
Day 3: Discuss why lawful authority and order matter.
Day 4: Identify irresponsible citizen behaviours.
Day 5: Prepare a civic responsibility checklist.

Character
Responsible citizens do not only demand rights. They also fulfil duties.

Week 3. Righteousness, Justice and National Greatness

Teaching focus
Righteousness, justice, fairness, truth, compassion and how moral values affect public life.

Scripture
Micah 6:8 “He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss righteousness in personal life.
Day 2: Discuss justice in public life.
Day 3: Identify examples of fairness and unfairness in society.
Day 4: Role-play choosing justice over favouritism.
Day 5: Write a personal justice and mercy pledge.

Character
Nation builders must do justly, love mercy and walk humbly with God.

Week 4. Salt and Light in Society

Teaching focus
Believers as salt and light, influence, example, moral courage, public witness and responsible conduct.

Scripture
Matthew 5:13-14“Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss what it means to be salt in society.
Day 2: Discuss what it means to be light in society.
Day 3: Identify areas where young people can influence positively.
Day 4: Prepare a “Salt and Light” action plan.
Day 5: Present one practical way to shine in the community.

Character
Trainees must not only complain about darkness. They must shine as examples.

modules.title: Patriotism, Unity, Diversity and Peacebuilding
modules.content:
Module 2 of 7. Patriotism, Unity, Diversity and Peacebuilding

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 5. Patriotism and Love for Country

Teaching focus
Meaning of patriotism, responsible love for country, national service, praying for the nation and building hope without denying real problems.

Scripture
Jeremiah 29:7 “And seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives, and pray unto the LORD for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss the meaning of true patriotism.
Day 2: List ways citizens can seek the peace of their nation.
Day 3: Discuss the difference between constructive criticism and destructive speech.
Day 4: Write a prayer point list for the nation.
Day 5: Prepare a personal commitment to serve the nation.

Character
True patriotism is not blind praise. It is responsible love, prayer and service.

Week 6. National Unity and Respect for Diversity

Teaching focus
Unity, ethnic diversity, religious diversity, cultural respect, national identity and avoiding division.

Scripture
Psalm 133:1 “Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss the meaning of unity.
Day 2: Identify different cultures and communities in the nation.
Day 3: Discuss dangers of tribal hatred and religious hatred.
Day 4: Role-play respectful interaction across differences.
Day 5: Prepare a unity pledge.

Character
Unity is good and pleasant. A nation cannot prosper when its people hate one another.

Week 7. Peacebuilding and Conflict Prevention

Teaching focus
Causes of conflict, rumours, provocation, revenge, listening, mediation, reconciliation and peace language.

Scripture
Matthew 5:9 “Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify common causes of conflict in communities.
Day 2: Discuss the role of rumours in violence.
Day 3: Role-play calming a disagreement.
Day 4: Prepare a peacebuilding communication checklist.
Day 5: Write a reflection on being a peacemaker.

Character
Nation builders must be peacemakers, not conflict promoters.

Week 8. Responsible Speech and Social Media Conduct

Teaching focus
Hate speech, fake news, rumours, online insults, responsible sharing, public influence and digital citizenship.

Scripture
Ephesians 4:25 “Wherefore putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss how words can divide a nation.
Day 2: Identify examples of harmful public speech.
Day 3: Review sample social media posts for truth and peace.
Day 4: Prepare a responsible sharing checklist.
Day 5: Write a digital nation-building pledge.

Character
Falsehood and careless speech can damage communities. Nation builders speak truthfully and responsibly.

modules.title: Leadership, Service, Public Ethics and Anti-Corruption
modules.content:
Module 3 of 7. Leadership, Service, Public Ethics and Anti-Corruption

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 9. Leadership as Service

Teaching focus
Servant leadership, responsibility, humility, example, sacrifice and leading for the good of others.

Scripture
Mark 10:45 “For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss leadership as service.
Day 2: Identify differences between selfish leadership and servant leadership.
Day 3: Role-play a leader serving a team.
Day 4: Prepare a servant leadership checklist.
Day 5: Write a leadership service commitment.

Character
Leadership is not for pride or oppression. Leadership is for service.

Week 10. Integrity and Anti-Corruption

Teaching focus
Meaning of corruption, bribery, cheating, false records, theft, favouritism, accountability and personal integrity.

Scripture
Proverbs 11:1 “A false balance is abomination to the LORD: but a just weight is his delight.”

Practice
Day 1: Define corruption in simple terms.
Day 2: Identify common corrupt practices in society.
Day 3: Role-play refusing a bribe.
Day 4: Prepare an anti-corruption pledge.
Day 5: Discuss how small dishonesty grows into national decay.

Character
Corruption begins with the heart. A nation builder must reject dishonest gain.

Week 11. Public Trust and Accountability

Teaching focus
Stewardship, public resources, entrusted responsibility, transparency, reporting and consequences of misuse.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 4:2 “Moreover it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss the meaning of public trust.
Day 2: List resources that belong to the public or community.
Day 3: Discuss how misuse of resources affects people.
Day 4: Prepare a simple accountability report from a sample activity.
Day 5: Write a reflection on faithfulness in stewardship.

Character
A steward does not behave like an owner. Public resources must be protected.

Week 12. Lawfulness, Order and Respect for Institutions

Teaching focus
Rule of law awareness, due process, justice, public institutions, lawful conduct and responsible protest or advocacy awareness.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 14:40 “Let all things be done decently and in order.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss why order is important in society.
Day 2: Identify institutions that help society function.
Day 3: Discuss the danger of lawlessness and mob action.
Day 4: Role-play raising a complaint through proper channels.
Day 5: Prepare a lawful conduct checklist.

Character
Nation builders pursue justice with order, not destruction.

modules.title: Community Development, Volunteerism and Social Responsibility
modules.content:
Module 4 of 7. Community Development, Volunteerism and Social Responsibility

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 13. Understanding Community Development

Teaching focus
Meaning of community development, local needs, local resources, participation, sustainability and community ownership.

Scripture
Nehemiah 2:18 “Then I told them of the hand of my God which was good upon me; as also the king’s words that he had spoken unto me. And they said, Let us rise up and build.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss the meaning of community development.
Day 2: Identify needs in the Academy or local community.
Day 3: Identify local resources that can help solve the problem.
Day 4: Prepare a simple community development idea.
Day 5: Present the idea to the class.

Character
Nation builders do not wait for everything to be done by others. They rise and build.

Week 14. Volunteerism and Service to the Vulnerable

Teaching focus
Meaning of volunteerism, serving without immediate reward, helping vulnerable people, compassion and social responsibility.

Scripture
Galatians 5:13 “For, brethren, ye have been called unto liberty; only use not liberty for an occasion to the flesh, but by love serve one another.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss the meaning of volunteerism.
Day 2: Identify vulnerable groups in society.
Day 3: Plan a simple service activity.
Day 4: Role-play serving with respect and dignity.
Day 5: Write a personal volunteer service pledge.

Character
Freedom should not make people selfish. Love should move trainees to serve others.

Week 15. Environmental Responsibility and Public Cleanliness

Teaching focus
Clean environment, waste management, sanitation, public health, tree planting awareness, drainage and community clean-up.

Scripture
Genesis 2:15 “And the LORD God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss environmental stewardship.
Day 2: Identify environmental problems in the community.
Day 3: Prepare a clean-up or sanitation plan.
Day 4: Conduct a supervised cleanliness inspection.
Day 5: Prepare an environmental responsibility checklist.

Character
God expects people to dress and keep what He has entrusted to them.

Week 16. Education, Mentorship and Youth Development

Teaching focus
Importance of education, mentoring younger people, literacy, skills development, discipline and positive peer influence.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:6 “Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss the importance of education in nation building.
Day 2: Identify younger people who need mentoring.
Day 3: Prepare a simple mentoring plan.
Day 4: Role-play encouraging a younger student.
Day 5: Write a youth development action note.

Character
A nation’s future is shaped by how young people are trained.

modules.title: Productivity, Work, Enterprise and Economic Nation Building
modules.content:
Module 5 of 7. Productivity, Work, Enterprise and Economic Nation Building

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 17. Dignity of Work and National Productivity

Teaching focus
Work ethic, diligence, punctuality, skill, productivity, avoiding idleness and contributing to national growth.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:29 “Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss how work builds a nation.
Day 2: Identify poor work habits that weaken society.
Day 3: Prepare a personal productivity plan.
Day 4: Role-play workplace diligence.
Day 5: Write a reflection on diligence and national development.

Character
Diligent workers help build strong families, businesses, institutions and nations.

Week 18. Entrepreneurship and Local Economic Development

Teaching focus
Enterprise, value creation, local production, small business, honest trade, job creation and community wealth.

Scripture
Deuteronomy 8:18 “But thou shalt remember the LORD thy God: for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss how entrepreneurship builds the nation.
Day 2: Identify local business opportunities.
Day 3: Choose one small enterprise idea.
Day 4: Prepare a simple business impact note.
Day 5: Present how the enterprise can help the community.

Character
Wealth creation should serve God, families and communities.

Week 19. Financial Discipline and Resource Stewardship

Teaching focus
Saving, budgeting, avoiding waste, responsible spending, public resource care and financial integrity.

Scripture
Proverbs 21:20 “There is treasure to be desired and oil in the dwelling of the wise; but a foolish man spendeth it up.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss the link between financial discipline and development.
Day 2: Prepare a simple personal budget.
Day 3: Identify wasteful spending habits.
Day 4: Prepare a resource stewardship checklist.
Day 5: Write a financial discipline commitment.

Character
A person who cannot manage personal resources may struggle to manage public resources.

Week 20. Skills, Innovation and Problem-Solving

Teaching focus
Skills development, creativity, innovation, local solutions, technology awareness, practical problem-solving and continuous learning.

Scripture
Daniel 1:17 “As for these four children, God gave them knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify skills that can build the nation.
Day 2: Discuss problems that need local solutions.
Day 3: Brainstorm practical solutions to one local problem.
Day 4: Prepare an innovation idea note.
Day 5: Present the idea and receive feedback.

Character
Knowledge and skill should be used to solve problems and serve society.

modules.title: Governance Awareness, Advocacy, Public Service and National Vision
modules.content:
Module 6 of 7. Governance Awareness, Advocacy, Public Service and National Vision

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 21. Governance Awareness and Citizen Participation

Teaching focus
Government, public institutions, citizen participation, community meetings, public feedback, responsible advocacy and civic engagement.

Scripture
Proverbs 11:14 “Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss how citizens can participate responsibly.
Day 2: Identify public issues citizens can raise respectfully.
Day 3: Prepare a community feedback note.
Day 4: Role-play a respectful meeting with leaders.
Day 5: Prepare a responsible civic participation checklist.

Character
Good governance improves when citizens give wise counsel and participate responsibly.

Week 22. Responsible Advocacy and Social Change

Teaching focus
Advocacy, raising concerns, peaceful communication, evidence, lawful engagement, respect and avoiding violence.

Scripture
Isaiah 1:17 “Learn to do well; seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss the meaning of advocacy.
Day 2: Identify one social issue that needs attention.
Day 3: Prepare a respectful advocacy message.
Day 4: Discuss why advocacy must avoid violence and falsehood.
Day 5: Present a peaceful advocacy plan.

Character
Nation builders speak for justice with truth, peace and responsibility.

Week 23. Public Service and Responsible Leadership

Teaching focus
Public service, leadership responsibility, fairness, humility, accountability, serving citizens and avoiding abuse of power.

Scripture
Proverbs 29:2 “When the righteous are in authority, the people rejoice: but when the wicked beareth rule, the people mourn.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss why leadership affects national life.
Day 2: Identify qualities of righteous leadership.
Day 3: Role-play fair decision-making.
Day 4: Prepare a responsible leadership checklist.
Day 5: Write a public service leadership reflection.

Character
Leadership is not a licence for oppression. Righteous leadership brings joy to the people.

Week 24. National Vision and Hope for the Future

Teaching focus
National vision, hope, responsibility, generational thinking, long-term development and building beyond oneself.

Scripture
Psalm 33:12 “Blessed is the nation whose God is the LORD; and the people whom he hath chosen for his own inheritance.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss the kind of nation trainees desire to see.
Day 2: Identify values needed for national transformation.
Day 3: Prepare a personal nation-building vision statement.
Day 4: Prepare a group national hope poster.
Day 5: Present a future-focused nation-building speech.

Character
Hope must be joined with responsibility. A blessed nation honours God and practises righteousness.

modules.title: Practical Nation Building Project and Attachment Preparation
modules.content:
Module 7 of 7. Practical Nation Building Project and Attachment Preparation

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 25. Departmental Mini-Project Planning

Teaching focus
Planning a nation-building mini-project, identifying a local problem, setting objectives, assigning roles, preparing resources, managing risks and expected outcomes.

Scripture
Habakkuk 2:2 “And the LORD answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.”

Practice
Day 1: Choose a nation-building mini-project.
Day 2: Write the project vision, goal and objectives.
Day 3: Identify beneficiaries, stakeholders and resources.
Day 4: Prepare a timeline, budget and responsibility chart.
Day 5: Submit the full project plan for trainer approval.

Character
A clear written vision helps people understand and act.

Week 26. Departmental Mini-Project Implementation

Teaching focus
Carrying out a supervised nation-building project with teamwork, communication, peace, accountability and service.

Scripture
Nehemiah 4:6 “So built we the wall; and all the wall was joined together unto the half thereof: for the people had a mind to work.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare tools, materials, team roles and service area.
Day 2: Begin project implementation according to plan.
Day 3: Continue assigned tasks and record progress.
Day 4: Review teamwork, safety, ethics and impact.
Day 5: Prepare a project progress report.

Character
Progress comes when people have a mind to work and cooperate with discipline.

Week 27. Final Report, Reflection and Nation Building Portfolio

Teaching focus
Project completion, impact review, lessons learnt, final report, testimonies, photographs where approved and personal reflection.

Scripture
Ecclesiastes 7:8 “Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof.”

Practice
Day 1: Check whether project objectives were achieved.
Day 2: Gather feedback from beneficiaries or observers.
Day 3: Prepare final activity report.
Day 4: Write lessons learnt and recommendations.
Day 5: Organise nation-building portfolio.

Character
Starting well is important, but finishing well is better.

Week 28. Industrial Attachment and Community Service Preparation

Teaching focus
Preparing for attachment, community service, workplace citizenship, public ethics, daily logs, service conduct and final readiness.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:29 “Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify attachment settings where nation-building values are needed.
Day 2: Prepare personal attachment and community service goals.
Day 3: Practise writing daily nation-building attachment logs.
Day 4: Review ethics, peacebuilding, punctuality and workplace responsibility.
Day 5: Complete final departmental readiness assessment.

Character
Diligence opens doors. A responsible trainee can serve the nation in any workplace.

modules.title: Office Orientation, Conduct and Administrative Discipline
modules.content:
Module 1 of 7. Office Orientation, Conduct and Administrative Discipline

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 1. Introduction to Office Administration

Teaching focus
Meaning of office administration, importance of office work, types of offices, role of administrators and dignity of administrative service.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 14:40 “Let all things be done decently and in order.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss the meaning of office administration.
Day 2: Identify different offices in schools, churches, hospitals, businesses and public institutions.
Day 3: List the duties of an office administrator.
Day 4: Discuss what happens when an office is disorganised.
Day 5: Write a reflection on why order is important in office work.

Character
Administration brings order. A trainee must learn to organise information, people and tasks properly.

Week 2. Professional Office Conduct

Teaching focus
Punctuality, dressing, greeting, respect, sitting posture, speaking politely, obedience to instructions and workplace discipline.

Scripture
Colossians 3:23 “And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.”

Practice
Day 1: Practise professional greeting.
Day 2: Review proper office appearance.
Day 3: Role-play receiving instruction from a supervisor.
Day 4: Discuss common poor office behaviours.
Day 5: Prepare an office conduct checklist.

Character
Office work must be done heartily and respectfully, not casually.

Week 3. Office Tools, Equipment and Workspace Organisation

Teaching focus
Desk, chair, files, folders, stapler, printer, computer, notebook, register, cabinet, stationery and workspace order.

Scripture
Luke 16:10 “He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify common office tools and equipment.
Day 2: Arrange a desk properly.
Day 3: Sort stationery and office supplies.
Day 4: Prepare an office equipment register.
Day 5: Clean and organise a practice office area.

Character
Faithfulness can be seen in how a trainee handles small office tools and resources.

Week 4. Confidentiality and Office Ethics

Teaching focus
Confidential documents, private information, gossip, unauthorised access, trust, honesty and office boundaries.

Scripture
Proverbs 11:13 “A talebearer revealeth secrets: but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss the meaning of confidentiality.
Day 2: Identify examples of confidential information.
Day 3: Role-play refusing to disclose private information.
Day 4: Prepare an office confidentiality pledge.
Day 5: Discuss the damage caused by gossip.

Character
A faithful office worker protects confidential matters and refuses gossip.

Teaching focus
Letters, memos, notices, reports, headings, spacing, alignment, signatures, dates and proofreading.

Scripture
Habakkuk 2:2 “And the LORD answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.”

Day 1: Identify parts of an official letter.
Day 2: Type or write a simple memo.
Day 3: Prepare a simple notice.
Day 4: Proofread a sample document.
Day 5: Submit a clean formatted document.

Clear documents help people understand instructions and take action.

Physical files, folders, labels, alphabetical filing, numerical filing, date filing, subject filing and file retrieval.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 14:40 “Let all things be done decently and in order.”

Day 1: Label practice files.
Day 2: Arrange files alphabetically.
Day 3: Arrange files by date.

Day 5: Prepare a simple filing guide.

A good filing system saves time and prevents confusion.

Proverbs 25:11 “A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in pictures of silver.”

Day 4: Practise sorting correspondence by department.

Words and records must be handled carefully because communication affects relationships and decisions.

Attendance register, visitor register, dispatch register, asset register, stock register, meeting register and daily duty log.

Proverbs 27:23 “Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, and look well to thy herds.”

Day 2: Prepare an attendance register.
Day 3: Prepare an asset register.
Day 4: Prepare a daily duty log.
Day 5: Review registers for completeness and neatness.

Character
A responsible administrator knows the state of what has been entrusted to the office.

Scripture
Romans 12:10 “Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another.”

Practice

Day 2: Complete a visitor register.
Day 3: Role-play directing visitors to the right office.
Day 4: Practise handling waiting visitors respectfully.
Day 5: Prepare a reception checklist.

Character
Reception is a place of honour. Visitors should be treated with respect and kindness.

Week 10. Telephone Etiquette and Message Taking

Teaching focus
Answering calls, greeting, tone of voice, listening, message notes, confirming details and ending calls politely.

Scripture
Colossians 4:6 “Let your speech be alway with grace, seasoned with salt, that ye may know how ye ought to answer every man.”

Practice
Day 1: Practise answering a phone call professionally.
Day 2: Practise taking a message.
Day 3: Practise confirming name, number and purpose of call.
Day 4: Role-play handling an impatient caller.
Day 5: Prepare a telephone etiquette checklist.

Character
Office speech must be gracious, clear and respectful.

Week 11. Customer Service and Public Relations

Teaching focus
Understanding clients, patience, service attitude, answering enquiries, handling complaints and protecting organisational image.

Scripture
Matthew 7:12 “Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss how visitors and clients want to be treated.
Day 2: Practise answering simple enquiries.
Day 3: Role-play handling a complaint.
Day 4: Prepare a customer service checklist.
Day 5: Write a reflection on treating others well.

Character
Treat visitors and clients the way you would want to be treated.

Week 12. Professional Email and Written Communication

Teaching focus
Email address, subject line, greeting, message body, attachment, reply, forwarding, tone and professional language.

Scripture
Proverbs 15:1 “A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify parts of a professional email.
Day 2: Write a simple official email.
Day 3: Attach a document to an email where available.
Day 4: Rewrite a rude message politely.
Day 5: Prepare an email etiquette guide.

Character
A soft and respectful answer can prevent conflict and protect relationships.

modules.title: Meetings, Minutes, Scheduling and Task Follow-Up

Teaching focus

Scripture
Proverbs 24:27 “Prepare thy work without, and make it fit for thyself in the field; and afterwards build thine house.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify reasons for office meetings.
Day 2: Prepare a meeting notice.
Day 3: Prepare a simple agenda.
Day 4: Arrange a mock meeting room.
Day 5: Prepare a meeting preparation checklist.

Character
Good meetings require preparation. Poor preparation wastes time.

Week 14. Minute Taking and Action Points

Teaching focus
Meaning of minutes, attendance, apologies, matters discussed, decisions, action points, responsible persons and deadlines.

Scripture
Habakkuk 2:2 “And the LORD answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.”

Practice
Day 1: Observe a mock meeting.
Day 2: Record attendance and key points.
Day 3: Write simple minutes.
Day 4: Identify action points and deadlines.
Day 5: Submit typed or neatly written minutes.

Character
Minutes make decisions plain and help people act responsibly.

Week 15. Scheduling, Calendars and Appointments

Teaching focus
Daily schedule, weekly plan, appointments, reminders, deadlines, avoiding clashes and supervisor support.

Scripture
Ecclesiastes 3:1 “To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare a daily schedule.
Day 2: Prepare a weekly calendar.
Day 3: Record sample appointments.
Day 4: Identify schedule conflicts.
Day 5: Prepare an appointment management checklist.

Character
Time must be managed wisely. Every task has its proper time.

Week 16. Task Management and Follow-Up

Teaching focus
Task lists, priority, delegation awareness, follow-up, reporting progress, reminders and completion tracking.

Scripture
Proverbs 21:5 “The thoughts of the diligent tend only to plenteousness; but of every one that is hasty only to want.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare a daily task list.
Day 2: Rank tasks by priority.
Day 3: Track assigned tasks.
Day 4: Prepare a simple progress update.
Day 5: Review completed and pending tasks.

Character
Diligent planning and follow-up produce results.

Week 17. Office Supplies and Inventory Control

Teaching focus
Stationery, supplies, stock records, issuing items, preventing waste, reordering and accountability.

Scripture
John 6:12 “When they were filled, he said unto his disciples, Gather up the fragments that remain, that nothing be lost.”

Day 1: Identify common office supplies.
Day 2: Prepare a stationery stock card.
Day 3: Record items issued.
Day 4: Identify wasteful use of office supplies.
Day 5: Prepare an office supply control checklist.

Character
Waste is poor stewardship. Office supplies must be used wisely.

Week 18. Office Equipment Care and Maintenance Reporting

Teaching focus
Computer, printer, photocopier, furniture, fan, lights, cabinets, maintenance reports and fault reporting.

Scripture
Luke 16:10 “He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify office equipment.
Day 2: Inspect equipment condition.
Day 3: Prepare an equipment register.
Day 4: Write a maintenance report for a faulty item.
Day 5: Prepare an equipment care checklist.

Character
Faithfulness is shown in caring for equipment that belongs to the organisation.

Week 19. Simple Office Reports

Teaching focus
Daily report, weekly report, activity report, incident report, inventory report and supervisor update.

Scripture
Proverbs 18:13 “He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare a daily office activity report.
Day 2: Prepare a weekly duty report.
Day 3: Prepare an incident report from a sample case.
Day 4: Review reports for facts and clarity.
Day 5: Present a report to the trainer.

Good reports must be based on facts, not assumptions.

Week 20. Digital Office Administration

Word processing, spreadsheets, digital filing, email, scanned documents, naming files, backup and password safety.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 14:40 “Let all things be done decently and in order.”

Day 1: Create a digital office folder.
Day 2: Type and save an official letter.
Day 3: Prepare a simple spreadsheet record.
Day 4: Practise digital file naming.
Day 5: Organise a digital filing system.

Character
Digital files must also be managed decently and in order.

Module 6 of 7. Office Leadership Support, Ethics, Enterprise and Workplace Readiness

Week 21. Supporting Supervisors and Office Teams

Teaching focus
Understanding authority, receiving instructions, preparing documents for supervisors, reminders, follow-up and teamwork.

Scripture
Hebrews 13:17 “Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls.”

Practice
Day 1: Role-play receiving instructions from a supervisor.
Day 2: Prepare a supervisor’s task reminder list.
Day 3: Prepare documents for review.
Day 4: Practise giving a respectful progress update.
Day 5: Prepare a supervisor support checklist.

Character
Office workers must respect authority and support leadership with humility.

Week 22. Workplace Ethics and Anti-Corruption Awareness

Teaching focus
Honesty, bribery, favouritism, false records, absenteeism, office gossip, misuse of resources and accountability.

Scripture
Proverbs 11:1 “A false balance is abomination to the LORD: but a just weight is his delight.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss dishonest practices in offices.
Day 2: Role-play refusing to falsify a record.
Day 3: Discuss misuse of office time and resources.
Day 4: Prepare an office ethics pledge.
Day 5: Review case studies on office integrity.

Character
God delights in honesty. Office administration must not become a place of corruption.

Week 23. Administrative Support for Events and Programmes

Teaching focus
Event records, attendance, registration, materials, communication, programme schedule, logistics and feedback forms.

Scripture
Nehemiah 2:18 “Then I told them of the hand of my God which was good upon me; as also the king’s words that he had spoken unto me. And they said, Let us rise up and build.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare a programme registration form.
Day 2: Prepare an event checklist.
Day 3: Prepare an attendance sheet.
Day 4: Prepare a feedback form.
Day 5: Plan administrative support for a mock programme.

Character
Good administration helps vision become organised action.

Week 24. Office Administration Enterprise Opportunities

Teaching focus
Typing service, filing service, reception support, meeting minutes, document formatting, records support and virtual administration awareness.

Scripture
Deuteronomy 8:18 “But thou shalt remember the LORD thy God: for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth.”

Practice
Day 1: List enterprise opportunities in office administration.
Day 2: Identify customers for one administrative service.
Day 3: Prepare a simple service description.
Day 4: Prepare a small-start budget.
Day 5: Write an office administration enterprise idea note.

Character
The power to create wealth comes from God. Administrative enterprise must be built on honesty, accuracy and service.

modules.content:
Module 7 of 7. Advanced Practice, Departmental Project and Attachment Preparation

Week 25. Departmental Mini-Project Planning

Teaching focus
Planning an office administration mini-project, team roles, documents, records, timeline, confidentiality and expected result.

Scripture
Habakkuk 2:2 “And the LORD answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.”

Practice
Day 1: Choose a safe departmental administrative mini-project.
Day 2: Prepare project goals and expected results.
Day 3: Prepare documents, registers and templates.
Day 4: Assign team roles and deadlines.
Day 5: Submit project plan for trainer approval.

Character
Clear planning helps administrative work become organised and effective.

Week 26. Departmental Mini-Project Implementation

Teaching focus
Carrying out a supervised administrative project with accuracy, order, teamwork, records and reporting.

Scripture
Nehemiah 4:6 “So built we the wall; and all the wall was joined together unto the half thereof: for the people had a mind to work.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare the office area, tools and records.
Day 2: Begin filing, reception, report, register or event support project.
Day 3: Continue assigned tasks and check accuracy.
Day 4: Prepare project progress report.
Day 5: Review records, correct errors and submit progress update.

Character
Progress comes when people have a mind to work and cooperate with discipline.

Week 27. Final Practical Demonstration and Portfolio

Teaching focus
Demonstrating document preparation, filing, reception, correspondence, minutes, scheduling, reports and portfolio evidence.

Scripture
2 Timothy 2:15 “Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed.”

Practice
Day 1: Demonstrate document preparation and filing.
Day 2: Demonstrate reception and telephone etiquette.
Day 3: Demonstrate minute taking, scheduling and report writing.
Day 4: Organise office administration portfolio.
Day 5: Present practical evidence to the trainer.

Character
A trained worker should not be ashamed. Diligence, skill and discipline prepare trainees for approval.

Week 28. Industrial Attachment Preparation

Teaching focus
Preparing for office placement, supervisor conduct, confidentiality, daily logs, records, punctuality and final readiness.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:29 “Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify possible office administration attachment placements.
Day 2: Prepare personal attachment learning goals.
Day 3: Practise writing daily office attachment logs.
Day 4: Review confidentiality, office conduct and workplace behaviour.
Day 5: Complete final departmental readiness assessment.

Character
Diligence opens doors. A faithful office administrator can serve in important places.

modules.title: Orientation, Animal Care, Safety and Farm Discipline
modules.content:
Module 1 of 7. Orientation, Animal Care, Safety and Farm Discipline

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 1. Introduction to Poultry and Livestock

Teaching focus
Meaning of poultry and livestock, importance of animal production, food security, income generation and dignity of farm work.

Scripture
Genesis 1:28 “And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it.”

Practice
Day 1: Walk around the animal unit and identify poultry and livestock areas.
Day 2: List common poultry and livestock species in the community.
Day 3: Discuss the benefits of eggs, meat, milk and manure.
Day 4: Identify common problems in animal farming, such as disease, poor feeding, poor housing and poor records.
Day 5: Write a reflection on why animal farming is important for families and communities.

Character
Animal farming is part of stewardship. Trainees must use God-given resources productively and responsibly.

Week 2. Animal Welfare, Compassion and Responsibility

Teaching focus
Meaning of animal welfare, kindness to animals, avoiding cruelty, careful handling and responsible care.

Scripture
Proverbs 12:10 “A righteous man regardeth the life of his beast: but the tender mercies of the wicked are cruel.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss signs of comfortable and uncomfortable animals.
Day 2: Observe animal behaviour from a safe distance.
Day 3: Identify poor welfare conditions such as overcrowding, lack of water and dirty housing.
Day 4: Prepare an animal welfare checklist.
Day 5: Write a short note on why cruelty to animals is wrong.

Character
A righteous person cares for animals. Neglect and cruelty do not reflect Kingdom character.

Week 3. Farm Safety and Personal Hygiene

Teaching focus
Farm hazards, animal bites, scratches, dust, manure, sharp tools, slippery floors, handwashing and protective clothing.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:3 “A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify common hazards in poultry and livestock areas.
Day 2: Demonstrate correct handwashing after animal contact.
Day 3: Demonstrate safe movement inside animal housing.
Day 4: Prepare a farm safety checklist.
Day 5: Conduct a supervised safety inspection.

Character
Safety is wisdom. A careless trainee can injure himself, herself, others or the animals.

Week 4. Farm Tools, Equipment and Housing Areas

Teaching focus
Feeders, drinkers, buckets, shovels, brooms, wheelbarrows, crates, egg trays, pens, cages, brooder areas and tool care.

Scripture
Luke 16:10 “He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify poultry and livestock tools and equipment.
Day 2: Clean feeders and drinkers under supervision.
Day 3: Arrange tools in the correct storage area.
Day 4: Prepare a tool and equipment register.
Day 5: Record damaged or missing equipment.

Character
Faithfulness begins with small things. A trainee who cares for tools can be trusted with animals and farm resources.

Week 5. Poultry Housing and Brooder Awareness

Teaching focus
Poultry house design, ventilation, litter, spacing, brooding, heat, light, protection and cleanliness.

Scripture
Proverbs 24:3 “Through wisdom is an house builded; and by understanding it is established.”

Practice
Day 1: Inspect a poultry house or model and identify important parts.
Day 2: Discuss ventilation and overcrowding.
Day 3: Prepare clean litter under supervision.
Day 4: Observe brooder setup where available.
Day 5: Prepare a poultry house checklist.

Character
Good housing requires wisdom. Poor housing can cause disease, stress and poor growth.

Week 6. Livestock Housing and Pen Management

Teaching focus
Goat, sheep, pig, cattle or rabbit housing awareness, ventilation, drainage, shade, bedding, fencing and cleanliness.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 14:40 “Let all things be done decently and in order.”

Practice
Day 1: Inspect a livestock pen or housing model.
Day 2: Identify good and poor housing features.
Day 3: Clean a livestock pen under supervision.
Day 4: Check drainage and dry resting area.
Day 5: Prepare a livestock housing checklist.

Character
Order and cleanliness protect animal health and farm productivity.

Week 7. Feeding Principles for Poultry and Livestock

Teaching focus
Feed types, balanced feeding awareness, feeding times, feed waste, feed storage and signs of poor feeding.

Scripture
Proverbs 27:23 “Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, and look well to thy herds.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify different feeds used on the farm.
Day 2: Fill feeders correctly under supervision.
Day 3: Observe feeding behaviour.
Day 4: Record feed quantity used.
Day 5: Discuss how feed waste affects profit.

Character
A diligent trainee observes whether animals are feeding well. Appetite changes can reveal problems.

Week 8. Watering, Clean Water and Daily Observation

Teaching focus
Clean water, drinker hygiene, dehydration signs, water contamination, daily observation and reporting.

Scripture
Isaiah 58:11 “And thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not.”

Practice
Day 1: Clean drinkers and water containers.
Day 2: Fill drinkers with clean water.
Day 3: Observe whether animals are drinking well.
Day 4: Identify dirty or contaminated water.
Day 5: Record water supply problems and solutions.

Character
Clean water supports life. Trainees must not neglect watering because animals depend on it daily.

Week 9. Chick Brooding Awareness

Matthew 23:37 “How often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings.”

Day 5: Prepare a brooding observation checklist.

Character
Care requires watchfulness. Young animals need special attention, protection and warmth.

Week 10. Poultry Feeding, Growth and Litter Management

Teaching focus
Starter, grower and finisher feed awareness, growth observation, litter dryness, ammonia smell and ventilation.

Scripture
Luke 16:10 “He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify feed stages at awareness level.
Day 2: Feed birds under supervision.
Day 3: Observe bird growth and behaviour.
Day 4: Stir or replace wet litter under supervision.
Day 5: Record feeding and litter condition.

Character
Small daily tasks affect the final result. Wet litter and poor feeding can destroy a flock.

Week 11. Egg Production and Egg Handling Awareness

Teaching focus
Layers, nesting areas, egg collection, egg cleaning awareness, storage, breakage prevention and egg records.

Scripture
Psalm 128:2 “For thou shalt eat the labour of thine hands: happy shalt thou be, and it shall be well with thee.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify nesting areas where available.
Day 2: Collect eggs carefully under supervision.
Day 3: Sort cracked and good eggs.
Day 4: Arrange eggs in trays properly.
Day 5: Record number of eggs collected.

Character
Careful labour produces reward. Egg handling must be gentle and responsible.

Week 12. Poultry Health Observation and Biosecurity

Teaching focus
Sick bird signs, isolation awareness, mortality records, footbaths, handwashing, visitor control and disease prevention.

Scripture
Song of Solomon 2:15 “Take us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vines: for our vines have tender grapes.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify signs of sick birds from pictures or safe observation.
Day 2: Practise handwashing and footbath use where available.
Day 3: Prepare a mortality record sheet.
Day 4: Discuss visitor control and farm entry rules.
Day 5: Prepare a poultry biosecurity checklist.

Character
Small signs must not be ignored. Early reporting can save the flock.

modules.title: Livestock Management Practice
modules.content:
Module 4 of 7. Livestock Management Practice

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 13. Goat and Sheep Management Awareness

Teaching focus
Housing, feeding, watering, grazing awareness, common behaviour, signs of sickness and safe handling.

Scripture
Proverbs 27:27 “And thou shalt have goats’ milk enough for thy food, for the food of thy household, and for the maintenance for thy maidens.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify goats and sheep and discuss their uses.
Day 2: Observe feeding behaviour.
Day 3: Clean the pen under supervision.
Day 4: Observe body condition at awareness level.
Day 5: Prepare a goat and sheep care checklist.

Character
Livestock can support households. Proper care can bring food, income and stability.

Week 14. Cattle Management Awareness

Teaching focus
Cattle housing, feeding, watering, milking awareness, manure handling, safety around large animals and disease observation.

Scripture
Proverbs 14:4 “Where no oxen are, the crib is clean: but much increase is by the strength of the ox.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss the uses of cattle.
Day 2: Observe cattle feeding and watering from a safe distance where available.
Day 3: Identify safety rules around large animals.
Day 4: Discuss manure handling and farm hygiene.
Day 5: Prepare a cattle care awareness note.

Character
Productivity requires responsibility. Animals bring increase, but they also require work and care.

Week 15. Pig and Rabbit Management Awareness

Teaching focus
Pig and rabbit housing where applicable, feeding, watering, cleanliness, reproduction awareness and disease observation.

Scripture
Proverbs 12:10 “A righteous man regardeth the life of his beast: but the tender mercies of the wicked are cruel.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify pigs and rabbits from pictures, videos or farm examples.
Day 2: Discuss housing and feeding needs.
Day 3: Prepare a simple cleaning checklist.
Day 4: Observe behaviour and comfort signs where available.
Day 5: Write a care plan for one livestock species.

Character
Every animal under human care must be treated responsibly and kindly.

Week 16. Manure Management and Farm Sanitation

Teaching focus
Manure collection, composting awareness, odour control, flies, drainage, waste disposal and sanitation.

Scripture
John 6:12 “When they were filled, he said unto his disciples, Gather up the fragments that remain, that nothing be lost.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify manure and waste areas.
Day 2: Collect manure safely under supervision.
Day 3: Discuss composting and use of manure for crops.
Day 4: Clean and disinfect selected equipment under supervision.
Day 5: Prepare a farm sanitation checklist.

Character
Waste can become useful when managed properly. Stewardship reduces loss and protects health.

modules.title: Animal Health Awareness, Records and Farm Productivity
modules.content:
Module 5 of 7. Animal Health Awareness, Records and Farm Productivity

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 17. Signs of Sickness and Early Reporting

Teaching focus
Loss of appetite, weakness, coughing, diarrhoea, abnormal droppings, wounds, poor growth, isolation and early reporting.

Scripture
Proverbs 27:23 “Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, and look well to thy herds.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify signs of sickness from pictures or safe observation.
Day 2: Prepare a daily animal observation sheet.
Day 3: Practise reporting a sick animal to the trainer.
Day 4: Discuss why treatment must be supervised by qualified persons.
Day 5: Write a sickness observation report.

Character
Diligent observation can prevent loss. A responsible trainee reports problems early.

Week 18. Vaccination, Medication and Veterinary Supervision Awareness

Teaching focus
Vaccination records, medication awareness, veterinary supervision, withdrawal periods awareness, avoiding self-treatment and safe storage.

Scripture
Proverbs 19:20 “Hear counsel, and receive instruction, that thou mayest be wise in thy latter end.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss why animal health professionals are important.
Day 2: Observe a sample vaccination or treatment record.
Day 3: Discuss why trainees must not medicate animals without approval.
Day 4: Prepare a medicine storage awareness checklist.
Day 5: Record questions to ask a veterinary officer or animal health worker.

Character
Wise trainees receive instruction. Animal treatment must not be done carelessly or proudly.

Week 19. Farm Records and Production Tracking

Teaching focus
Animal count, feed records, egg records, mortality records, weight gain awareness, sales records and expense records.

Scripture
Habakkuk 2:2 “And the LORD answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.”

Practice
Day 1: Create a simple animal count record.
Day 2: Record feed used.
Day 3: Record eggs collected or production output where available.
Day 4: Record mortality or sickness observations.
Day 5: Review records for neatness and truthfulness.

Character
Clear records protect accountability. A farm without records cannot easily measure progress or loss.

Week 20. Productivity, Growth and Feed Cost Awareness

Teaching focus
Growth, feed conversion awareness, feed cost, waste reduction, production targets and farm profitability.

Scripture
Proverbs 21:5 “The thoughts of the diligent tend only to plenteousness; but of every one that is hasty only to want.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss how feed cost affects profit.
Day 2: Identify causes of feed waste.
Day 3: Prepare a simple feed cost record.
Day 4: Discuss growth and production goals.
Day 5: Prepare a productivity improvement note.

Character
Diligent planning improves productivity. Careless feeding and poor records lead to loss.

modules.title: Agribusiness, Marketing, Processing and Enterprise
modules.content:
Module 6 of 7. Agribusiness, Marketing, Processing and Enterprise

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 21. Poultry and Livestock Business Opportunities

Teaching focus
Eggs, broilers, layers, goats, sheep, cattle, rabbits, feed sales, manure sales, animal products and small enterprise.

Scripture
Deuteronomy 8:18 “But thou shalt remember the LORD thy God: for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth.”

Practice
Day 1: List poultry and livestock business opportunities.
Day 2: Identify customers for eggs, meat, live animals or manure.
Day 3: Choose one enterprise idea.
Day 4: Prepare a simple service or product description.
Day 5: Write a poultry or livestock enterprise idea note.

Character
The power to create wealth comes from God. Animal farming enterprise must be built on honesty, care and service.

Week 22. Farm Budgeting and Costing

Teaching focus
Cost of chicks, feed, housing, medicine, labour, water, transport, mortality, sales and profit.

Scripture
Luke 14:28 “For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost?”

Practice
Day 1: List start-up costs for a small poultry or livestock project.
Day 2: Estimate feed cost using sample prices.
Day 3: Estimate sales income using sample production figures.
Day 4: Prepare a simple profit and loss example.
Day 5: Prepare a small farm budget.

Character
Wise farmers count the cost before starting. Poor planning can lead to abandoned projects.

Week 23. Marketing, Customer Care and Product Quality

Teaching focus
Selling eggs, live birds, meat animals, milk awareness, manure, packaging, customer trust, honesty and quality.

Scripture
Proverbs 11:1 “A false balance is abomination to the LORD: but a just weight is his delight.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify possible customers for poultry and livestock products.
Day 2: Practise sorting eggs or products where available.
Day 3: Role-play selling farm products to a customer.
Day 4: Prepare a simple marketing plan.
Day 5: Discuss honest weights, fair prices and customer trust.

Character
Animal products must be sold honestly. False weight, bad products and lies destroy trust.

Week 24. Cooperative Farming and Small-Start Enterprise

Teaching focus
Group farming, cooperative savings, shared labour, shared tools, group records, trust and starting small.

Scripture
Ecclesiastes 4:9 “Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss cooperative poultry or livestock farming.
Day 2: Create a sample cooperative group structure.
Day 3: Write simple cooperative rules.
Day 4: Prepare a group enterprise budget.
Day 5: Present a cooperative poultry or livestock plan.

Character
Teamwork can increase productivity, but it requires honesty, trust and accountability.

modules.title: Advanced Practice, Departmental Project and Attachment Preparation
modules.content:
Module 7 of 7. Advanced Practice, Departmental Project and Attachment Preparation

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 25. Departmental Mini-Project Planning

Teaching focus
Planning a poultry or livestock mini-project, team roles, housing, feed, water, records, safety and expected outcome.

Scripture
Nehemiah 2:18 “Then I told them of the hand of my God which was good upon me; as also the king’s words that he had spoken unto me. And they said, Let us rise up and build.”

Practice
Day 1: Choose a safe departmental mini-project.
Day 2: Prepare project goals and expected results.
Day 3: Prepare tools, feed, records and safety checklist.
Day 4: Assign team roles and reporting duties.
Day 5: Submit project plan for trainer approval.

Character
Vision must become organised action. Trainees must rise and build responsibly.

Week 26. Departmental Mini-Project Implementation

Teaching focus
Carrying out a supervised poultry or livestock project with hygiene, teamwork, records and quality checks.

Scripture
Nehemiah 4:6 “So built we the wall; and all the wall was joined together unto the half thereof: for the people had a mind to work.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare the animal area, tools and records.
Day 2: Begin feeding, cleaning, observation or production project under supervision.
Day 3: Continue assigned tasks and record progress.
Day 4: Check hygiene, animal comfort, records and teamwork.
Day 5: Clean the area and review project progress.

Character
Progress comes when people have a mind to work and cooperate with discipline.

Week 27. Final Practical Demonstration and Portfolio

Teaching focus
Demonstrating animal identification, feeding, watering, housing inspection, health observation, records and portfolio evidence.

Scripture
2 Timothy 2:15 “Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed.”

Practice
Day 1: Demonstrate poultry and livestock identification.
Day 2: Demonstrate feeder and drinker cleaning.
Day 3: Demonstrate daily animal observation and record keeping.
Day 4: Organise poultry and livestock portfolio.
Day 5: Present practical evidence to the trainer.

Character
A trained worker should not be ashamed. Diligence, skill and discipline prepare trainees for approval.

Week 28. Industrial Attachment Preparation

Teaching focus
Preparing for poultry or livestock farm placement, supervisor conduct, farm safety, daily logs, animal welfare and final readiness.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:29 “Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify possible poultry and livestock attachment placements.
Day 2: Prepare personal attachment learning goals.
Day 3: Practise writing daily poultry and livestock attachment logs.
Day 4: Review farm safety, biosecurity and workplace behaviour.
Day 5: Complete final departmental readiness assessment.

Character
Diligence opens doors. A faithful trainee can be trusted with greater responsibility.

modules.title: Project Management Orientation, Vision and Planning Foundation
modules.content:
Module 1 of 7. Project Management Orientation, Vision and Planning Foundation

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 1. Introduction to Project Management

Teaching focus
Meaning of a project, meaning of project management, types of projects, project success and the value of organised work.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 14:40 “Let all things be done decently and in order.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss the meaning of a project.
Day 2: List examples of projects in the Academy, community, church and business.
Day 3: Identify why some projects fail.
Day 4: Identify what makes a project successful.
Day 5: Write a reflection on why order is necessary in project work.

Character
Good projects require order. Disorder turns good ideas into confusion.

Week 2. Project Vision and Goal Setting

Teaching focus
Vision, goals, objectives, expected results, beneficiaries and writing clear project statements.

Scripture
Habakkuk 2:2 “And the LORD answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify a simple community or Academy project idea.
Day 2: Write a project vision statement.
Day 3: Write one main project goal.
Day 4: Write three simple objectives.
Day 5: Present the project vision to the class.

Character
A clear written vision helps people understand the direction of the work.

Week 3. Project Needs and Problem Identification

Teaching focus
Identifying problems, needs assessment, root causes, beneficiaries, project justification and local relevance.

Scripture
Nehemiah 2:17 “Then said I unto them, Ye see the distress that we are in, how Jerusalem lieth waste: come, and let us build up the wall.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify one problem in the Academy or community.
Day 2: Discuss who is affected by the problem.
Day 3: Identify causes of the problem.
Day 4: Explain why the project is needed.
Day 5: Prepare a simple needs assessment note.

Character
A good project begins with seeing real needs and responding responsibly.

Week 4. Project Scope and Boundaries

Teaching focus
Meaning of project scope, what is included, what is not included, expected outputs, limitations and avoiding confusion.

Scripture
Proverbs 4:26 “Ponder the path of thy feet, and let all thy ways be established.”

Practice
Day 1: Define the scope of a small project.
Day 2: List what the project will include.
Day 3: List what the project will not include.
Day 4: Identify possible confusion if scope is not clear.
Day 5: Prepare a simple project scope statement.

Character
Wise people define their path clearly. Clear scope prevents confusion and quarrels.

modules.title: Work Planning, Scheduling, Roles and Communication
modules.content:
Module 2 of 7. Work Planning, Scheduling, Roles and Communication

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 5. Work Breakdown and Activity Planning

Teaching focus
Breaking projects into smaller tasks, activity lists, work packages, sequence and responsibility.

Scripture
Proverbs 24:27 “Prepare thy work without, and make it fit for thyself in the field; and afterwards build thine house.”

Practice
Day 1: Choose a small project idea.
Day 2: Break the project into major tasks.
Day 3: Break each task into smaller activities.
Day 4: Arrange activities in proper order.
Day 5: Prepare a work breakdown chart.

Character
Preparation makes work easier. A project should be broken into clear tasks before execution.

Week 6. Project Scheduling and Timelines

Teaching focus
Start dates, end dates, activity duration, deadlines, daily plans, weekly schedules and timeline tracking.

Scripture
Ecclesiastes 3:1 “To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven.”

Practice
Day 1: Estimate how long each project activity will take.
Day 2: Prepare a simple project timeline.
Day 3: Identify activities that must come first.
Day 4: Add deadlines to each activity.
Day 5: Review the schedule for realism.

Character
Every task has its time. Project workers must respect time and deadlines.

Week 7. Project Team Roles and Responsibilities

Teaching focus
Project leader, secretary, treasurer, logistics officer, safety officer, procurement support, monitoring support and team accountability.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 12:18 “But now hath God set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him.”

Practice
Day 1: List possible project team roles.
Day 2: Assign roles for a sample project.
Day 3: Write duties for each role.
Day 4: Discuss why every role matters.
Day 5: Prepare a team responsibility chart.

Character
Every team member has a part to play. No role should be despised.

Week 8. Project Communication and Meetings

Teaching focus
Project meetings, agendas, meeting notes, updates, communication channels, escalation and respectful reporting.

Scripture
Colossians 4:6 “Let your speech be alway with grace, seasoned with salt, that ye may know how ye ought to answer every man.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare a project meeting agenda.
Day 2: Hold a mock project meeting.
Day 3: Record meeting decisions.
Day 4: Prepare action points.
Day 5: Give a respectful project update.

Character
Good communication must be clear, respectful and purposeful.
