modules.title: Budgeting, Procurement, Resource Management and Accountability
modules.content:
Module 3 of 7. Budgeting, Procurement, Resource Management and Accountability

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 9. Project Budgeting Foundation

Teaching focus
Meaning of budget, materials, labour, transport, tools, services, emergency allowance and approval.

Scripture
Luke 14:28 “For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost?”

Practice
Day 1: List items needed for a small project.
Day 2: Estimate cost for each item.
Day 3: Add labour and transport awareness costs.
Day 4: Prepare a simple project budget.
Day 5: Present the budget for trainer review.

Character
Wise people count the cost before starting. Budgeting protects projects from waste and failure.

Week 10. Cost Control and Waste Prevention

Teaching focus
Tracking spending, avoiding waste, comparing budget with actual cost, preventing leakage and reporting differences.

Scripture
John 6:12 “When they were filled, he said unto his disciples, Gather up the fragments that remain, that nothing be lost.”

Practice
Day 1: Review a sample project budget.
Day 2: Record sample project expenses.
Day 3: Compare planned cost with actual cost.
Day 4: Identify causes of waste.
Day 5: Prepare a cost control checklist.

Character
Waste is poor stewardship. Project resources must be protected.

Week 11. Procurement and Material Control Awareness

Teaching focus
Material requests, supplier comparison, purchase approval, delivery note, receiving materials, issuing materials and stock records.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 4:2 “Moreover it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare a material request form.
Day 2: Compare sample supplier prices.
Day 3: Prepare a simple purchase record.
Day 4: Record materials received.
Day 5: Prepare a material issue record.

Character
Project resources are entrusted resources. Faithfulness is required in procurement and material control.

Week 12. Financial Accountability and Project Records

Teaching focus
Receipts, vouchers, expense records, petty cash, approvals, financial summaries and truthful reporting.

Scripture
Proverbs 11:1 “A false balance is abomination to the LORD: but a just weight is his delight.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify receipts and vouchers.
Day 2: Record sample project expenses.
Day 3: Match expenses with supporting documents.
Day 4: Prepare a simple project finance report.
Day 5: Discuss the danger of false financial records.

Character
God hates false balances. Project money must be recorded honestly.

modules.title: Risk, Safety, Quality and Problem-Solving
modules.content:
Module 4 of 7. Risk, Safety, Quality and Problem-Solving

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 13. Project Risk Identification

Teaching focus
Meaning of risk, common project risks, delays, cost increases, accidents, poor quality, conflict and resource shortages.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:3 “A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished.”

Practice
Day 1: Define risk in simple language.
Day 2: Identify risks in a sample project.
Day 3: List causes of delays.
Day 4: Prepare a simple risk register.
Day 5: Discuss how early planning reduces danger.

Character
A prudent project worker sees danger early and plans wisely.

Week 14. Project Safety Management

Teaching focus
Safety planning, hazard identification, personal protective equipment, emergency reporting, site safety and event safety.

Scripture
Proverbs 27:12 “A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself; but the simple pass on, and are punished.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify safety hazards in different project types.
Day 2: Prepare a project safety checklist.
Day 3: Assign a safety officer role in a mock project.
Day 4: Prepare an emergency reporting plan.
Day 5: Conduct a supervised safety review.

Character
Safety is part of good project leadership. Lives must not be endangered by carelessness.

Week 15. Quality Management and Standards

Teaching focus
Meaning of quality, project standards, inspection, correction, rework, customer satisfaction and excellence.

Scripture
Colossians 3:23 “And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss what quality means in projects.
Day 2: Prepare a quality checklist.
Day 3: Inspect a sample project output.
Day 4: Identify defects and improvements.
Day 5: Write a quality review report.

Character
Quality matters because work should be done heartily as unto the Lord.

Week 16. Problem-Solving and Corrective Action

Teaching focus
Identifying problems, analysing causes, choosing solutions, reporting issues, taking corrective action and learning lessons.

Scripture
James 1:5 “If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify a problem in a sample project.
Day 2: Discuss possible causes.
Day 3: List possible solutions.
Day 4: Choose the best solution and explain why.
Day 5: Prepare a corrective action plan.

Character
Project problems require wisdom, not panic. Trainees must seek wisdom and act responsibly.

modules.title: Monitoring, Evaluation, Reporting and Stakeholder Engagement
modules.content:
Module 5 of 7. Monitoring, Evaluation, Reporting and Stakeholder Engagement

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 17. Monitoring Project Progress

Teaching focus
Meaning of monitoring, tracking activities, checking timelines, checking budgets, evidence gathering and progress updates.

Scripture
Proverbs 27:23 “Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, and look well to thy herds.”

Practice
Day 1: Review a project activity plan.
Day 2: Mark completed and pending activities.
Day 3: Check budget usage.
Day 4: Collect evidence of progress.
Day 5: Prepare a progress monitoring note.

Character
Diligent project workers know the state of the work entrusted to them.

Week 18. Project Reporting

Teaching focus
Daily reports, weekly reports, activity reports, incident reports, financial reports and clear presentation.

Scripture
Habakkuk 2:2 “And the LORD answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare a daily project report.
Day 2: Prepare a weekly activity report.
Day 3: Prepare an incident report from a sample case.
Day 4: Prepare a financial summary report.
Day 5: Present the report clearly to the class.

Character
Reports must be clear, truthful and useful for decision-making.

Week 19. Stakeholder Engagement and Community Relations

Teaching focus
Stakeholders, beneficiaries, sponsors, supervisors, community leaders, team members, communication and expectation management.

Scripture
Romans 12:18 “If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify stakeholders in a sample project.
Day 2: List each stakeholder’s interest.
Day 3: Prepare a communication plan.
Day 4: Role-play meeting a community leader.
Day 5: Discuss how to handle stakeholder concerns respectfully.

Character
Project managers must work peacefully with people and manage expectations wisely.

Week 20. Evaluation and Lessons Learnt

Teaching focus
Meaning of evaluation, outputs, outcomes, feedback, lessons learnt, success indicators and future improvement.

Scripture
2 Corinthians 13:5 “Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify project outputs and outcomes.
Day 2: Prepare simple evaluation questions.
Day 3: Review a completed sample project.
Day 4: Write lessons learnt.
Day 5: Present recommendations for improvement.

Character
Evaluation helps people learn, improve and avoid repeating mistakes.

modules.title: Project Administration, Leadership, Ethics and Enterprise
modules.content:
Module 6 of 7. Project Administration, Leadership, Ethics and Enterprise

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 21. Project Documentation and Filing

Teaching focus
Project files, project briefs, budgets, reports, receipts, minutes, photos, approvals, contracts awareness and final documents.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 14:40 “Let all things be done decently and in order.”

Practice
Day 1: Create a project file index.
Day 2: Arrange project documents in proper order.
Day 3: Label project files.
Day 4: Prepare a project document checklist.
Day 5: Review a sample project file for completeness.

Character
Well-organised documents protect memory, accountability and future learning.

Week 22. Project Leadership and Team Motivation

Teaching focus
Leadership, service, encouragement, conflict management, delegation, discipline, example and team morale.

Scripture
Mark 10:45 “For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss leadership as service.
Day 2: Role-play encouraging a tired team member.
Day 3: Practise giving instructions respectfully.
Day 4: Discuss simple conflict resolution.
Day 5: Prepare a project leadership checklist.

Character
True leadership is service. A project leader must not be proud or harsh.

Week 23. Project Ethics, Transparency and Anti-Corruption

Teaching focus
Honest records, avoiding bribery, avoiding favouritism, fair procurement, truthful reports, proper approvals and accountability.

Scripture
Proverbs 10:9 “He that walketh uprightly walketh surely: but he that perverteth his ways shall be known.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss dishonest practices in project work.
Day 2: Role-play refusing to falsify a report.
Day 3: Discuss fair procurement.
Day 4: Prepare a project ethics pledge.
Day 5: Review case studies on corruption and transparency.

Character
A project built on dishonesty will eventually be exposed. Uprightness brings security.

Week 24. Project Management Enterprise Opportunities

Teaching focus
Project coordination support, event planning, community project support, monitoring support, reporting support and small project administration.

Scripture
Deuteronomy 8:18 “But thou shalt remember the LORD thy God: for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth.”

Practice
Day 1: List enterprise opportunities in project management support.
Day 2: Identify customers for one project support service.
Day 3: Prepare a simple service description.
Day 4: Prepare a small-start budget.
Day 5: Write a project management enterprise idea note.

Character
The power to create wealth comes from God. Project management enterprise must be built on honesty, order and service.

modules.title: Advanced Practice, Departmental Project and Attachment Preparation
modules.content:
Module 7 of 7. Advanced Practice, Departmental Project and Attachment Preparation

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 25. Departmental Mini-Project Planning

Teaching focus
Planning a supervised project from start to finish, including goal, scope, schedule, budget, team roles, risks, monitoring and report format.

Scripture
Nehemiah 2:18 “Then I told them of the hand of my God which was good upon me; as also the king’s words that he had spoken unto me. And they said, Let us rise up and build.”

Practice
Day 1: Choose a departmental mini-project.
Day 2: Write project goal, objectives and scope.
Day 3: Prepare schedule, budget and role chart.
Day 4: Prepare risk, safety and monitoring checklist.
Day 5: Submit full project plan for trainer approval.

Character
Vision must move from words into organised action. Trainees must rise and build responsibly.

Week 26. Departmental Mini-Project Implementation

Teaching focus
Carrying out a supervised project with planning, teamwork, safety, resource control, monitoring and progress reporting.

Scripture
Nehemiah 4:6 “So built we the wall; and all the wall was joined together unto the half thereof: for the people had a mind to work.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare project area, tools and records.
Day 2: Begin project implementation according to plan.
Day 3: Continue assigned tasks and monitor progress.
Day 4: Check quality, safety, budget and teamwork.
Day 5: Prepare project progress report.

Character
Progress comes when people have a mind to work and cooperate with discipline.

Week 27. Project Closure, Final Report and Portfolio

Teaching focus
Completing a project, checking outputs, preparing final report, lessons learnt, financial summary and portfolio evidence.

Scripture
Ecclesiastes 7:8 “Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof.”

Practice
Day 1: Check whether project objectives were achieved.
Day 2: Prepare final activity report.
Day 3: Prepare final budget and expense summary.
Day 4: Write lessons learnt and recommendations.
Day 5: Organise project management portfolio.

Character
Starting is important, but finishing well is better.

Week 28. Industrial Attachment Preparation

Teaching focus
Preparing for project-related placement, supervisor conduct, project records, daily logs, teamwork, confidentiality and final readiness.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:29 “Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify possible project management attachment placements.
Day 2: Prepare personal attachment learning goals.
Day 3: Practise writing daily project attachment logs.
Day 4: Review project ethics, communication and workplace behaviour.
Day 5: Complete final departmental readiness assessment.

Character
Diligence opens doors. A faithful project trainee can be trusted with greater responsibility.

modules.title: Public Administration Orientation, Governance and Public Service
modules.content:
Module 1 of 7. Public Administration Orientation, Governance and Public Service

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 1. Introduction to Public Administration

Teaching focus
Meaning of public administration, importance of public institutions, role of administrators and connection between administration and public welfare.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 14:40 “Let all things be done decently and in order.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss the meaning of public administration.
Day 2: Identify public offices in the community, local government, schools, hospitals and ministries.
Day 3: List services provided by public institutions.
Day 4: Discuss what happens when public offices are disorganised.
Day 5: Write a reflection on why order is important in public service.

Character
Public administration brings order to society. Disorder in public offices affects many people.

Week 2. Government, Governance and Authority

Teaching focus
Meaning of government, meaning of governance, levels of government awareness, lawful authority, public order and civic responsibility.

Scripture
Romans 13:1 “Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God.”

Practice
Day 1: Define government and governance in simple terms.
Day 2: Identify local, state and national government functions at awareness level.
Day 3: Discuss why lawful authority is important.
Day 4: Prepare a simple governance chart.
Day 5: Discuss how citizens should relate to public authority.

Character
Public service requires respect for lawful authority and responsible civic behaviour.

Week 3. The Heart of Public Service

Teaching focus
Service to citizens, humility, patience, fairness, compassion, duty and public trust.

Scripture
Micah 6:8 “He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss what it means to serve the public.
Day 2: Identify examples of fair and unfair treatment of citizens.
Day 3: Role-play serving an elderly citizen respectfully.
Day 4: Prepare a public service attitude checklist.
Day 5: Write a personal public service pledge.

Character
Public service must be rooted in justice, mercy and humility.

Week 4. Public Office Conduct and Discipline

Teaching focus
Punctuality, official dressing, respectful communication, obedience to procedure, confidentiality and office discipline.

Scripture
Colossians 3:23 “And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.”

Practice
Day 1: Practise professional greeting in a public office.
Day 2: Review proper office appearance.
Day 3: Role-play receiving instructions from a supervisor.
Day 4: Discuss poor conduct in public offices.
Day 5: Prepare a public office conduct checklist.

Character
Public duties must be done heartily and responsibly because many lives can be affected by administrative behaviour.

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 5. Public Records and Documentation

Teaching focus
Meaning of public records, registers, files, correspondence, minutes, reports, confidentiality and record protection.

Scripture
Habakkuk 2:2 “And the LORD answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify public office records and registers.
Day 2: Prepare a simple citizen request register.
Day 3: Prepare an incoming correspondence record.
Day 4: Prepare an outgoing correspondence record.
Day 5: File sample public documents neatly.

Character
Clear records help public offices act responsibly and reduce confusion.

Week 6. Administrative Procedures and Due Process

Teaching focus
Procedures, approvals, official channels, forms, signatures, filing, escalation and why due process matters.

Scripture
Proverbs 19:20 “Hear counsel, and receive instruction, that thou mayest be wise in thy latter end.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss what due process means.
Day 2: Arrange a simple approval process for a public request.
Day 3: Identify missing steps in a sample procedure.
Day 4: Role-play submitting a request through proper channels.
Day 5: Prepare a due process checklist.

Character
Wise people follow proper instruction. Due process protects fairness and accountability.

Week 7. Citizen Reception and Public Communication

Teaching focus
Welcoming citizens, listening, asking questions respectfully, giving directions, taking messages and protecting public trust.

Scripture
Colossians 4:6 “Let your speech be alway with grace, seasoned with salt, that ye may know how ye ought to answer every man.”

Practice
Day 1: Practise welcoming citizens politely.
Day 2: Complete a visitor or citizen enquiry register.
Day 3: Role-play explaining a simple office procedure.
Day 4: Practise directing a citizen to the right office.
Day 5: Prepare a citizen service communication checklist.

Character
Public communication must be gracious, respectful and clear.

Week 8. Handling Complaints and Public Concerns

Teaching focus
Listening to complaints, recording concerns, avoiding argument, reporting issues, following up and treating people with dignity.

Scripture
James 1:19 “Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss common complaints citizens bring to public offices.
Day 2: Practise listening without interrupting.
Day 3: Record a sample complaint.
Day 4: Role-play responding to an angry citizen calmly.
Day 5: Prepare a complaint handling report.

Character
A public servant must be quick to listen and slow to anger.

modules.title: Public Policy, Programme Support and Community Engagement
modules.content:

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 9. Introduction to Public Policy

Teaching focus
Meaning of policy, public problems, policy decisions, policy implementation and how policies affect citizens.

Scripture
Proverbs 29:2 “When the righteous are in authority, the people rejoice: but when the wicked beareth rule, the people mourn.”

Practice
Day 1: Define public policy in simple language.
Day 2: Identify examples of public policies in education, health, roads, sanitation and agriculture.
Day 3: Discuss how good policies help people.
Day 4: Discuss how poor implementation affects citizens.
Day 5: Prepare a simple policy awareness note.

Character
Righteous leadership and good administration can bring joy and improvement to people.

Week 10. Policy Implementation and Programme Support

Teaching focus
Turning decisions into action, programme activities, roles, timelines, resources, public communication and reporting.

Scripture
Nehemiah 2:18 “Then I told them of the hand of my God which was good upon me; as also the king’s words that he had spoken unto me. And they said, Let us rise up and build.”

Practice
Day 1: Choose a simple public programme example.
Day 2: List activities needed to implement the programme.
Day 3: Assign team roles.
Day 4: Prepare a simple implementation timeline.
Day 5: Present the programme support plan.

Character
Good policy requires action. People must rise and build responsibly.

Week 11. Community Needs and Stakeholder Engagement

Teaching focus
Community needs, stakeholders, local leaders, youth groups, women groups, religious leaders, businesses and public consultations.

Scripture
Proverbs 11:14 “Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify stakeholders in a community project.
Day 2: List possible community needs.
Day 3: Prepare questions for a community consultation.
Day 4: Role-play a meeting with community representatives.
Day 5: Prepare a stakeholder engagement checklist.

Character
Good administration listens to wise counsel and includes people responsibly.

Week 12. Public Meetings, Minutes and Community Reports

Teaching focus
Meeting notice, agenda, attendance, minutes, decisions, action points, community feedback and report writing.

Scripture
Habakkuk 2:2 “And the LORD answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare a public meeting notice.
Day 2: Prepare a meeting agenda.
Day 3: Conduct a mock public meeting.
Day 4: Write minutes and action points.
Day 5: Prepare a community meeting report.

Character
Public meetings must be properly recorded so that decisions can be followed.

modules.content:
Module 4 of 7. Public Finance, Budgeting, Procurement and Resource Stewardship

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 13. Introduction to Public Finance

Teaching focus
Meaning of public funds, sources of public money, public spending, accountability, receipts, approvals and financial responsibility.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 4:2 “Moreover it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss what public funds mean.
Day 2: List examples of public spending.
Day 3: Identify why public money must be protected.
Day 4: Prepare a simple public finance responsibility chart.
Day 5: Write a reflection on financial stewardship.

Character
Public money is entrusted money. Faithfulness is required.

Week 14. Public Budgeting Awareness

Teaching focus
Meaning of budget, public needs, planned income, planned expenditure, priorities, cost control and budget monitoring.

Scripture
Luke 14:28 “For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost?”

Practice
Day 1: Identify needs for a sample community project.
Day 2: List expected costs.
Day 3: Prioritise essential and non-essential items.
Day 4: Prepare a simple public programme budget.
Day 5: Review the budget for waste and missing items.

Character
Wise public administrators count the cost before implementing programmes.

Week 15. Procurement and Public Resource Control Awareness

Teaching focus
Procurement meaning, requesting materials, supplier comparison, approval, receipts, delivery notes, stock records and avoiding favouritism.

Scripture
Proverbs 11:1 “A false balance is abomination to the LORD: but a just weight is his delight.”

Practice
Day 1: Define procurement in simple terms.
Day 2: Prepare a material request form.
Day 3: Compare sample supplier prices.
Day 4: Record items received.
Day 5: Discuss why favouritism and false prices are wrong.

Character
Public procurement must be fair, honest and transparent.

Week 16. Waste Prevention and Public Property Care

Teaching focus
Office supplies, vehicles, equipment, buildings, furniture, stationery, fuel awareness, maintenance reporting and anti-waste culture.

Scripture
John 6:12 “When they were filled, he said unto his disciples, Gather up the fragments that remain, that nothing be lost.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify public resources that are often wasted.
Day 2: Prepare a public property care checklist.
Day 3: Record sample office supplies issued.
Day 4: Write a maintenance report for a damaged item.
Day 5: Prepare a waste prevention note.

Character
Waste is poor stewardship. Public property must be protected.

modules.title: Ethics, Accountability, Rule of Law and Service Delivery
modules.content:
Module 5 of 7. Ethics, Accountability, Rule of Law and Service Delivery

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 17. Public Service Ethics

Teaching focus
Honesty, fairness, neutrality, confidentiality, respect, impartiality, integrity and public trust.

Scripture
Micah 6:8 “He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss the meaning of ethics.
Day 2: Identify ethical and unethical public service behaviours.
Day 3: Role-play fair treatment of two citizens.
Day 4: Prepare a public service ethics pledge.
Day 5: Review case studies on justice and mercy.

Character
God requires justice, mercy and humility. Public service must reflect these values.

Week 18. Anti-Corruption and Transparency

Teaching focus
Bribery, favouritism, ghost records, false receipts, missing files, misuse of office, abuse of power and transparency.

Scripture
Proverbs 10:9 “He that walketh uprightly walketh surely: but he that perverteth his ways shall be known.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss examples of corruption in public administration.
Day 2: Role-play refusing a bribe.
Day 3: Identify false records in a sample case.
Day 4: Prepare an anti-corruption checklist.
Day 5: Write a personal integrity commitment.

Character
Dishonesty may be hidden for a time, but uprightness is safer and stronger.

Week 19. Rule of Law and Administrative Justice Awareness

Teaching focus
Meaning of rule of law, fairness, rights awareness, due process, appeals, records, non-discrimination and lawful procedure.

Scripture
Deuteronomy 16:20 “That which is altogether just shalt thou follow, that thou mayest live, and inherit the land which the LORD thy God giveth thee.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss the meaning of fairness in public decisions.
Day 2: Identify examples of unfair treatment.
Day 3: Arrange steps in a simple due process exercise.
Day 4: Role-play responding to a citizen’s appeal respectfully.
Day 5: Prepare an administrative justice checklist.

Character
Public administration must pursue what is just and fair.

Week 20. Service Delivery and Public Satisfaction

Teaching focus
Service standards, timeliness, access, quality, feedback, complaint resolution and improving public services.

Scripture
Matthew 7:12 “Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify services citizens expect from public offices.
Day 2: Prepare a service delivery checklist.
Day 3: Develop a simple citizen feedback form.
Day 4: Review sample public feedback.
Day 5: Prepare a service improvement plan.

Character
Public servants should treat citizens the way they would want to be treated.

modules.title: Monitoring, Reporting, Development Planning and Public Leadership
modules.content:
Module 6 of 7. Monitoring, Reporting, Development Planning and Public Leadership

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 21. Monitoring Public Programmes

Teaching focus
Tracking activities, checking progress, identifying delays, collecting evidence, field visit awareness and monitoring reports.

Scripture
Proverbs 27:23 “Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, and look well to thy herds.”

Practice
Day 1: Review a sample public programme plan.
Day 2: Mark completed and pending activities.
Day 3: Prepare a monitoring checklist.
Day 4: Record evidence of progress.
Day 5: Prepare a monitoring report.

Character
Diligent public administrators know the state of programmes entrusted to them.

Week 22. Public Reporting and Documentation

Teaching focus
Activity reports, field reports, incident reports, monthly reports, data summaries, recommendations and report presentation.

Scripture
Proverbs 18:13 “He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare a simple activity report.
Day 2: Prepare a field visit report from a sample case.
Day 3: Prepare an incident report.
Day 4: Review reports for facts and clarity.
Day 5: Present a report to the class.

Character
Public reports must be based on facts, not assumptions.

Week 23. Development Planning and Community Projects

Teaching focus
Local development needs, project planning, priorities, public participation, timelines, budgets and implementation support.

Scripture
Proverbs 24:27 “Prepare thy work without, and make it fit for thyself in the field; and afterwards build thine house.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify one community development need.
Day 2: Prepare a simple development project goal.
Day 3: Prepare activities, timeline and roles.
Day 4: Prepare a simple budget.
Day 5: Present the community development plan.

Character
Good development requires preparation before action.

Week 24. Public Administration Enterprise and Employability Opportunities

Teaching focus
Administrative support, records support, community project support, public meeting support, civic education support and NGO field administration.

Scripture
Deuteronomy 8:18 “But thou shalt remember the LORD thy God: for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth.”

Practice
Day 1: List opportunities connected to public administration skills.
Day 2: Identify customers or organisations that need administrative support.
Day 3: Prepare a simple service description.
Day 4: Prepare a small-start budget.
Day 5: Write a public administration enterprise or employability idea note.

Character
The power to create wealth comes from God. Public administration-related enterprise must be built on honesty, order and service.

modules.title: Advanced Practice, Departmental Project and Attachment Preparation
modules.content:
Module 7 of 7. Advanced Practice, Departmental Project and Attachment Preparation

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 25. Departmental Mini-Project Planning

Teaching focus
Planning a public administration mini-project, including need, objective, stakeholders, records, budget, ethics, monitoring and final report format.

Scripture
Nehemiah 2:18 “Then I told them of the hand of my God which was good upon me; as also the king’s words that he had spoken unto me. And they said, Let us rise up and build.”

Practice
Day 1: Choose a safe departmental public administration mini-project.
Day 2: Write project goal, objectives and stakeholders.
Day 3: Prepare records, forms and budget.
Day 4: Prepare ethics, monitoring and communication checklist.
Day 5: Submit full project plan for trainer approval.

Character
Vision must move from words into organised public service action.

Week 26. Departmental Mini-Project Implementation

Teaching focus
Carrying out a supervised public administration project with records, teamwork, citizen service, communication, accountability and monitoring.

Scripture
Nehemiah 4:6 “So built we the wall; and all the wall was joined together unto the half thereof: for the people had a mind to work.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare documents, workspace and team roles.
Day 2: Begin records, community engagement, service desk or administrative support task.
Day 3: Continue assigned duties and monitor progress.
Day 4: Review records, communication, ethics and teamwork.
Day 5: Prepare project progress report.

Character
Progress comes when people have a mind to work and cooperate with discipline.

Week 27. Final Report, Evaluation and Portfolio

Teaching focus
Project completion, final report, feedback, lessons learnt, public service reflection and portfolio evidence.

Scripture
Ecclesiastes 7:8 “Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof.”

Practice
Day 1: Check whether project objectives were achieved.
Day 2: Prepare final activity report.
Day 3: Prepare feedback and lessons learnt.
Day 4: Organise public administration portfolio.
Day 5: Present final project evidence to the trainer.

Character
Starting well is important, but finishing well is better.

Week 28. Industrial Attachment Preparation

Teaching focus
Preparing for public administration placement, supervisor conduct, confidentiality, public ethics, daily logs, office records and final readiness.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:29 “Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify possible public administration attachment placements.
Day 2: Prepare personal attachment learning goals.
Day 3: Practise writing daily public administration attachment logs.
Day 4: Review public service ethics, confidentiality and workplace behaviour.
Day 5: Complete final departmental readiness assessment.

Character
Diligence opens doors. A faithful public administration trainee can serve in important institutions.

modules.title: Road Construction Orientation, Safety and Dignity of Labour
modules.content:
Module 1 of 7. Road Construction Orientation, Safety and Dignity of Labour

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 1. Introduction to Road Construction

Teaching focus
Meaning of road construction, importance of roads, types of roads, community development and dignity of road work.

Scripture
Isaiah 40:3 “The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the LORD, make straight in the desert a highway for our God.”

Practice
Day 1: Walk around the Academy environment and identify roads, paths, drains and access ways.
Day 2: List different types of roads in the community.
Day 3: Discuss how poor roads affect health, business, farming and education.
Day 4: Identify common road defects such as potholes, erosion, cracks and blocked drains.
Day 5: Write a reflection on why road construction is important for communities.

Character
Road work prepares the way for people. Trainees must understand that good roads serve families, communities and the nation.

Week 2. Road Construction Site Discipline and Safety

Teaching focus
Site rules, road work hazards, personal protective equipment, moving vehicles, traffic control and obedience to supervisors.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:3 “A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify road construction hazards from pictures, videos or supervised site examples.
Day 2: Demonstrate correct use of boots, helmets, gloves and reflective jackets where available.
Day 3: Practise safe movement around a road work area.
Day 4: Prepare a basic road site safety checklist.
Day 5: Conduct a supervised safety inspection of a practice work area.

Character
Safety is wisdom. A careless trainee can harm himself, herself, other workers, road users and the reputation of the Academy.

Week 3. Road Construction Tools and Equipment Awareness

Teaching focus
Common road construction tools, light equipment awareness, safe handling, cleaning, storage and accountability.

Scripture
Luke 16:10 “He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify common road tools such as shovel, rake, pickaxe, wheelbarrow, measuring tape, pegs and strings.
Day 2: Practise safe carrying of tools.
Day 3: Demonstrate cleaning and storage of tools after work.
Day 4: Prepare a tool issue and return register.
Day 5: Discuss why tool care is important on a road construction site.

Character
Faithfulness begins with small things. A trainee who cannot care for small tools cannot be trusted with larger equipment.

Week 4. Road Materials and Material Stewardship

Teaching focus
Sand, gravel, laterite, stones, cement, water, bitumen awareness, storage, handling and waste reduction.

Scripture
John 6:12 “When they were filled, he said unto his disciples, Gather up the fragments that remain, that nothing be lost.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify common road construction materials.
Day 2: Compare sand, gravel, laterite and stones.
Day 3: Discuss how materials are wasted on road sites.
Day 4: Demonstrate proper stockpiling and storage awareness.
Day 5: Prepare a material stewardship checklist.

Character
Waste is poor stewardship. Road materials must be handled carefully because waste increases cost and delays projects.

modules.title: Measurement, Setting-Out, Road Alignment and Site Preparation
modules.content:
Module 2 of 7. Measurement, Setting-Out, Road Alignment and Site Preparation

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 5. Basic Measurement in Road Construction

Teaching focus
Length, width, depth, measuring tape, road width, shoulder width, drain depth and accurate recording.

Scripture
Proverbs 11:1 “A false balance is abomination to the LORD: but a just weight is his delight.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify measuring tools used in simple road work.
Day 2: Practise measuring short distances with measuring tape.
Day 3: Measure road width or pathway width in a safe training area.
Day 4: Record simple measurements neatly.
Day 5: Compare group measurements and discuss errors.

Character
Accuracy is part of integrity. Wrong measurement can cause waste, poor work and unsafe roads.

Week 6. Road Alignment and Setting-Out Awareness

Teaching focus
Road lines, road edges, pegs, strings, alignment, curves awareness, straightness and simple layout.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 14:40 “Let all things be done decently and in order.”

Practice
Day 1: Demonstrate how to use pegs and string to mark a straight line.
Day 2: Mark a simple road edge in a practice area.
Day 3: Mark road width using measuring tape.
Day 4: Identify alignment errors.
Day 5: Draw a simple road layout sketch.

Character
Order matters. If the alignment is wrong at the beginning, the whole road work can be affected.

Week 7. Clearing, Grubbing and Site Preparation

Teaching focus
Clearing vegetation, removing roots, removing waste, preparing access, protecting workers and preparing for earthworks.

Scripture
Isaiah 40:3 “The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the LORD, make straight in the desert a highway for our God.”

Practice
Day 1: Inspect a practice site and identify obstacles.
Day 2: Clear light vegetation under supervision.
Day 3: Remove stones, roots, sticks and waste materials from the work area.
Day 4: Create safe access paths.
Day 5: Record site preparation activities in a site logbook.

Character
Preparation comes before construction. A good worker prepares the ground before expecting good results.

Week 8. Basic Road Levels, Slope and Water Flow Awareness

Teaching focus
Why roads need slope, basic levelling awareness, water flow, avoiding standing water and protecting the road surface.

Scripture
Proverbs 4:26 “Ponder the path of thy feet, and let all thy ways be established.”

Practice
Day 1: Observe how water flows on different ground surfaces.
Day 2: Identify areas where water collects.
Day 3: Use a simple water flow demonstration on a small soil model.
Day 4: Discuss why roads should not hold standing water.
Day 5: Record observations on slope and water movement.

Character
A wise person considers the path carefully. Road workers must think ahead so that water does not destroy the road.

modules.title: Earthworks, Soil, Drainage and Compaction
modules.content:
Module 3 of 7. Earthworks, Soil, Drainage and Compaction

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 9. Soil Types and Road Foundation Awareness

Teaching focus
Soil identification, good and poor road materials, soft ground, laterite awareness and foundation importance.

Scripture
Matthew 7:24 “Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock.”

Practice
Day 1: Collect soil samples from different areas.
Day 2: Compare soil colour, texture and moisture.
Day 3: Identify soft or weak ground areas.
Day 4: Discuss why roads need a strong foundation.
Day 5: Record soil observations in the site logbook.

Character
Strong structures need strong foundations. A trainee’s life also needs obedience, discipline and truth as a foundation.

Week 10. Excavation, Filling and Embankment Awareness

Teaching focus
Cutting, filling, embankment, safe excavation, unsuitable material and proper supervision.

Scripture
Proverbs 24:27 “Prepare thy work without, and make it fit for thyself in the field; and afterwards build thine house.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss excavation and filling using diagrams or site examples.
Day 2: Mark a small area for shallow practice excavation.
Day 3: Remove soil under supervision.
Day 4: Fill a low area with approved material under supervision.
Day 5: Record excavation and filling observations.

Character
Proper preparation prevents failure. Trainees must not rush into building before the ground is ready.

Week 11. Road Drainage and Side Drains

Teaching focus
Importance of drainage, side drains, water channels, blocked drains, erosion and maintenance.

Scripture
Isaiah 58:11 “And thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify side drains in the community or training area.
Day 2: Observe blocked and open drains where available.
Day 3: Clear a small drainage path under supervision.
Day 4: Demonstrate simple water flow in a drain model.
Day 5: Prepare a drainage maintenance checklist.

Character
Water can bless or destroy depending on how it is managed. Good drainage protects roads and communities.

Week 12. Compaction Awareness

Teaching focus
Meaning of compaction, why compaction is important, layers, moisture awareness, manual compaction and equipment awareness.

Scripture
James 1:4 “But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss loose soil and compacted soil.
Day 2: Spread soil in a small practice area.
Day 3: Add appropriate moisture under supervision.
Day 4: Compact soil manually with safe tools where available.
Day 5: Compare loose and compacted areas and record observations.

Character
Strength comes through process. Just as soil must be compacted layer by layer, character is formed through discipline and patience.

modules.content:
Module 4 of 7. Pavement Layers, Materials and Surface Awareness

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 13. Road Pavement Layers

Teaching focus
Subgrade, subbase, base course, wearing surface, layer thickness awareness and quality.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 3:10 “According to the grace of God which is given unto me, as a wise masterbuilder, I have laid the foundation.”

Practice
Day 1: Draw and label simple road pavement layers.
Day 2: Identify materials used for different layers.
Day 3: Build a small road layer model using soil, gravel and sand.
Day 4: Discuss what happens when layers are weak.
Day 5: Record lessons on road layer structure.

Character
Hidden layers matter. What people do not see can determine the strength of what they do see.

Week 14. Subgrade and Subbase Preparation Awareness

Teaching focus
Preparing road foundation, spreading materials, removing unsuitable materials, moisture control and compaction.

Scripture
Psalm 11:3 “If the foundations be destroyed, what can the righteous do?”

Practice
Day 1: Inspect a practice ground for weak materials.
Day 2: Spread selected material over a small area.
Day 3: Level the material under supervision.
Day 4: Compact the material manually where safe.
Day 5: Complete a subgrade and subbase quality checklist.

Character
Foundations matter. Poor hidden work can later cause visible failure.

Week 15. Base Course and Aggregate Awareness

Teaching focus
Aggregates, stone sizes, base course function, material quality, spreading and compaction awareness.

Scripture
Proverbs 24:4 “And by knowledge shall the chambers be filled with all precious and pleasant riches.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify different aggregate sizes where available.
Day 2: Discuss good and poor aggregate quality.
Day 3: Spread aggregate in a small training area.
Day 4: Discuss compaction and surface strength.
Day 5: Record aggregate observations and uses.

Character
Knowledge improves quality. Trainees must understand materials before using them.

Week 16. Asphalt, Bitumen and Concrete Road Awareness

Teaching focus
Asphalt roads, bitumen awareness, concrete roads, hot material safety, surface finishing and curing awareness.

Scripture
Ecclesiastes 9:10 “Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss the difference between earth roads, asphalt roads and concrete roads.
Day 2: Identify asphalt and bitumen through pictures, samples or supervised demonstration.
Day 3: Discuss safety around hot asphalt and bitumen.
Day 4: Observe concrete road surface or concrete sample where available.
Day 5: Record advantages and disadvantages of different road surfaces.

Character
Every surface must be finished with care. Work should be done with seriousness and excellence.

modules.title: Road Maintenance, Repairs and Quality Control
modules.content:
Module 5 of 7. Road Maintenance, Repairs and Quality Control

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 17. Common Road Defects

Teaching focus
Potholes, cracks, rutting, erosion, shoulder damage, blocked drains and causes of road failure.

Scripture
Song of Solomon 2:15 “Take us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vines: for our vines have tender grapes.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify common road defects from pictures or safe site observation.
Day 2: Discuss causes of potholes.
Day 3: Discuss how blocked drains damage roads.
Day 4: Prepare a road defect observation sheet.
Day 5: Record defects found in a safe training area.

Character
Small problems can become big failures if ignored. Early correction prevents greater damage.

Week 18. Pothole Repair Awareness

Teaching focus
Pothole cleaning, cutting awareness, filling material, compaction, safety signs and traffic control.

Scripture
Nehemiah 2:17 “Then said I unto them, Ye see the distress that we are in, how Jerusalem lieth waste: come, and let us build up the wall.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss pothole repair steps using pictures or demonstration.
Day 2: Clean a small simulated pothole area under supervision.
Day 3: Prepare filling material awareness.
Day 4: Compact a simulated repair area under supervision.
Day 5: Record repair process and safety requirements.

Character
Responsible people do not only complain about damage. They participate in repair and restoration.

Week 19. Road Shoulder and Drain Maintenance

Teaching focus
Road shoulders, edge protection, drainage cleaning, erosion control and routine maintenance.

Scripture
Proverbs 27:23 “Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, and look well to thy herds.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify road shoulders and drains.
Day 2: Clear light debris from a safe drainage area under supervision.
Day 3: Observe shoulder damage and erosion.
Day 4: Prepare a maintenance checklist.
Day 5: Write a simple road maintenance report.

Character
Responsible workers inspect what is entrusted to them. Regular care prevents major damage.

Week 20. Road Quality Control and Inspection

Teaching focus
Checking alignment, levels, material quality, compaction, drainage, workmanship and reporting defects.

Scripture
2 Corinthians 13:5 “Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss what quality means in road construction.
Day 2: Inspect a small training area using a quality checklist.
Day 3: Identify poor workmanship from examples.
Day 4: Prepare a simple quality report.
Day 5: Present inspection findings to the trainer.

Character
Inspection is not punishment. It helps reveal weaknesses that must be corrected.

modules.title: Traffic Control, Project Management, Costing and Enterprise
modules.content:
Module 6 of 7. Traffic Control, Project Management, Costing and Enterprise

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 21. Traffic Control and Road User Safety

Teaching focus
Traffic awareness, warning signs, cones, flagging awareness, pedestrian safety and protecting workers.

Scripture
Romans 12:18 “If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss dangers of working near traffic.
Day 2: Identify warning signs, cones and barriers where available.
Day 3: Practise setting up a simple safe work zone model.
Day 4: Role-play communicating with road users respectfully.
Day 5: Prepare a traffic safety checklist.

Character
Road workers must protect lives and maintain peace with road users, drivers and communities.

Week 22. Road Work Records and Daily Site Logs

Teaching focus
Site diary, attendance, material records, tool records, work progress, weather notes and safety records.

Scripture
Habakkuk 2:2 “And the LORD answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.”

Practice
Day 1: Create a simple road work site logbook.
Day 2: Record tools and materials used for a sample task.
Day 3: Record weather and work progress.
Day 4: Prepare a simple safety observation note.
Day 5: Review records for accuracy and neatness.

Character
Clear records protect accountability. What is not recorded may be forgotten or disputed.

Week 23. Road Construction Costing and Resource Planning

Teaching focus
Material list, labour cost awareness, transport, equipment hire awareness, waste allowance and simple costing.

Scripture
Luke 14:28 “For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost?”

Practice
Day 1: List materials for a simple drainage or road repair task.
Day 2: Estimate quantities at awareness level.
Day 3: Add labour and transport awareness costs.
Day 4: Discuss how waste affects project cost.
Day 5: Prepare a simple road work cost sheet.

Character
Planning and costing prevent waste. A wise worker counts the cost before beginning.

Week 24. Road Construction Enterprise Opportunities

Teaching focus
Small road maintenance services, drainage cleaning, material supply, labour groups, tool hiring, record keeping and ethical enterprise.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:1 “A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold.”

Practice
Day 1: List road construction and maintenance enterprise opportunities.
Day 2: Identify customers for one road-related service.
Day 3: Prepare a simple service description.
Day 4: Role-play customer communication.
Day 5: Write a simple road construction enterprise idea note.

Character
A good name is valuable. In road work, poor quality and dishonesty can destroy future opportunities.

modules.title: Advanced Practice, Departmental Project and Attachment Preparation
modules.content:
Module 7 of 7. Advanced Practice, Departmental Project and Attachment Preparation

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 25. Departmental Mini-Project Planning

Teaching focus
Planning a safe road-related mini-project, roles, tools, materials, cost, traffic safety and expected outcome.

Scripture
Nehemiah 2:18 “Then I told them of the hand of my God which was good upon me; as also the king’s words that he had spoken unto me. And they said, Let us rise up and build.”

Practice
Day 1: Choose a safe road-related departmental mini-project.
Day 2: Write project goals and expected results.
Day 3: Prepare a tool and material list.
Day 4: Assign team roles and safety officers.
Day 5: Submit project plan for trainer approval.

Character
Vision must become organised action. Trainees must rise and build responsibly.

Week 26. Departmental Mini-Project Implementation

Teaching focus
Carrying out a supervised road-related project with safety, teamwork, records and quality checks.

Scripture
Nehemiah 4:6 “So built we the wall; and all the wall was joined together unto the half thereof: for the people had a mind to work.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare project area and tools.
Day 2: Begin project implementation under supervision.
Day 3: Continue assigned tasks and record progress.
Day 4: Check safety, quality and teamwork.
Day 5: Clean the area and review progress.

Character
Progress comes when people are willing to work together.

Week 27. Final Practical Demonstration and Portfolio

Teaching focus
Demonstrating tool use, measurement, road layer awareness, drainage awareness, records, safety and project evidence.

Scripture
2 Timothy 2:15 “Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed.”

Practice
Day 1: Demonstrate tool identification and safe handling.
Day 2: Demonstrate measurement and marking of a practice road section.
Day 3: Demonstrate drainage or compaction awareness under supervision.
Day 4: Organise road construction portfolio.
Day 5: Present practical evidence to trainer.

Character
A trained worker should not be ashamed. Diligence, skill and discipline prepare trainees for approval.

Week 28. Industrial Attachment Preparation

Teaching focus
Preparing for road construction placement, supervisor conduct, site safety, traffic awareness, daily logs and workplace expectations.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:29 “Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify possible road construction attachment placements.
Day 2: Prepare personal attachment learning goals.
Day 3: Practise writing daily road construction attachment logs.
Day 4: Review site safety, traffic control and workplace behaviour.
Day 5: Complete final departmental readiness assessment.

Character
Diligence opens doors. A faithful trainee can be trusted with greater responsibility.

modules.title: Survey Orientation, Measurement and Site Discipline
modules.content:
Module 1 of 7. Survey Orientation, Measurement and Site Discipline

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 1. Introduction to Survey and Site Management

Teaching focus
Meaning of surveying, meaning of site management, importance of measurement, site order and the role of survey and site support workers.

Scripture
Proverbs 24:3 “Through wisdom is an house builded; and by understanding it is established.”

Practice
Day 1: Walk around the Academy environment and identify buildings, roads, drains, open spaces and site features.
Day 2: Discuss why construction projects need measurement and order.
Day 3: Identify people involved in site work, such as surveyors, engineers, site supervisors, foremen, masons, carpenters and labourers.
Day 4: Discuss what can go wrong when a site is poorly measured or poorly managed.
Day 5: Write a reflection on why wisdom and understanding are important in survey and site management.

Character
A wise worker does not guess. Survey and site management teach trainees to think, measure, plan and act with understanding.

Week 2. Site Discipline, Safety and Professional Conduct

Teaching focus
Site rules, punctuality, protective equipment, safe movement, obedience to supervisors and professional behaviour.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:3 “A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify common site hazards such as open holes, sharp objects, falling materials and moving vehicles.
Day 2: Demonstrate correct use of boots, helmets, gloves and reflective jackets where available.
Day 3: Practise safe movement around a site.
Day 4: Prepare a basic site safety checklist.
Day 5: Conduct a supervised site safety inspection.

Character
Safety is wisdom. A trainee who ignores danger can harm people and damage the project.

Week 3. Basic Measurement Tools and Their Uses

Teaching focus
Measuring tape, pegs, strings, spirit level, plumb bob awareness, ranging rods awareness, notebooks and tool care.

Scripture
Luke 16:10 “He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify basic measurement and site management tools.
Day 2: Practise handling measuring tape properly.
Day 3: Practise placing pegs and tying strings.
Day 4: Clean and store tools after use.
Day 5: Complete a tool issue and return register.

Character
Tool care is a test of responsibility. Faithfulness in small tools prepares trainees for greater trust.

Week 4. Units of Measurement and Accurate Recording

Teaching focus
Metres, centimetres, millimetres, simple conversion awareness, neat recording and avoiding guessing.

Scripture
Proverbs 11:1 “A false balance is abomination to the LORD: but a just weight is his delight.”

Practice
Day 1: Practise reading measurements on a tape.
Day 2: Measure simple objects and record results.
Day 3: Convert simple metres to centimetres at awareness level.
Day 4: Compare measurements from different groups.
Day 5: Review common measurement errors and correct them.

Character
Accuracy is part of integrity. A trainee must not guess, exaggerate or falsify measurements.

modules.title: Distance Measurement, Lines, Angles and Setting-Out Awareness
modules.content:
Module 2 of 7. Distance Measurement, Lines, Angles and Setting-Out Awareness

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 5. Measuring Distance and Marking Points

Teaching focus
Measuring short distances, long distances at awareness level, marking points, recording points and checking work.

Scripture
2 Corinthians 13:5 “Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves.”

Practice
Day 1: Measure a short distance between two points.
Day 2: Mark points with pegs.
Day 3: Measure the same distance twice and compare results.
Day 4: Record point names and distances in a notebook.
Day 5: Review errors and repeat the measurement correctly.

Character
Good workers check their work. Examination helps correct errors before they become serious.

Week 6. Straight Lines, Pegs and Strings

Teaching focus
Creating straight lines, maintaining alignment, protecting line marks and understanding why straight lines matter.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 14:40 “Let all things be done decently and in order.”

Practice
Day 1: Demonstrate how to use pegs and strings.
Day 2: Mark a straight line on the ground.
Day 3: Check line alignment by sighting.
Day 4: Protect marked lines from disturbance.
Day 5: Record the purpose of line marking in site work.

Character
Order begins with correct lines. A confused line can create confused work.

Week 7. Right Angles and Simple Layout Awareness

Teaching focus
Right angle awareness, rectangular layout, diagonal checking, simple room layout and accuracy.

Scripture
Amos 7:7 “Behold, the Lord stood upon a wall made by a plumbline, with a plumbline in his hand.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss right angles using a simple room or block.
Day 2: Mark a rectangular layout with pegs and strings.
Day 3: Check opposite sides.
Day 4: Check diagonals at awareness level.
Day 5: Correct a simple layout error under supervision.

Character
God values uprightness. Trainees must learn to build straight and live straight.

Week 8. Setting-Out for Buildings and Roads Awareness

Teaching focus
Building lines, road edges, reference points, site boundaries awareness, protecting marks and reporting errors.

Scripture
Proverbs 4:26 “Ponder the path of thy feet, and let all thy ways be established.”

Practice
Day 1: Observe a simple building setting-out example.
Day 2: Observe a simple road edge marking example.
Day 3: Mark a small practice building line.
Day 4: Mark a small practice road edge.
Day 5: Draw a simple setting-out sketch.

Character
A wise person considers the path carefully. Site work must be established through careful marking and planning.

modules.title: Levelling Awareness, Slope, Drainage and Site Observation
modules.content:
Module 3 of 7. Levelling Awareness, Slope, Drainage and Site Observation

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 9. Understanding Levels and Slopes

Teaching focus
Meaning of level, slope, high ground, low ground, water flow and why levels matter in buildings and roads.

Scripture
Isaiah 40:4 “Every valley shall be exalted, and every mountain and hill shall be made low: and the crooked shall be made straight, and the rough places plain.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify high and low points in the training area.
Day 2: Observe how water moves on sloping ground.
Day 3: Use a simple model to show slope and flow.
Day 4: Identify areas where water can collect.
Day 5: Record observations on levels and drainage.

Character
Uneven ground affects construction. In life, rough places must also be corrected through discipline and growth.

Week 10. Spirit Level and Simple Levelling Tools

Teaching focus
Spirit level use, water level awareness, level checking, slope observation and safe tool handling.

Scripture
Proverbs 4:7 “Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify a spirit level and explain its use.
Day 2: Check whether a surface is level.
Day 3: Observe simple water level demonstration.
Day 4: Compare level and sloping surfaces.
Day 5: Record levelling observations in the site notebook.

Character
Understanding matters. Trainees should not only use tools, they should know why the tools are used.

Week 11. Drainage Observation and Water Flow Management

Teaching focus
Drainage, standing water, side drains, slope direction, erosion and drainage reporting.

Scripture
Isaiah 58:11 “And thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify drains, gutters or water channels in the training area.
Day 2: Observe blocked and open drainage paths.
Day 3: Mark water flow direction on a simple sketch.
Day 4: Clear light debris from a safe drainage area under supervision.
Day 5: Prepare a drainage observation report.

Character
Water must be guided properly. Poor drainage can damage buildings, roads and communities.

Week 12. Site Observation and Defect Reporting

Teaching focus
Observing site conditions, identifying hazards, defects, wrong levels, poor access and simple reporting.

Scripture
Proverbs 27:23 “Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, and look well to thy herds.”

Practice
Day 1: Inspect a training site and identify visible concerns.
Day 2: Record site hazards.
Day 3: Record drainage or access problems.
Day 4: Prepare a simple site observation report.
Day 5: Present observations to the trainer.

Character
Responsible people observe what is entrusted to them. Neglect leads to loss.

modules.content:
Module 4 of 7. Site Organisation, Records, Materials and Labour Management

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 13. Site Organisation and Layout

Teaching focus
Site entrance, storage areas, tool area, material area, waste area, work zones, movement paths and safety.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 14:40 “Let all things be done decently and in order.”

Practice
Day 1: Draw a simple site organisation plan.
Day 2: Mark tool and material areas in a practice site.
Day 3: Identify unsafe site organisation problems.
Day 4: Arrange tools and materials properly.
Day 5: Review site order using a checklist.

Character
Order improves safety, speed and quality. A disorganised site delays work and creates danger.

Week 14. Tool Control and Equipment Records

Teaching focus
Tool issue, tool return, damaged tools, missing tools, accountability and storage.

Scripture
Luke 16:10 “He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much.”

Practice
Day 1: Create a simple tool register.
Day 2: Issue tools to groups using the register.
Day 3: Check tools after practical work.
Day 4: Record damaged or missing tools.
Day 5: Review tool accountability lessons.

Character
Faithfulness can be seen in how a trainee handles another person’s property.

Week 15. Material Control and Waste Reduction

Teaching focus
Material delivery, storage, usage records, waste tracking, material protection and reporting.

Scripture
John 6:12 “When they were filled, he said unto his disciples, Gather up the fragments that remain, that nothing be lost.”

Practice
Day 1: Create a simple material record sheet.
Day 2: Record sample materials received.
Day 3: Record materials used for a small task.
Day 4: Identify how materials are wasted on sites.
Day 5: Prepare a material stewardship checklist.

Character
Waste is poor stewardship. Site managers must protect materials and reduce loss.

Week 16. Labour Attendance and Daily Site Reports

Teaching focus
Attendance records, daily work records, weather notes, tasks completed, problems faced and supervisor reporting.

Scripture
Habakkuk 2:2 “And the LORD answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.”

Practice
Day 1: Create a simple labour attendance sheet.
Day 2: Record sample worker attendance.
Day 3: Write a simple daily site report.
Day 4: Record weather and work progress.
Day 5: Review reports for neatness and truthfulness.

Character
Clear reporting prevents confusion. Written records help supervisors make good decisions.

modules.title: Quality Control, Site Communication and Supervision Awareness
modules.content:
Module 5 of 7. Quality Control, Site Communication and Supervision Awareness

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 17. Introduction to Quality Control

Teaching focus
Meaning of quality, why inspection matters, common site defects, correction and rework.

Scripture
Colossians 3:23 “And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss what quality means in building and road work.
Day 2: Identify examples of good and poor workmanship from pictures or safe samples.
Day 3: Prepare a simple quality checklist.
Day 4: Inspect a small practice task.
Day 5: Write a simple quality observation report.

Character
Quality matters because work should be done heartily as unto the Lord.

Week 18. Checking Work Against Instructions

Teaching focus
Following drawings, measurements, supervisor instructions, work specifications at awareness level and avoiding guesswork.

Scripture
Proverbs 19:20 “Hear counsel, and receive instruction, that thou mayest be wise in thy latter end.”

Practice
Day 1: Read a simple instruction for a practical task.
Day 2: Compare the task with the instruction.
Day 3: Identify where instructions were followed or missed.
Day 4: Correct simple errors under supervision.
Day 5: Record lessons on following instructions.

Character
Teachability protects workers from errors. A wise trainee listens before acting.

Week 19. Site Communication and Reporting Problems

Teaching focus
Respectful communication, progress reporting, hazard reporting, delay reporting and supervisor updates.

Scripture
Ephesians 4:25 “Wherefore putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour.”

Practice
Day 1: Practise giving a simple site update.
Day 2: Practise reporting a hazard respectfully.
Day 3: Practise reporting a material shortage.
Day 4: Practise reporting a delay without blaming others.
Day 5: Write a sample site communication note.

Character
Truthful communication builds trust. Hiding problems can damage the whole project.

Week 20. Supervision Awareness and Team Coordination

Teaching focus
Role of site supervisor, coordinating tasks, assigning simple roles, monitoring progress and teamwork.

Scripture
Ecclesiastes 4:9 “Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss the role of a site supervisor.
Day 2: Assign simple team roles for a practical task.
Day 3: Monitor progress using a checklist.
Day 4: Review teamwork strengths and weaknesses.
Day 5: Prepare a simple team coordination report.

Character
Good teamwork increases productivity. Site management requires people to work together with respect.

modules.title: Site Planning, Cost Awareness, Procurement and Enterprise
modules.content:
Module 6 of 7. Site Planning, Cost Awareness, Procurement and Enterprise

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 21. Daily Work Planning and Task Scheduling

Teaching focus
Daily work plan, task priority, time management, assigning responsibilities and reviewing progress.

Scripture
Proverbs 21:5 “The thoughts of the diligent tend only to plenteousness; but of every one that is hasty only to want.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare a simple daily work plan.
Day 2: List tasks in order of priority.
Day 3: Assign roles for a group practical task.
Day 4: Monitor task completion.
Day 5: Review the day’s plan and record lessons.

Character
Diligent planning produces better results. Hasty work produces waste.

Week 22. Simple Site Cost Awareness

Teaching focus
Materials, labour, transport, tools, equipment hire awareness, waste cost and simple cost records.

Scripture
Luke 14:28 “For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost?”

Practice
Day 1: List materials for a small site task.
Day 2: Estimate simple material quantities at awareness level.
Day 3: Add labour and transport awareness costs.
Day 4: Discuss how waste increases cost.
Day 5: Prepare a simple cost record.

Character
A wise worker counts the cost. Poor costing can lead to abandoned projects and wasted resources.

Week 23. Procurement and Inventory Awareness

Teaching focus
Requesting materials, receiving materials, checking quantity, storage, stock records and preventing theft.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 4:2 “Moreover it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare a sample material request form.
Day 2: Receive sample materials and check quantity.
Day 3: Record materials in a stock sheet.
Day 4: Issue materials for a sample task.
Day 5: Compare stock balance and discuss accountability.

Character
Site resources must be handled faithfully. Stewardship requires honesty and careful records.

Week 24. Survey and Site Management Enterprise Opportunities

Teaching focus
Site support services, measurement support, record keeping, tool control, material inventory, safety monitoring and ethical enterprise.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:1 “A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold.”

Practice
Day 1: List enterprise opportunities in survey and site support.
Day 2: Identify customers for one site management support service.
Day 3: Prepare a simple service description.
Day 4: Role-play customer or contractor communication.
Day 5: Prepare a simple enterprise idea note.

Character
A good name is valuable. Site management enterprise must be built on trust, accuracy and honesty.

modules.title: Advanced Practice, Departmental Project and Attachment Preparation
modules.content:
Module 7 of 7. Advanced Practice, Departmental Project and Attachment Preparation

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 25. Departmental Mini-Project Planning

Teaching focus
Planning a simple survey or site management project, roles, tools, records, safety and expected results.

Scripture
Nehemiah 2:18 “Then I told them of the hand of my God which was good upon me; as also the king’s words that he had spoken unto me. And they said, Let us rise up and build.”

Practice
Day 1: Choose a safe departmental mini-project.
Day 2: Write project goals and expected results.
Day 3: Prepare tools, records and safety checklist.
Day 4: Assign team roles and reporting duties.
Day 5: Submit project plan for trainer approval.

Character
Vision must become organised action. Trainees must rise and build responsibly.

Week 26. Departmental Mini-Project Implementation

Teaching focus
Carrying out a supervised survey or site management project with safety, records, teamwork and quality checks.

Scripture
Nehemiah 4:6 “So built we the wall; and all the wall was joined together unto the half thereof: for the people had a mind to work.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare the project area and tools.
Day 2: Begin measurement or site organisation task under supervision.
Day 3: Continue assigned tasks and record progress.
Day 4: Check safety, quality, records and teamwork.
Day 5: Clean the area and review progress.

Character
Progress comes when people have a mind to work and a willingness to cooperate.

Week 27. Final Practical Demonstration and Portfolio

Teaching focus
Demonstrating measurement, setting-out awareness, site organisation, records, safety and project evidence.

Scripture
2 Timothy 2:15 “Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed.”

Practice
Day 1: Demonstrate tool identification and safe handling.
Day 2: Demonstrate measurement and point marking.
Day 3: Demonstrate simple setting-out or site organisation under supervision.
Day 4: Organise survey and site management portfolio.
Day 5: Present practical evidence to trainer.

Character
A trained worker should not be ashamed. Diligence, skill and discipline prepare trainees for approval.

Week 28. Industrial Attachment Preparation

Teaching focus
Preparing for survey or site management placement, supervisor conduct, site safety, daily logs, workplace expectations and final readiness.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:29 “Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify possible attachment placements.
Day 2: Prepare personal attachment learning goals.
Day 3: Practise writing daily survey or site management attachment logs.
Day 4: Review site safety, reporting and workplace behaviour.
Day 5: Complete final departmental readiness assessment.

Character
Diligence opens doors. A faithful trainee can be trusted with greater responsibility.
