modules.title: Welding Orientation, Safety and Tool Identification
modules.content:
Module 1 of 7. Welding Orientation, Safety and Tool Identification

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 1. Introduction to Welding and Fabrication

Teaching focus
Meaning of welding, meaning of fabrication, importance of metal work, common products made by welders and dignity of technical work.

Scripture
Exodus 31:3 “And I have filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship.”

Practice
Day 1: Walk around the workshop and identify welding and fabrication areas.
Day 2: List common metal products in the community, such as gates, doors, windows, railings, tanks and frames.
Day 3: Discuss why strong metal work is important for safety and service.
Day 4: Identify different workers in a welding workshop.
Day 5: Write a reflection on why skill must be developed with wisdom.

Character
Skill is valuable, but skill without wisdom and discipline is dangerous.

Week 2. Welding Workshop Safety

Teaching focus
Fire hazards, electric shock, arc eye, burns, fumes, sparks, sharp metal, grinder danger and workshop conduct.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:3 “A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify welding workshop hazards.
Day 2: Demonstrate correct use of welding helmet, gloves, apron and boots.
Day 3: Identify safe and unsafe workshop behaviour.
Day 4: Prepare a welding workshop safety checklist.
Day 5: Conduct a supervised safety inspection.

Character
Safety is wisdom. A careless trainee can cause fire, injury or blindness.

Week 3. Welding Tools and Equipment Identification

Teaching focus
Welding machine, electrode holder, earth clamp, cables, electrodes, grinder, clamps, hammer, chipping hammer, wire brush and measuring tools.

Scripture
Luke 16:10 “He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify welding tools and state their uses.
Day 2: Identify parts of a welding machine at awareness level.
Day 3: Identify grinder parts and discuss grinder safety.
Day 4: Clean and arrange tools after use.
Day 5: Complete a tool issue and return register.

Character
Tool care shows responsibility. A trainee who misuses tools cannot be trusted with equipment.

Week 4. Fire Prevention and Workshop Order

Teaching focus
Fire extinguishers, sparks, flammable materials, gas safety awareness, cable arrangement, ventilation and workshop cleanliness.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 14:40 “Let all things be done decently and in order.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify fire risks in a welding workshop.
Day 2: Locate fire extinguisher and discuss its importance.
Day 3: Remove flammable materials from a practice work area.
Day 4: Arrange cables and tools safely.
Day 5: Prepare a workshop order and fire prevention checklist.

Character
Order prevents danger. A disorganised welding workshop can quickly become unsafe.

modules.title: Measurement, Marking, Cutting and Metal Preparation
modules.content:
Module 2 of 7. Measurement, Marking, Cutting and Metal Preparation

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 5. Basic Measurement in Fabrication

Teaching focus
Length, width, thickness, measuring tape, square, marking tools, accuracy and recording dimensions.

Scripture
Proverbs 11:1 “A false balance is abomination to the LORD: but a just weight is his delight.”

Practice
Day 1: Practise reading measurements on a tape.
Day 2: Measure metal pieces and record dimensions.
Day 3: Use a square to check right angles.
Day 4: Compare group measurements and correct errors.
Day 5: Prepare a simple measurement record.

Character
Accuracy is part of honesty. Wrong measurement can waste materials and spoil the job.

Week 6. Marking, Cutting Lines and Material Preparation

Teaching focus
Marking metal, cutting lines, checking twice before cutting, material preparation and avoiding waste.

Scripture
Proverbs 24:27 “Prepare thy work without, and make it fit for thyself in the field; and afterwards build thine house.”

Practice
Day 1: Mark straight cutting lines on sample metal pieces.
Day 2: Check measurements before cutting.
Day 3: Prepare metal surfaces by cleaning dirt or rust.
Day 4: Arrange metal pieces according to marked dimensions.
Day 5: Write a reflection on why preparation matters.

Character
Preparation prevents waste. A trainee must not rush into cutting or welding without checking.

Week 7. Cutting Tools and Cutting Safety Awareness

Teaching focus
Hacksaw, angle grinder, cutting disc, gas cutting awareness, sharp edges, sparks, eye protection and supervised cutting.

Scripture
Proverbs 19:20 “Hear counsel, and receive instruction, that thou mayest be wise in thy latter end.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify cutting tools and state their uses.
Day 2: Demonstrate safe use of hacksaw.
Day 3: Observe angle grinder cutting demonstration under supervision.
Day 4: Identify cutting hazards.
Day 5: Prepare a cutting safety checklist.

Character
Instruction protects life. A trainee must never cut metal without permission and supervision.

Week 8. Grinding, Edge Preparation and Cleaning

Teaching focus
Grinding disc, grinding sparks, removing burrs, edge preparation, cleaning weld area and safe finishing.

Scripture
Proverbs 4:7 “Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify grinding tools and safety equipment.
Day 2: Observe grinding demonstration under supervision.
Day 3: Practise filing or smoothing sharp edges where safe.
Day 4: Clean metal surfaces before welding.
Day 5: Record grinding safety rules.

Character
Trainees should understand why metal is cleaned and prepared before welding. Good preparation improves quality.

modules.title: Welding Process Awareness and Basic Supervised Practice
modules.content:
Module 3 of 7. Welding Process Awareness and Basic Supervised Practice

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 9. Introduction to Arc Welding

Teaching focus
Meaning of arc welding, welding machine, electrode, earth clamp, current awareness, arc light danger and supervised practice.

Scripture
Colossians 3:23 “And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify arc welding equipment.
Day 2: Discuss the danger of looking at the welding arc without protection.
Day 3: Observe trainer demonstration of arc welding.
Day 4: Practise safe positioning and helmet use without welding.
Day 5: Record arc welding safety and preparation steps.

Character
Welding must be done with seriousness. Careless work can injure people and weaken structures.

Week 10. Electrode Handling and Welding Position Awareness

Teaching focus
Electrode types at basic level, dry storage, electrode holder, work angle, travel direction, flat position and safe handling.

Scripture
2 Timothy 2:15 “Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify electrodes and discuss their purpose.
Day 2: Demonstrate safe electrode holder handling.
Day 3: Practise work angle using dry run movement.
Day 4: Observe flat position welding demonstration.
Day 5: Prepare an electrode handling note.

Character
A good worker studies and practises. Welding skill grows through learning, correction and discipline.

Week 11. Tack Welding and Simple Bead Practice

Teaching focus
Tack welding, bead laying, arc control awareness, speed awareness, slag, chipping and wire brushing.

Scripture
Ecclesiastes 9:10 “Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might.”

Practice
Day 1: Observe tack welding demonstration.
Day 2: Practise clamping two metal pieces.
Day 3: Practise tack welding under close supervision where safe.
Day 4: Observe simple bead welding demonstration.
Day 5: Clean slag with chipping hammer and wire brush under supervision.

Character
Work must be done with focus and seriousness. Small welds still require attention.

Week 12. Common Weld Defects and Quality Awareness

Teaching focus
Weak welds, cracks, porosity, undercut, poor penetration, excessive slag, wrong fit-up and quality checking.

Scripture
2 Corinthians 13:5 “Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify good and poor welds from samples or pictures.
Day 2: Discuss causes of poor welds.
Day 3: Inspect practice welds under trainer guidance.
Day 4: Prepare a weld quality checklist.
Day 5: Record personal areas for improvement.

Character
Inspection helps reveal weakness. A trainee must be willing to correct poor work.

modules.title: Joint Preparation, Fabrication and Assembly
modules.content:
Module 4 of 7. Joint Preparation, Fabrication and Assembly

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 13. Types of Joints in Welding

Teaching focus
Butt joint, lap joint, T-joint, corner joint, edge joint, joint preparation and uses.

Scripture
Ecclesiastes 4:9 “Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify different joint types from samples or diagrams.
Day 2: Arrange metal pieces for lap and butt joints.
Day 3: Arrange metal pieces for T-joint and corner joint.
Day 4: Clamp joints in position.
Day 5: Draw and label common joint types.

Character
Joining materials properly teaches teamwork. Strength increases when parts are joined correctly.

Week 14. Clamping, Alignment and Squareness

Teaching focus
Clamps, vice, square, alignment, distortion awareness, checking before welding and correcting fit-up.

Scripture
Amos 7:7 “Behold, the Lord stood upon a wall made by a plumbline, with a plumbline in his hand.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify clamps and vice.
Day 2: Clamp two metal pieces safely.
Day 3: Check alignment using a square.
Day 4: Correct poor fit-up under supervision.
Day 5: Complete an alignment checklist.

Character
God values straightness. Trainees must build straight and live uprightly.

Week 15. Simple Frame Fabrication

Teaching focus
Reading simple sketches, measuring, cutting, arranging, tack welding, checking square and finishing.

Scripture
Habakkuk 2:2 “And the LORD answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.”

Practice
Day 1: Read a simple frame sketch.
Day 2: Prepare a material list for the frame.
Day 3: Measure and mark pieces.
Day 4: Arrange and clamp pieces.
Day 5: Tack weld or observe tack welding under supervision.

Character
Clear drawings and records help workers understand the work and avoid confusion.

Week 16. Gates, Windows, Railings and Metal Furniture Awareness

Teaching focus
Common fabrication products, design awareness, strength, finishing, hinges, handles, customer needs and quality.

Scripture
Proverbs 24:3 “Through wisdom is an house builded; and by understanding it is established.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify common fabricated products in the community.
Day 2: Discuss what makes a gate or window strong and safe.
Day 3: Draw a simple window guard or small frame design.
Day 4: Prepare a basic material list.
Day 5: Discuss customer needs and quality expectations.

Character
Good fabrication requires wisdom, understanding and attention to the needs of the user.

modules.title: Repair Work, Finishing and Workshop Productivity
modules.content:
Module 5 of 7. Repair Work, Finishing and Workshop Productivity

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 17. Metal Repair Awareness

Teaching focus
Identifying cracks, broken joints, rusted parts, reinforcement, patching awareness and repair safety.

Scripture
Nehemiah 2:17 “Then said I unto them, Ye see the distress that we are in, how Jerusalem lieth waste: come, and let us build up the wall.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify broken metal parts from samples or pictures.
Day 2: Discuss repair options at awareness level.
Day 3: Clean a repair area under supervision.
Day 4: Prepare a repair observation report.
Day 5: Discuss when repairs are unsafe and must be rejected.

Character
Responsible people help repair what is broken, but repair must be done safely and honestly.

Week 18. Grinding, Finishing and Surface Preparation for Painting

Teaching focus
Grinding welds, smoothing edges, removing slag, rust protection, primer and painting awareness.

Scripture
Psalm 90:17 “And let the beauty of the LORD our God be upon us: and establish thou the work of our hands upon us.”

Practice
Day 1: Inspect welded work for sharp edges.
Day 2: Observe grinding and finishing demonstration.
Day 3: Smooth edges under supervision where safe.
Day 4: Clean metal surface for painting.
Day 5: Discuss how finishing adds beauty and value.

Character
Good finishing shows care. Trainees should desire God to establish the work of their hands.

Week 19. Workshop Productivity and Waste Reduction

Teaching focus
Work planning, material cutting list, offcut management, time use, teamwork and reducing mistakes.

Scripture
John 6:12 “When they were filled, he said unto his disciples, Gather up the fragments that remain, that nothing be lost.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare a cutting list for a simple project.
Day 2: Sort usable offcuts from waste.
Day 3: Record materials used for a sample task.
Day 4: Discuss how wrong cutting wastes money.
Day 5: Prepare a waste reduction checklist.

Character
Waste is poor stewardship. A responsible welder protects materials.

Week 20. Job Cards, Workshop Records and Customer Communication

Teaching focus
Customer request, job description, material list, labour record, delivery date, cost awareness and respectful communication.

Scripture
Ephesians 4:25 “Wherefore putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour.”

Practice
Day 1: Create a simple welding job card.
Day 2: Record customer request for a sample gate or frame.
Day 3: Prepare a material list.
Day 4: Prepare a simple work progress report.
Day 5: Role-play explaining job progress to a customer.

Character
Truthful communication builds trust. A welder must not lie about materials, progress or cost.

modules.title: Costing, Enterprise, Workshop Management and Ethics
modules.content:
Module 6 of 7. Costing, Enterprise, Workshop Management and Ethics

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 21. Material Costing and Simple Quotation

Teaching focus
Metal prices, electrodes, discs, labour, transport, painting, overheads and honest quotation.

Scripture
Luke 14:28 “For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost?”

Practice
Day 1: List materials needed for a simple metal frame.
Day 2: Estimate material cost using sample prices.
Day 3: Add labour and finishing cost awareness.
Day 4: Prepare a simple quotation.
Day 5: Review quotation for honesty and completeness.

Character
Wise workers count the cost. Poor costing leads to loss, conflict and abandoned jobs.

Week 22. Workshop Organisation and Inventory Control

Teaching focus
Tool storage, electrode storage, metal stock, offcuts, discs, gas cylinder storage awareness and inventory records.

Scripture
1 Corinthians 14:40 “Let all things be done decently and in order.”

Practice
Day 1: Draw a simple welding workshop layout.
Day 2: Arrange tools and materials in assigned areas.
Day 3: Prepare an electrode and disc record sheet.
Day 4: Sort metal pieces and offcuts.
Day 5: Conduct a workshop organisation review.

Character
Order saves time, prevents accidents and protects workshop resources.

Week 23. Welding Business Ethics and Customer Trust

Teaching focus
Honest measurement, material quality, fair pricing, strong welds, delivery promises, customer care and reputation.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:1 “A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold.”

Practice
Day 1: Discuss dishonest practices in welding business.
Day 2: Prepare a customer trust checklist.
Day 3: Role-play handling a customer complaint.
Day 4: Discuss the danger of weak welds and fake materials.
Day 5: Write a welding business ethics pledge.

Character
A good name is more valuable than quick profit. Dishonest welding can destroy lives and reputation.

Week 24. Welding and Fabrication Enterprise Opportunities

Teaching focus
Small welding services, gates, windows, repairs, metal furniture, agricultural tools, workshop support and cooperative enterprise.

Scripture
Deuteronomy 8:18 “But thou shalt remember the LORD thy God: for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth.”

Practice
Day 1: List enterprise opportunities in welding and fabrication.
Day 2: Identify customers for one welding service.
Day 3: Prepare a simple service description.
Day 4: Prepare a small-start budget.
Day 5: Write a welding and fabrication enterprise idea note.

Character
The power to create wealth comes from God. Welding enterprise must be built on safety, honesty, skill and service.

modules.title: Advanced Practice, Departmental Project and Attachment Preparation
modules.content:
Module 7 of 7. Advanced Practice, Departmental Project and Attachment Preparation

Read each section in order. Mark the module complete, then pass the checkpoint with at least 70 percent. The next module stays locked until you do.

Week 25. Departmental Mini-Project Planning

Teaching focus
Planning a safe welding or fabrication mini-project, team roles, materials, tools, safety controls, costing and expected outcome.

Scripture
Nehemiah 2:18 “Then I told them of the hand of my God which was good upon me; as also the king’s words that he had spoken unto me. And they said, Let us rise up and build.”

Practice
Day 1: Choose a safe departmental mini-project.
Day 2: Prepare a project sketch and material list.
Day 3: Prepare tools, safety equipment and cost estimate.
Day 4: Assign team roles and safety officers.
Day 5: Submit project plan for trainer approval.

Character
Vision must become organised action. Trainees must rise and build responsibly.

Week 26. Departmental Mini-Project Implementation

Teaching focus
Carrying out a supervised welding or fabrication project with safety, teamwork, records and quality checks.

Scripture
Nehemiah 4:6 “So built we the wall; and all the wall was joined together unto the half thereof: for the people had a mind to work.”

Practice
Day 1: Prepare the workshop area, tools and materials.
Day 2: Measure, mark and cut materials under supervision.
Day 3: Clamp, tack and weld under supervision where safe.
Day 4: Grind, clean and inspect work under supervision.
Day 5: Clean the area and review project progress.

Character
Progress comes when people have a mind to work and cooperate with discipline.

Week 27. Final Practical Demonstration and Portfolio

Teaching focus
Demonstrating tool use, measurement, marking, safety checks, basic welding awareness, records and portfolio evidence.

Scripture
2 Timothy 2:15 “Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed.”

Practice
Day 1: Demonstrate tool identification and safe handling.
Day 2: Demonstrate measurement and marking.
Day 3: Demonstrate clamping and joint preparation.
Day 4: Organise welding and fabrication portfolio.
Day 5: Present practical evidence to the trainer.

Character
A trained worker should not be ashamed. Diligence, skill and discipline prepare trainees for approval.

Week 28. Industrial Attachment Preparation

Teaching focus
Preparing for welding workshop placement, supervisor conduct, workshop safety, daily logs, customer care and final readiness.

Scripture
Proverbs 22:29 “Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.”

Practice
Day 1: Identify possible welding and fabrication attachment placements.
Day 2: Prepare personal attachment learning goals.
Day 3: Practise writing daily welding attachment logs.
Day 4: Review workshop safety and workplace behaviour.
Day 5: Complete final departmental readiness assessment.

Character
Diligence opens doors. A faithful trainee can be trusted with greater responsibility.
